mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Lebanon and the Syrian Arab Republic, 3–7 December 2025
mission_country_or_region: Lebanon and the Syrian Arab Republic

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Political Engagement and Mandate Assessment Mission
main_risks: Continued Israeli violations of sovereignty, air strikes, and illegal territorial occupation in both Syria and Lebanon.
Security fragility, terrorism threats (Da'esh, Ansar al-Sunnah), and high concentration of explosive remnants of war in Syria.
Severe funding shortfalls for humanitarian aid and recovery, compounded by the chilling operational effects of sanctions in Syria.
Risk of renewed conflict between Hizbullah and Israel, non-State weapons retention, and operational vacuum during UNIFIL's drawdown in southern Lebanon.
main_commitments: Syrian Government commitment to transitional justice, missing persons institutions, 1974 Disengagement Agreement, and non-export of crises.
Lebanese Government commitment to the National Shield Plan, State monopoly over weapons, expanding LAF deployment south of the Litani, and implementing Security Council Resolution 1701 (2006).
United Nations commitment to assist Syria's transition from relief to recovery and explore options for post-UNIFIL implementation of Resolution 1701 (2006) in Lebanon.
main_policy_signals: Unanimous Security Council support for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of both Syria and Lebanon.
Call for comprehensive sanctions relief for Syria to enable economic recovery and sustainable peace.
Demand for full compliance with Security Council Resolution 1701 (2006), Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese positions/buffer zones, and ceasefire commitments.
Strong support for State monopoly over weapons in Lebanon and intensified international support to strengthen the Lebanese Armed Forces.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Syria and Lebanon provided first-hand assessment of complex post-conflict transition and volatile security dynamics. In Syria, interlocutors emphasized political transition, transitional justice, sovereignty challenges from Israeli air strikes/incursions, and the dire economic impact of sanctions and humanitarian cuts. In Lebanon, discussions focused on the National Shield Plan to establish State monopoly over arms, expanding LAF deployment south of the Litani River, Israeli violations along the Blue Line, and planning for successor arrangements to UNIFIL following its mandated drawdown.

activities.activity_description: Briefing on Syrian political and security situations by Deputy Special Envoy Najat Rochdi and UNDSS.
Drive through destroyed suburb of Jawbar and visit to the Old City of Damascus, Bayt al-Wali, and Umayyad Mosque.
Meeting with President of Syria Ahmed al-Sharaa and Cabinet Ministers.
Briefing by UN Country Team in Syria, OSE-Syria, UNDSS, UNDOF, and UNTSO.
Meeting with representatives of Syrian civil society.
Meeting with communities affected by events in the coastal region and Suwayda'.
Working lunch with Syrian religious notables.
Meeting with heads of Syrian national commissions (Transitional Justice, Fact-Finding) and Governors of Tartus, Ladhiqiyah, Suwayda', and Dar'a.
Press stakeout by mission co-leads at the conclusion of the Syria visit.
Viewing the city of Damascus from Mount Qasiyun.
Briefing on Lebanese political and security situations by UN Deputy Special Coordinator Imran Riza and UNDSS.
Meeting with President of Lebanon Joseph Aoun.
Meeting with Speaker of Parliament of Lebanon Nabih Berri.
Meeting with Prime Minister of Lebanon Nawaf Salam.
Meeting with Minister for Foreign Affairs and Emigrants of Lebanon Youssef Raggi.
Meeting with Commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces General Rodolphe Haykal and operational briefing by LAF Director of Operations.
Meeting with Chair of the Cessation of Hostilities Implementation Mechanism Lt. Gen. Joseph Clearfield.
Briefing by acting Executive Secretary of ESCWA Mourad Wahba.
Briefing by UNIFIL Head of Mission and Force Commander Maj. Gen. Diodato Abagnara.
Visit to and operational briefing at United Nations Position 1-31 in Sector West, southern Lebanon.
Press stakeout by mission co-leads at the conclusion of the Lebanon visit.

records.record_text: The Deputy Special Envoy noted that 14 years of conflict had left deep institutional scars, widespread destruction of infrastructure and unresolved housing and property issues, while the humanitarian situation remained dire with diminishing funding for essential programmes.
records.actor_source: Deputy Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for Syria
records.political_signal: Highlights urgent national needs and fragile recovery state in Syria.
records.policy_implication: Requires sustained humanitarian assistance and funding shift toward early recovery.

records.record_text: The Deputy Special Envoy appealed for comprehensive sanctions relief, sustained funding and political space, especially for civil society, so that the Syrian Arab Republic could transition to sustainable peace.
records.actor_source: Deputy Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for Syria
records.political_signal: Advocates for sanctions removal to unlock economic transition and recovery.
records.policy_implication: Security Council and UN Member States urged to review unilateral sanctions mechanisms.

records.record_text: UNDSS highlighted the overall fragility of conditions and identified hotspots including Aleppo, coastal region, Homs, Dayr al-Zawr, Rif Dimashq and the south, where activities of Ansar al-Sunnah, Da'esh and other terrorist groups remained of concern.
records.political_signal: Underscores persistent multi-front terrorist and security risks in Syria.
records.policy_implication: Requires security coordination and targeted counter-terrorism focus.

records.record_text: President Ahmed al-Sharaa declared that with liberation of Syria from the former regime, the region and world had become safer, and that conduct of late 2024 hostilities and peaceful power handover had been in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
records.actor_source: President of the Syrian Arab Republic
records.political_signal: Frames new Syrian government legitimacy around resolution 2254 compliance.
records.policy_implication: Positions government as legitimate transition partner for international engagement.

records.record_text: President al-Sharaa sought support of the Security Council in maintaining Syria's territorial integrity in the face of Israeli violations, citing 1,000 air strikes and 400 incursions in 2025, and requested compelling Israel to comply with the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.
records.actor_source: President of the Syrian Arab Republic
records.political_signal: Demands UN action to halt Israeli military actions on Syrian territory.
records.policy_implication: Pressures Security Council to enforce 1974 Disengagement Agreement and UNDOF mandate.

records.record_text: Security Council members reiterated solidarity with the Syrian Arab Republic and strong support for its sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, with several expressing grave concern at Israeli violations.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms UNSC consensus on Syrian state sovereignty and territorial integrity.
records.policy_implication: Provides political framework for Council oversight on regional military activity in Syria.

records.record_text: The UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator a.i. warned that predictable funding for Syria is rapidly diminishing, forcing cuts to food, health, protection, education and gender-based violence services, while sanctions chill procurement and banking.
records.actor_source: UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator a.i.
records.political_signal: Highlights impending humanitarian failure due to donor fatigue and financial sanctions.
records.policy_implication: Urgent appeal to international donors and sanctioning bodies to adjust operational terms.

records.record_text: An UNDOF official reported that unauthorized presence of the Israel Defense Forces and roadblocks in the area of separation constrained mission implementation, requesting Council support for respect of the 1974 Agreement.
records.political_signal: Highlights operational obstruction of UNDOF by Israeli military presence.
records.policy_implication: Calls for diplomatic pressure on Israel to clear the area of separation.

records.record_text: Syrian civil society representatives called for an inclusive transitional process without quota-based approaches, independent funding for truth-seeking and accountability mechanisms, decentralization, implementation of resolution 1325 (2000), and state monopoly over weapons.
records.political_signal: Demands genuine civil participation, rights protections, and non-sectarian security structures.
records.policy_implication: UN programs must directly support civil society inclusion and independent transitional justice.

records.record_text: Representatives of national commissions briefed the Council on draft transitional justice legislation aligned with international standards and investigations into coastal region and Suwayda' violence that led to suspect lists transmitted to the Public Prosecutor.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates institutional steps toward legal accountability and judicial reform.
records.policy_implication: Requires technical and financial assistance from UN body to sustain transparent trials.

records.record_text: UN Deputy Special Coordinator Imran Riza informed members that preparations were under way for resolution 1701 (2006) implementation post-UNIFIL withdrawal, emphasizing the need to prevent a security vacuum that could be filled by actors outside State authority.
records.actor_source: UN Deputy Special Coordinator for Lebanon
records.political_signal: Warns of critical security risks during UNIFIL transition.
records.policy_implication: UNSC must define clear successor mechanisms for monitoring, reporting, and LAF support prior to UNIFIL exit.

records.record_text: A Department of Safety and Security official outlined four future scenarios for Lebanon: conflict renewal between Hizbullah and Israel (assessed as likely), renewed terrorist attacks (moderately likely), violent internal instability (moderately likely), and regional war (unlikely).
records.political_signal: Identifies elevated probability of resumed Hizbullah-Israel conflict.
records.policy_implication: Underscores need for active diplomatic de-escalation via the Cessation Mechanism.

records.record_text: President Joseph Aoun emphasized ongoing state efforts to establish a monopoly over weapons, increased LAF deployment south of the Litani River, and requested international donor support to rebuild the south while condemning continued Israeli violations.
records.political_signal: Signals Lebanese executive commitment to state arms control and LAF expansion.
records.policy_implication: Requires international commitments for LAF funding and reconstruction assistance.

records.record_text: Speaker Nabih Berri stated that Lebanon's stability rests on resolution 1701 (2006) and 2790 (2025), noting LAF presence in the south had increased to 9,300 soldiers, and warned Lebanon cannot bear UNIFIL's withdrawal without a credible alternative.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms Lebanese parliamentary adherence to UN resolutions while demanding peacekeeping continuity.
records.policy_implication: UNSC must ensure successor oversight mechanisms to preserve Blue Line stability.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Nawaf Salam highlighted the historic August 2025 decision to establish state monopoly over weapons and emphasized that post-UNIFIL monitoring, verification and liaison responsibilities must be assigned to an entity like UNTSO or UNDOF due to lack of trust between parties.
records.political_signal: Proposes leveraging existing UN footprints (UNTSO/UNDOF) to fulfill post-UNIFIL roles.
records.policy_implication: Feeds into UN Secretary-General's June 2026 report on options for resolution 1701 implementation.

records.record_text: Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi called for immediate, unconditional Israeli withdrawal from five occupied points and two buffer zones, noting retention of non-state weapons is a domestic issue being addressed via state policy.
records.actor_source: Minister for Foreign Affairs and Emigrants of Lebanon
records.political_signal: Demands cessation of Israeli military occupation points to break the cycle of mistrust.
records.policy_implication: Focuses international diplomatic leverage on Israeli operational compliance.

records.record_text: LAF Commander General Rodolphe Haykal reported that the LAF cleared 88 per cent of phase one areas under the National Shield Plan, but stressed that LAF cannot undertake UNIFIL's core tasks of monitoring, reporting, and liaising with Israel.
records.actor_source: Commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces
records.political_signal: Clarifies strict operational boundaries between sovereign military role and third-party UN monitoring.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces requirement for impartial international liaison and verification entity post-UNIFIL.

records.record_text: UNIFIL Force Commander Maj. Gen. Abagnara reported that since November 2024, UNIFIL recorded over 8,000 air violations, direct fire attacks on peacekeepers, and illegal occupation of five positions and two buffer zones by the IDF in contravention of resolution 1701 (2006).
records.actor_source: UNIFIL Head of Mission and Force Commander
records.political_signal: Documents severe structural violations of resolution 1701 and physical risks to peacekeepers.
records.policy_implication: Demands Security Council action to enforce safety of UN personnel and respect for Blue Line.

records.record_text: UNIFIL Force Commander noted that UNIFIL observed no evidence of attempts by Hizbullah to re-establish an organized military presence south of the Litani River, while LAF deployed nearly 9,000 troops supported by CUWA operations.
records.actor_source: UNIFIL Head of Mission and Force Commander
records.political_signal: Verifies progress in non-state disarmament compliance south of the Litani River.
records.policy_implication: Provides objective baseline data countering claims of non-state re-armament in UNIFIL area.

records.record_text: During field inspection at Position 1-31, Council members observed an illegal forward operating base constructed by the IDF inside Lebanese territory and noted extensive destruction of adjacent civilian villages.
records.political_signal: Direct Council verification of foreign military breach of Lebanese sovereignty.
records.policy_implication: Strengthens factual evidence base for Council deliberations on resolution 1701 implementation.

records.record_text: In press stakeouts, mission co-leads expressed support for the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Lebanon and Syria, called for international support for the LAF, supported state monopoly over arms, and demanded guarantees for peacekeeper safety.
records.political_signal: Unifies Council stance on sovereignty, state arms control, and international support to host forces.
records.policy_implication: Sets broad political parameters for future UNSC resolution drafting on Lebanon and Syria.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Ethiopia, 16 and 17 October 2025

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Annual Joint Consultative Meeting with the AU Peace and Security Council
main_risks: Precarious financial situation of AUSSOM and insufficient pledge levels for effective operations
Lack of unity among domestic stakeholders and neighbouring States in Sudan
Multiple uncoordinated mediation initiatives hindering peace in Sudan
Socioeconomic drivers (poverty, unemployment, weak State institutions, social media dynamics) fueling youth discontent and unconstitutional changes of government
Ongoing instability across the Horn of Africa, Sahel, Lake Chad basin, and Great Lakes region
main_commitments: Agreement to convene the eleventh informal joint seminar and twentieth annual joint consultative meeting in New York on dates to be jointly agreed
main_policy_signals: Imperative of enhanced UN-AU partnership, coordination, and harmonization in addressing complex African conflicts
Need for international support and sustainable financing for AU-led peace support operations under resolution 2719 (2023)
Urgency of restarting an inclusive political process in Sudan and maintaining regional stability in the Horn of Africa
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The UN Security Council mission to Addis Ababa on 16–17 October 2025 fulfilled the annual institutional engagement with the African Union Peace and Security Council (10th informal joint seminar and 19th annual joint consultative meeting). Complementary bilateral meetings were conducted with AU Commission leadership, UN senior envoys, and the Foreign Minister of Ethiopia. Discussions centered on operationalizing resolution 2719 (2023) for AU peace support operations, financial sustainability for AUSSOM, addressing armed conflicts in Sudan, South Sudan, eastern DRC, and the Sahel, preventing unconstitutional changes of government, and strengthening UN-AU strategic partnership.

activities.activity_description: Tenth informal joint seminar between the members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council of the African Union on WPS, terrorism, and resolution 2719 (2023)
Nineteenth annual joint consultative meeting between the members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council of the African Union
Meeting with United Nations officials (SRSG to the AU Parfait Onanga-Anyanga and Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa Guang Cong)
Meeting with the Chairperson of the African Union Commission (Mahmoud Ali Youssouf), Deputy Chairperson, and AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security
Meeting with the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia (Gedion Timethewos Hessebon)

actors_met.actor_name: Peace and Security Council of the African Union (AU PSC)
Bankole Adeoye (African Union Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security)
Mahmoud Ali Youssouf (Chairperson of the African Union Commission)
Selma Malika Haddadi (Deputy Chairperson of the African Union Commission)
Parfait Onanga-Anyanga (Special Representative of the Secretary-General to the African Union and Head of UNOAU)
Guang Cong (Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for the Horn of Africa)
Gedion Timethewos Hessebon (Minister for Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia)

records.record_text: The general objective of the annual joint consultative meeting between the members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council of the African Union is to strengthen partnership and enhance cooperation between the two Councils through the exchange of views on matters of mutual concern in the maintenance of international peace and security, with a particular focus on Africa.
records.actor_target: Peace and Security Council of the African Union
records.political_signal: Institutional reaffirmation of strategic partnership between the UN Security Council and the AU Peace and Security Council.
records.policy_implication: Continued institutionalization of joint UN-AU consultative mechanisms.

records.record_text: Council members expressed appreciation for the briefings and expressed support for a strong partnership with the African Union to address the complex and multidimensional conflicts in the Sudan, South Sudan and the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: Security Council consensus on partnering with the AU to address key African conflicts.
records.policy_implication: Support for joint UN-AU initiatives in Sudan, South Sudan, and eastern DRC.

records.record_text: There was also discussion about the situation in Madagascar and tensions between Eritrea and Ethiopia.
records.political_signal: Monitoring regional friction points in the Horn of Africa and the Indian Ocean region.
records.policy_implication: Need for diplomatic vigilance regarding bilateral tensions between Eritrea and Ethiopia.

records.record_text: Council members commended the role of the three African members of the Security Council in strengthening coordination with the Peace and Security Council of the African Union.
records.actor_target: A3 (African members of the Security Council)
records.political_signal: Recognition of the pivotal bridging role played by the A3 in UN-AU relations.
records.policy_implication: Encouragement of continued coordination led by A3 members.

records.record_text: The Chairperson welcomed the continued cooperation between the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council of the African Union, noting that continent-wide challenges required enhanced coordination, mutual understanding and sustained engagement.
records.actor_source: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: AU leadership advocacy for deepened joint coordination in addressing continental threats.
records.policy_implication: Requirement for sustained diplomatic and operational alignment between UN and AU.

records.record_text: He highlighted the precarious financial situation of AUSSOM and, while welcoming the recent pledges announced in New York, noted that this level of support would not be sufficient for its effective operation.
records.actor_source: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: Direct signal that funding pledges for AUSSOM remain inadequate for operational effectiveness.
records.policy_implication: Urgent need for sustainable and predictable financing mechanisms for AUSSOM.

records.record_text: The Chairperson also underscored the urgency of restarting a political process in the Sudan amid a lack of unity among domestic stakeholders and neighbouring States, and the importance of avoiding further instability in East Africa.
records.actor_source: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: Call for unified international action to restart Sudan's political process and prevent regional spillover.
records.policy_implication: Harmonization of competing mediation efforts in Sudan.

records.record_text: More broadly, the Chairperson also outlined how poverty, unemployment, weak State institutions and social media dynamics fueled societal discontent, in particular among youth, creating the conditions for unconstitutional changes of government.
records.actor_source: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: Identification of structural socioeconomic and digital drivers behind unconstitutional changes of government.
records.policy_implication: Need for governance, youth engagement, and socio-economic developmental strategies in conflict prevention.

records.record_text: He took note of the ongoing African Union reviews of the African Peace and Security Architecture and the African Governance Architecture aimed at prioritizing the prevention of conflict.
records.actor_source: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: AU internal reform process prioritizing conflict prevention institutional mechanisms.
records.policy_implication: Potential realignments in APSA and AGA institutional framework.

records.record_text: Finally, he expressed his appreciation for all diplomatic and good offices initiatives of the United Nations and the Security Council in support of peace and security in Africa and underscored the importance of the coordination and harmonization of those efforts with the African Union.
records.actor_source: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: Requirement that UN good offices and mediation align closely with AU leadership.
records.policy_implication: Mandate alignment and joint diplomatic efforts.

records.record_text: During the discussion, they expressed concern over the situation in several countries neighbouring Ethiopia.
records.political_signal: Shared concern over widespread instability surrounding Ethiopia's immediate borders.
records.policy_implication: Focus on regional contagion risks in the Horn of Africa.

records.record_text: Regarding the Sudan, they emphasized the need to address the precarious situation on the ground and noted the challenges posed by multiple mediation initiatives.
records.political_signal: Critated fragmentation of mediation frameworks for Sudan.
records.policy_implication: Push for streamling mediation tracks into a single unified process.

records.record_text: On Somalia, Security Council members acknowledged the significant progress achieved on the political and security fronts, as well as the remaining substantial challenges, including with regard to adequate funding support to AUSSOM and the responsibilities of the international community in that regard.
records.political_signal: Recognition of Somali progress coupled with explicit burden-sharing responsibility on international donors.
records.policy_implication: Resource mobilization calls for AUSSOM transition.

records.record_text: Participants at the meeting further discussed the impact of the crisis in the Sahel on other regions and the importance of close cooperation of the two Councils to address the manifold challenges facing the region.
records.actor_target: Peace and Security Council of the African Union
records.political_signal: Recognition of inter-regional security spillover originating from the Sahel crisis.
records.policy_implication: Joint UNSC-AUPSC strategy for cross-regional threat mitigation (e.g., Gulf of Guinea).

records.record_text: On 30 October, following the nineteenth annual joint consultative meeting, the members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council of the African Union issued a joint press statement (SC/16205) in which they agreed to convene their eleventh informal joint seminar and the twentieth annual joint consultative meeting in New York on dates to be jointly agreed by the two sides in due course.
records.actor_target: Peace and Security Council of the African Union
records.political_signal: Formal commitment to maintain annual joint consultations in New York in 2026.
records.policy_implication: Planning for 11th joint seminar and 20th joint consultative meeting in New York.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Ethiopia, 5 and 6 October 2023

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Joint Consultative Meeting and Seminar with the African Union Peace and Security Council
main_risks: Escalation of conflict and severe humanitarian deterioration in the Sudan, Sahel region, Somalia, and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Fragmentation among Sudanese civilian stakeholders hindering joint AU-IGAD mediation efforts
Rise of terrorism and unconstitutional changes of government spreading across the Sahel and West African coastal States
Security vacuums arising from the withdrawal or liquidation of UN peacekeeping operations (MINUSMA, MONUSCO) and ATMIS drawdown
Unpredictable and unsustainable financing for African Union-led peace support operations
main_commitments: Issuance of a joint communiqué (S/2023/749) following the seventeenth annual joint consultative meeting
Conducting joint UNSC-AU PSC field and assessment missions on a case-by-case basis
Structuring monthly informal coordination meetings between the incoming Chair of the AU PSC and the President of the Security Council
Constructive engagement by Security Council members with African members on a draft framework resolution on AU PSO financing
Recognition of November as Africa Youth Month by the AU PSC and prospects for a joint UNSC-AU PSC session on youth, peace and security
main_policy_signals: Primacy of political solutions, national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and non-interference in regional conflict resolution
Urgent requirement for flexible, predictable, and sustainable financing for Security Council-authorized AU-led peace support operations
Emphasis on host State primary responsibility during UN mission drawdowns and transitions to avoid security vacuums
Call for enhanced representation and participation of youth in decision-making, preventive diplomacy, and peace processes
Call for Security Council working methods reform to ensure full participation of countries on the agenda and equitable representation for Africa
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Ethiopia on 5–6 October 2023 conducted the 8th informal joint seminar and 17th annual joint consultative meeting with the African Union Peace and Security Council (AU PSC) in Addis Ababa. The joint consultations addressed pressing security and political crises in the Sudan, Sahel region, Somalia, and eastern DRC, while also focusing on structural institutional issues including the financing of AU-led peace support operations, implementation of the Youth, Peace and Security agenda, and enhancing UNSC-AU PSC cooperation and working methods. The mission highlighted growing institutional alignment alongside distinct perspectives regarding financing mechanisms, mission drawdowns, and regional peace enforcement capabilities.

activities.activity_description: Eighth informal joint seminar between the members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council of the African Union on financing AU-led peace support operations, youth, peace and security, and working methods.

Seventeenth annual joint consultative meeting between the members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council of the African Union addressing situations in the Sudan, Sahel, Somalia/ATMIS, and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Meeting between Security Council members and SRSG Parfait Onanga-Anyanga and Special Envoy Hanna Tetteh on UN-AU partnership, PSO financing, and Horn of Africa issues.
Working lunch hosted by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia, Demeke Mekonnen Hassen, with Security Council members.

actors_met.actor_name: Peace and Security Council of the African Union
Bankole Adeoye, African Union Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security
Parfait Onanga-Anyanga, Special Representative of the Secretary-General to the African Union and Head of UNOAU
Hanna Tetteh, Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for the Horn of Africa
Demeke Mekonnen Hassen, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia

records.record_text: The Co-Chairs of the meeting highlighted the progress achieved over the past few years in strengthening the strategic partnership between the two organizations. Both made calls for closer coordination between the two Councils, including joint field missions, expressing hope that the consultations would add more value to their work.
records.actor_source: Co-Chairs of the XVII Joint Consultative Meeting (UNSC President / AU PSC Chair)
records.actor_target: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Strong institutional backing for joint UN-AU operational activities, including joint field missions.
records.policy_implication: May lead to increased frequency of joint UNSC-AU PSC field visits to regional conflict zones.

records.record_text: The Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security of the African Union and the Special Representative of the Secretary-General to the African Union noted the emergence of new threats, which demanded greater cooperation between the two Councils, such as the rise in terrorist attacks, adverse effects of climate change and resurgence of unconstitutional changes of government. Messrs. Adeoye and Onanga-Anyanga stressed the need for flexible, predictable and sustainable financing to the African Union peace support operations.
records.actor_source: Bankole Adeoye (AU Commissioner) and Parfait Onanga-Anyanga (SRSG)
records.actor_target: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Persistent high-level push from UN and AU leadership to secure UN assessed contributions for AU-led PSOs.
records.policy_implication: Strengthens momentum for Security Council action on sustainable financing frameworks for African peace support missions.

records.record_text: Members of both Councils noted that the scale of the crisis in the Sudan and its impact on the civilian population required impetus for urgent action towards a political solution to secure a durable ceasefire and better humanitarian access.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: Parties to the conflict in Sudan
records.political_signal: Unified UN-AU demand for an immediate ceasefire and political resolution in Sudan.
records.policy_implication: Directs diplomatic pressure toward coordinated regional and global mediation channels.

records.record_text: Regarding the African Union-IGAD joint working group, which was established to identify Sudanese stakeholders for the initiation of a mediation process, it was noted that the major obstacle that the initiative faced was fragmentation among the Sudanese civilian stakeholders.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Civilian political fragmentation is directly impeding effective joint AU-IGAD mediation.
records.policy_implication: Mediation support must prioritize unifying and organizing Sudanese civilian platforms.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council expressed deep concern over the continuing fragility of the security situation in the Sahel region, which was characterized by the continuation of terrorist attacks in the region. They also expressed concern over the resurgence of unconstitutional changes of government in the region.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Joint rejection of unconstitutional governance changes and grave concern over expanding violent extremism in the Sahel.
records.policy_implication: Calls for holistic governance and security interventions across the subregion.

records.record_text: Members of both Councils underscored the need for the two Councils to approach the withdrawal and ongoing liquidation of the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali collaboratively, emphasizing the need for joint approaches towards the stabilization in the country, while underscoring the primary responsibility of the transition Government in that regard.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Reaffirmation that host governments hold ultimate responsibility for security during UN mission drawdowns.
records.policy_implication: Requires close UN-AU alignment to mitigate security and humanitarian risks post-MINUSMA withdrawal.

records.record_text: The two Councils agreed that there were no military solutions to the security crisis in the Sahel and underscored the need to enhance national and regional resilience through early warning and response mechanisms.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Explicit consensus that purely kinetic responses are insufficient to resolve the Sahel security crisis.
records.policy_implication: Prioritizes early warning mechanisms, governance reforms, and root-cause interventions over military-only solutions.

records.record_text: Members of the two Councils also referred to the emerging geopolitical dynamics and external influence as among the factors driving instability in the Sahel. In that regard, they called for the principles of national sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference in internal affairs to be upheld.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Warning against geopolitical power competition and foreign interference destabilizing the Sahel.
records.policy_implication: Emphasizes adherence to foundational UN Charter principles in multilateral engagement in the Sahel.

records.record_text: Regarding the security transition, a member of the Peace and Security Council noted that the ATMIS drawdown was being driven by unpredictable financing and not the security situation in Somalia, given that Al-Shabaab still posed a potent threat.
records.actor_source: Member of the African Union Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: International donors and United Nations Security Council
records.political_signal: Critique that premature mission drawdown driven by funding shortfalls risks severe security reversals in Somalia.
records.policy_implication: Urges international partners to align ATMIS withdrawal timelines with real ground security assessments rather than budget constraints.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council expressed deep concern about the intensifying violence and attacks against civilians perpetrated by the armed groups, as well as the spread of hate speech, and deplored the worsening humanitarian situation. Some members also strongly condemned the alarming increase in sexual violence against women and girls.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Strong condemnation of atrocities against civilians and sexual violence in eastern DRC.
records.policy_implication: Demands immediate cessation of hostilities and criminal accountability for human rights abuses.

records.record_text: They further noted that the call of the Democratic Republic of the Congo for an expedited drawdown of the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) needed to be considered within the holistic context of the political and security developments in the country and implications for the region.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and UNSC
records.political_signal: Caution that MONUSCO's expedited departure must not create security vacuums or regional instability.
records.policy_implication: Requires structured transition benchmarks co-managed with DRC authorities and TPCs/PCCs.

records.record_text: Members of the two Councils welcomed the African Union contribution of $2 million to the East African Community Regional Force from the Peace Fund of the African Union and commended the good offices missions on behalf of the Secretary-General and sustained engagements of the Heads of the United Nations Office to the African Union and MONUSCO and the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for the Great Lakes Region.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: East African Community Regional Force / UN Envoys
records.political_signal: Concrete endorsement of utilizing the AU Peace Fund to support subregional peace operations.
records.policy_implication: Sets a precedent for AU Peace Fund disbursements to subregional regional force initiatives.

records.record_text: They stressed that African Union-led peace support operations had a complementary role in the maintenance of peace and security in Africa, particularly in contexts where kinetic action was required. They agreed on the need to address the issue of flexible, sustainable and predictable financing for African Union-led peace support operations mandated by the Security Council.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: United Nations Security Council and General Assembly
records.political_signal: Recognition that AU forces possess specialized military mandates for enforcement tasks where UN peacekeeping is structurally unsuited.
records.policy_implication: Provides conceptual basis for UN-assessed contribution financing for AU enforcement operations.

records.record_text: Members of the Peace and Security Council and the African members of the Security Council relayed the progress that the African Union had made in revitalizing the Peace Fund of the African Union and setting up the African Union Human Rights Compliance Framework. They strongly stressed the need for the Security Council to urgently take 'concrete action' on access to assessed contributions for African Union-led peace support operations authorized by the Security Council.
records.actor_source: AU PSC members and A3 (African members of the UNSC)
records.political_signal: Direct demand from African States for immediate UNSC resolution adoption enabling UN assessed funding.
records.policy_implication: Puts direct pressure on UNSC permanent members to resolve outstanding framework resolution negotiations.

records.record_text: Some members of the Security Council expressed their expectation that financing of African Union peace support operations should include some degree of burden-sharing with the African Union. These members also stressed that any future resolutions needed to specify the primary role of the Security Council in the authorization and oversight of African Union-led peace support operations as well as the General Assembly's mandate for budgetary approval and oversight.
records.actor_source: Some members of the United Nations Security Council
records.political_signal: Red lines set by key donors/P3 regarding financial burden-sharing and UNSC/GA mandate oversight authority over AU missions.
records.policy_implication: Drafting of resolution frameworks must incorporate statutory percentage limits and explicit UN oversight controls.

records.record_text: The two Councils further welcomed the progress made by the African Union in adopting the Continental Framework for Youth, Peace, and Security, the appointment of the African Union Youth Envoy and Youth Ambassadors for Peace, and the roll-out of the Youth for Peace programme. They also commended the operationalization of the Wise Youth initiative as a subsidiary programme of the African Union's Panel of the Wise and underscored the need to enhance the participation of youth in preventive diplomacy, dialogue, and mediation in Africa.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: African Union Commission and UN Secretariat
records.political_signal: Strong institutional support for institutionalizing youth leadership structures in peace processes across Africa.
records.policy_implication: Scales up institutional inclusion of young mediators and youth envoys in AU-UN preventive diplomacy.

records.record_text: Participants from both Councils called for more African Union officials to provide briefings at meetings of the Security Council, particularly when mandate renewals were under consideration. Participants also called for a stronger role of the African members of the Security Council, to serve as a bridge with the African Union. In that regard, some participants expressed support for granting the African members of the Security Council more opportunities as co-penholders on African issues.
records.actor_source: Participants from UNSC and AU PSC
records.political_signal: Push for structural reform of penholding practices in the Security Council to empower African elected members.
records.policy_implication: May lead to increased co-penholding assignments for A3 members on African peacekeeping and sanctions mandates.

records.record_text: Some participants also stressed the need to review, adjust and terminate the Security Council sanctions regimes, taking into account the evolution of the situation on the ground.
records.actor_source: Some participants from UNSC and AU PSC
records.political_signal: Call for easing or sunsetting UN sanctions on African States to align with evolving political developments.
records.policy_implication: Heightens political pressure during annual UNSC sanctions regime reviews and renewal discussions.

records.record_text: Members of the two Councils agreed to conduct joint field and assessment missions, with modalities of such trips being determined on a case-by-case basis.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Formal agreement to resume joint UNSC-AU PSC field visits.
records.policy_implication: Establishes a practical pathway for designing joint assessment missions to shared crisis regions.

records.record_text: On the working methods of the Security Council, the Deputy Prime Minister called for improvements to ensure that countries on the agenda of the Council can fully participate in discussions concerning them. He also expressed support for reforms of the Security Council, including the full and equitable representation of Africa.
records.actor_source: Demeke Mekonnen Hassen, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia
records.political_signal: Host nation critique of Security Council exclusivity and advocacy for Ezulwini Consensus representation.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces African Union diplomatic consensus demanding permanent and expanded seats on the Security Council.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 9–12 March 2023

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Security assessment, political engagement, and electoral review mission
main_risks: Continued deterioration of the security situation in eastern provinces due to M23 expansion and attacks by ADF, CODECO, and Mai-Mai
Hostile operating environment, disinformation, and movement restrictions facing MONUSCO personnel and humanitarian actors
Risk of electoral instability or non-inclusive elections due to persistent insecurity in the east and political tensions over electoral institutions
Escalation of humanitarian displacement and severe economic impact caused by armed group control over key supply routes
main_commitments: The Council delegation pledged to work towards an urgent response to provide humanitarian assistance to the population in need
The delegation committed itself to continuing to work towards the restoration of peace and stability in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and reiterated support for women leaders
The Council delegation expressed solidarity with the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the context of the deteriorating security situation in the east
main_policy_signals: The Security Council emphasized that the solution to the eastern DRC crisis must be political, urging full support for the complementary Nairobi and Luanda regional processes

The Security Council encouraged Congolese authorities to ensure peaceful, transparent, inclusive, and credible presidential and legislative elections within constitutional deadlines, while avoiding incitement to violence and widening democratic space
The Security Council stressed host state responsibility for protecting UN personnel and acknowledged the need to evaluate options for MONUSCO's reconfiguration
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo evaluated the worsening security crisis in the eastern provinces, preparations for the 2023 general elections, the mandate and transition of MONUSCO, and regional diplomatic efforts (Nairobi and Luanda processes). Congolese interlocutors across government, parliament, opposition, and civil society strongly called for sanctions against Rwanda for supporting M23, an upgrade of MONUSCO's mandate to peace enforcement, and support for DDR and security sector reform. The Council reiterated that the crisis requires a political solution, stressed the importance of respecting constitutional deadlines for elections, pledged support for humanitarian needs, and emphasized host state protection for UN personnel.

activities.activity_description: Briefing by the senior leadership of MONUSCO, the United Nations country team, and the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for the Great Lakes Region in Kinshasa.
Meeting with Prime Minister Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde Kyenge, Vice-Prime Ministers, Ministers, and senior military/police leadership in Kinshasa.
Meeting with the President of the National Assembly and the First Vice-President of the Senate and bureau members in Kinshasa.
Meeting with representatives of civil society organizations in Kinshasa.
Meeting with members of the political opposition in Kinshasa.
Meeting with President of the Republic Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo in Kinshasa.
Meeting with the Governor of North Kivu, Minister of National Defence and Former Combatants, and Minister of Social Affairs, Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity in Goma.
Wreath-laying ceremony to pay tribute to fallen peacekeepers in Goma.
Meeting with key actors of the Nairobi and Luanda processes, including the High Representative of the DRC President, Commander of EACRF, and Head of the Ad Hoc Verification Mechanism in Goma.
Meeting with the MONUSCO Mission force in Goma.
Meeting with natural resources experts in Goma.
Meeting with women leaders of civil society organizations in Goma.
Visit to the Bushagara internally displaced persons site outside Goma.
Concluding press conference led by mission co-leads in Goma.

records.record_text: United Nations representatives presented the deterioration of the security situation in the eastern provinces, marked by the continued expansion of the Mouvement du 23 mars (M23).
records.policy_implication: Highlights the critical threat posed by M23 expansion to regional stability.

records.record_text: Congolese authorities and people said they expected the international community to condemn and impose sanctions on Rwanda.
records.geographic_scope: Democratic Republic of the Congo / Rwanda
records.political_signal: Demands multilateral targeted sanctions and official condemnation of Rwandan support for M23.
records.policy_implication: Pressures UN Security Council to enforce sanctions against external state interference.

records.record_text: United Nations representatives underscored the need for a political solution to the crisis and for concerted support for the Nairobi and Luanda processes, as complementary regional initiatives.
records.policy_implication: Reaffirms regional diplomatic mechanisms as the primary pathway to resolve the crisis.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission members said that the solution to the crisis should be political and that ongoing efforts to implement decisions made under the Nairobi and Luanda processes should be further supported.
records.political_signal: Signals Security Council consensus on prioritizing political and diplomatic regional frameworks over purely military solutions.
records.policy_implication: Guides Security Council engagement toward bolstering the Nairobi and Luanda processes.

records.record_text: United Nations representatives advocated in favour of support to fund the humanitarian response plan in the light of the worsening of the humanitarian situation in the country.
records.policy_implication: Urges donor mobilization to address severe humanitarian funding shortfalls.

records.record_text: On the electoral process, they mentioned persistent tensions around voter registration and possible risks associated with an electoral process that would not respect the constitutional deadline.
records.policy_implication: Flags constitutional deadlines as critical to preventing wider political instability.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council mission observed that MONUSCO was operating in a very hostile environment, which impeded delivery on its mandate and the work of humanitarian actors.
records.policy_implication: Emphasizes the need for host state cooperation to mitigate anti-UN hostility and mandate operational bottlenecks.

records.record_text: MONUSCO representatives underlined the need to enforce the decision of the Congolese authorities not to integrate members of armed groups into the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.policy_implication: Supports ending the cycle of impunity and armed group recycling within national armed forces.

records.record_text: MONUSCO began providing logistical support to the Independent National Electoral Commission, at its official request, through the transport of 130 tons of electoral materials and continued to work with the United Nations country team to support efforts to consolidate the judicial system and transitional justice and prevent the recruitment of children.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates practical UN logistical support to technical electoral prep and institutional consolidation.

records.record_text: United Nations representatives also mentioned coordination and communication between MONUSCO, the Congolese armed forces, the East African Community regional force and bilateral forces, as part of efforts to deconflict operations and ensure effective protection of civilians.
records.policy_implication: Highlights complex operational coordination required among multiple military forces operating in eastern DRC.

records.record_text: Specific requests were made to Member States to provide MONUSCO with capacities and adequate means to support the implementation of its mandate, as set out in Security Council resolution 2666 (2022).
records.policy_implication: Urges force generation and capability pledges for MONUSCO.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister thanked the Council for having responded to the request of the Congolese authorities to lift the notification requirement for the provision of military materiel and assistance.
records.policy_implication: Acknowledges positive Council action on DRC sanctions modifications regarding arms notifications.

records.record_text: The Council delegation informed those present that the objective of the visit was to express solidarity with the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the context of the deteriorating security situation in the east and to identify areas where its support was needed.
records.political_signal: Conveys Council solidarity with DRC and willingness to assist amid security degradation.
records.policy_implication: Sets supportive diplomatic tone for the Council visit.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister gave a briefing on the security situation in the east and called upon the Security Council to examine evidence of support by Rwanda for M23, as contained in the reports of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and to impose sanctions against Rwanda.
records.political_signal: Formal state request for sanctions against Rwanda based on UN Group of Experts findings.
records.policy_implication: Places burden on Security Council to consider sanctions regime expansion.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister requested the support of the Council for regional efforts, an update of the Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Region (commonly known as the Addis Ababa framework agreement), in the light of the current security situation, and the implementation of the recommendations of the mini-summit held in Luanda on 23 November 2022.
records.political_signal: Demands modernization of the 2013 Addis Ababa framework to reflect present security realities.
records.policy_implication: Signals regional consensus on reviewing formal political peace frameworks.

records.record_text: Referring to the memorandum of 10 March 2023 on the new partnership between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the United Nations... Christophe Lutundula Apala Pen’apala noted that the new partnership should focus on the following three priorities for the Democratic Republic of the Congo: peace and security; political stability; and social and economic development.
records.actor_source: Vice-Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of the DRC
records.policy_implication: Defines host government core expectations for redefined UN engagement.

records.record_text: On MONUSCO, the Council’s interlocutors explained that the President had instructed the Government to work with the United Nations country team to review the joint transition plan, in order to focus the Mission’s role on the following four benchmarks: security; the protection of civilians; the Disarmament, Demobilization, Community Recovery and Stabilization Programme; and the electoral process.
records.policy_implication: Refocuses MONUSCO transition plan onto four essential mandate priorities.

records.record_text: They urged the Council to adapt the Mission’s mandate from peacekeeping to peacemaking or to provide the MONUSCO force with an effective Intervention Brigade.
records.political_signal: Demands structural shift toward robust peace enforcement against M23.
records.policy_implication: Challenges Security Council to adapt peacekeeping concepts to active conflict environment.

records.record_text: He called upon the United Nations to mobilize resources to support the implementation of the Disarmament, Demobilization, Community Recovery and Stabilization Programme.
records.actor_source: Vice-Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of the DRC
records.policy_implication: Highlights crucial funding gaps in national DDR-CS architecture.

records.record_text: The Vice-Prime Minister also reaffirmed the commitment of the Congolese authorities to hold elections in 2023, in accordance with Constitutional deadlines but cautioned that the persistent security situation in the east could impede the holding of an inclusive electoral process.
records.actor_source: Vice-Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of the DRC
records.policy_implication: Warns that eastern conflict threatens general franchise and electoral integrity.

records.record_text: On the issue of the repatriation of refugees, the Vice-Prime Minister reiterated his call upon the United Nations to support, through resource mobilization, the implementation of the 2010 tripartite agreement among the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
records.actor_source: Vice-Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of the DRC
records.policy_implication: Re-engages tripartite humanitarian agreements for refugee repatriation.

records.record_text: On the illicit exploitation of natural resources, he called upon the Security Council to impose sanctions on perpetrators and to strengthen verification mechanisms.
records.actor_source: Vice-Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of the DRC
records.policy_implication: Calls for targeted sanctions against networks profiting from illegal natural resource extraction.

records.record_text: The Council members also stressed that MONUSCO was deployed in the country to protect civilians and to help to restore stability, adding that United Nations personnel should be protected by the host country.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms legal status of forces obligation of the host state to protect UN peacekeepers.
records.policy_implication: Reminds government of status-of-forces duties amid anti-UN violence.

records.record_text: The President of the National Assembly called for all foreign support for the “aggression” against the Democratic Republic of the Congo to end and urged the Security Council to examine the report of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo regarding Rwandan support for M23.
records.actor_source: President of the National Assembly of the DRC
records.political_signal: Parliamentary demand for Council action against state support for domestic rebels.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces executive calls for Security Council investigation and sanctions.

records.record_text: The President of the National Assembly stated that the Congolese authorities were ready for dialogue, but stressed that M23 should withdraw from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.actor_source: President of the National Assembly of the DRC
records.political_signal: Sets unconditional precondition of M23 territorial withdrawal prior to political negotiations.
records.policy_implication: Frames state negotiation parameters under Luanda roadmap.

records.record_text: The President of the National Assembly noted that the perceived inaction of MONUSCO in areas where attacks against civilians occurred had prompted demonstrations against MONUSCO in July 2022.
records.actor_source: President of the National Assembly of the DRC
records.policy_implication: Explains public hostility toward MONUSCO as stemming from unmet protection expectations.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council mission encouraged the authorities of the Democratic Republic of the Congo to continue to work towards peaceful, transparent, inclusive and credible processes for the presidential and legislative elections scheduled in 2023, in accordance with the Constitution and electoral law, and stressed the importance of avoiding incitement to violence and of stepping up efforts to widen democratic space.
records.political_signal: Strong Council message calling for timely elections, protection of democratic space, and non-violence.
records.policy_implication: Defines Council political benchmark for political stability and election observation.

records.record_text: Representatives of civil society organizations stressed that the persistent security situation in the eastern provinces and the lack of credibility with regard to the Independent National Electoral Commission and the Constitutional Court were the main constraints for the holding of inclusive, free and fair elections.
records.policy_implication: Highlights distrust in electoral bodies as a primary risk to post-election stability.

records.record_text: Women leaders advocated in favour of the meaningful participation of civil society, including women’s groups, in ongoing political and peace processes and called for better protection of victims of sexual violence.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces WPS agenda implementation across Nairobi/Luanda processes and justice frameworks.

records.record_text: On the electoral process, some opposition leaders called for a consensual review of the composition of the Independent National Electoral Commission and the Constitutional Court and warned of the risk of political instability if the electoral process was not consensual, transparent, inclusive, credible and respectful of the constitutional deadline.
records.political_signal: Signals potential non-recognition of election results without institutional consensus.
records.policy_implication: Underscores need for political dialogue on electoral institutions.

records.record_text: The President's remarks were focused mainly on the deterioration of the security situation in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of relations with Rwanda. He stressed that the instability in the eastern part of the country was linked mainly to the illegal exploitation of natural resources.
records.policy_implication: Links regional military conflict directly to cross-border illegal resource exploitation.

records.record_text: He underscored that to regain the credibility of MONUSCO, the Security Council should strengthen the Intervention Brigade to enable it to conduct offensive operations against M23.
records.political_signal: Executive demand for offensive peace enforcement against M23 as key to mission legitimacy.
records.policy_implication: Directly impacts upcoming MONUSCO mandate renewal deliberations.

records.record_text: He denounced the terrorist attacks on civilian populations by the ADF group affiliated with Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (Da’esh) and the use of increasingly sophisticated explosive devices.
records.policy_implication: Highlights evolving counter-terrorism threats (IEDs/Da'esh link) in eastern DRC.

records.record_text: The Governor also provided information to the Security Council delegation on the illegal exploitation of natural resources and called upon the Council to require States members of the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region to respect the Protocol against the Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources of 30 November 2006 and to require international organizations involved in mining governance to launch a mechanism on the traceability of minerals exported by Rwanda.
records.policy_implication: Urges mandatory mineral traceability mechanisms targeting regional trade hubs.

records.record_text: Lieutenant General Nassone gave a briefing to the members of the Council mission on the work of the mechanism and informed them that M23 was not respecting the various timelines for its withdrawal.
records.actor_source: Head of Ad Hoc Verification Mechanism (Luanda process)
records.policy_implication: Confirms M23 non-compliance with Luanda process withdrawal timetables.

records.record_text: Major General Nyagah gave a briefing on the new deployment posture of the regional force and noted that control of supply roads to Goma by M23 was having a serious impact on the price of basic commodities, on humanitarian access and on freedom of movement and stressed the need to support the political tracks of the Nairobi process and the Luanda process through diplomatic pressure on M23 and its allies.
records.policy_implication: Underscores severe socio-economic and humanitarian siege conditions around Goma.

records.record_text: The exchange with the MONUSCO force revealed that the Mission had adapted its posture through physical presence and escorts, in order to better address the threat posed by armed groups such as ADF, CODECO and Mai-Mai, which continued their attacks against civilians in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.policy_implication: Reports operational adaptations for protection of civilians despite resource constraints.

records.record_text: Emphasis was placed on the need to accelerate security sector reforms by ensuring the professionalization of the Congolese armed forces, with a structured and clear chain of command.
records.policy_implication: Identifies command-and-control reform in FARDC as precondition for successful security transition.

records.record_text: The mission members indicated that the Council looked forward to receiving options for the reconfiguration of MONUSCO from the Secretary-General.
records.political_signal: Signals Council readiness to evaluate concrete mandate transformation and transition options.
records.policy_implication: Sets mandate review task for Secretariat ahead of upcoming mission report.

records.record_text: Experts made the following recommendations to strengthen security in artisanal mining areas: to provide support to States demonstrating a high level of commitment to the implementation, at the national level, of measures relating to the responsible sourcing of minerals; to support the implementation of initiatives that promote fair trade in minerals in the Great Lakes region; to advocate in favour of multi-donor support to strengthen the capacity of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the governance of the mining sector; to provide technical support to the National Commission to Combat Mining Fraud; to promote the use of national initiatives and the operationalization of local multi-stakeholder structures; to encourage destination countries and consumers of mining products to set up funds to support the stabilization and development of countries of origin; and to encourage States members of the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region to respect their commitments for the establishment of responsible supply chains and to boost the stability of mining areas.
records.actor_target: UN Security Council / Donors / ICGLR Member States
records.policy_implication: Provides comprehensive actionable policy roadmap for mineral governance and conflict-free supply chains.

records.record_text: The delegation reiterated the Council’s support for women leaders and committed itself to continuing to work towards the restoration of peace and stability in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.actor_target: Women Civil Society Leaders / DRC Population
records.political_signal: Reaffirms Security Council commitment to WPS and security restoration in eastern DRC.
records.policy_implication: Solidifies UN support for women civil society actors in regional peace tracks.

records.record_text: The delegation took note of the situation and pledged to work towards an urgent response to provide humanitarian assistance to the population in need.
records.political_signal: Pledges Council advocacy for urgent humanitarian funding for displaced populations.
records.policy_implication: Drives international attention toward severe IDP conditions in North Kivu.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Mali and the Niger, 23–25 October 2021

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Assessment of political transition, peace agreement implementation, and regional security
main_risks: Deteriorating security situation and expansion of violent extremist group activity in Mali and the central Sahel
Uncertainty and delays regarding the return to constitutional order and the agreed election timeline
Slow progress in implementing the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali
Severe humanitarian crisis, displacement, and severe underfunding of humanitarian response plans
Socioeconomic hardship, loss of educational opportunities, and risk of youth radicalization
main_commitments: Commitment by Malian transitional President to return to constitutional rule
Malian transitional Government's proposal to integrate 13,000 former rebel combatants into the army
Security Council support for political transition, MINUSMA, and ECOWAS/AU mediation efforts
Government of the Niger's commitment to safe, voluntary return of IDPs and refugees and prioritization of education reforms
main_policy_signals: Insistence by the Security Council and ECOWAS on adhering to the election timeline and transition charter
Call for accelerated implementation of priority measures under the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali
Need for predictable, sustainable support and funding mechanisms for regional counter-terrorism efforts and the G5 Sahel Joint Force
Urgency of holistic strategies addressing governance, security, human rights, and development root causes
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Mali and the Niger from 23 to 25 October 2021 focused on evaluating support for Mali's political transition, the implementation of the 2015 Peace Agreement, and the security and humanitarian dynamics in the broader Sahel. The mission highlighted critical political tensions regarding election timelines, escalating security threats from armed groups, and the urgent need for comprehensive governance, humanitarian, and development responses. Council members emphasized adherence to transition commitments while reaffirming engagement with regional partners and UN entities.

activities.activity_description: Meeting with the transitional President of Mali, Colonel Assimi Goïta, and Prime Minister Choguel Maïga in Bamako, Mali.
Meeting with signatory armed groups to the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali.
Engagement session with civil society representatives in Mali.
Briefing by Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Mali and Head of MINUSMA El Ghassim Wane, along with the MINUSMA Acting Force Commander and Police Commissioner.
Meeting with the United Nations country team in Mali.
Meeting with women representatives of signatory armed groups in Mali.
Consultation with the international mediation team led by the Ambassador of Algeria to Mali.
Meeting with the President of the Niger, Mohamed Bazoum, in Niamey.
Meeting with the Prime Minister of the Niger, Mahamadou Ouhoumoudou, and Foreign Minister Hassoumi Massoudou.
Briefing by Major General Oumar Bikimo, Commander of the Joint Force of the Group of Five for the Sahel, and staff at the joint command mechanism in the central sector.
Meeting and lunch hosted by the Resident Coordinator ad interim Diana Ofwona with the United Nations country team in the Niger.
Wreath-laying and tribute ceremony in Niamey for victims who lost their lives combating terrorism.
