records.record_text: Achieving this coherence would require innovative arrangements, shared strategic analysis and the harmonization of decision-making procedures. It would also require the development of a rapid intervention force for immediate regional responses to African conflicts.
records.actor_source: Alpha Oumar Konaré, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: Call for structural harmonization and rapid response capability between UN and AU.
records.policy_implication: May require establishing shared strategic analysis units and rapid response force frameworks.

records.record_text: Notwithstanding ongoing capacity-building initiatives, including the welcome establishment of a United Nations team to support the development of the African Standby Force, a major obstacle to a sustainable approach remained the lack of predictable funding. Reliance on voluntary donor funding inhibited long-term planning and deterred potential troop contributors.
records.political_signal: Voluntary funding models are insufficient for African security architecture sustainability.
records.policy_implication: Encourages consideration of UN assessed contributions for AU-led peace support operations.

records.record_text: Further to that principle, the Peace and Security Council also urged the Security Council to consider the possibility of financing African Union peace support missions from assessed contributions, as requested in the decision of the Assembly of Heads of State and Government of the African Union (Assembly/AU/Dec.145(VIII)).
records.actor_source: African Union Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Formal request from AU for UN assessed funding for AU peace operations.
records.policy_implication: UNSC must evaluate statutory and budgetary mechanisms under Chapter VIII.

records.record_text: They agreed to consider, on the basis of the forthcoming report of the Secretary-General, the modalities for supporting and improving in a sustained way the resource base and capacity of the African Union, and to examine the possibility of the financing of a peacekeeping operation undertaken by the African Union.
records.actor_source: United Nations Security Council and African Union Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: United Nations Secretariat and AU Commission
records.political_signal: Joint willingness to explore assessed UN funding for AU missions.
records.policy_implication: Prepares ground for Secretary-General's report on AU funding modalities.

records.record_text: The Chairperson of the African Union Commission stressed the urgent need to address the ongoing financial crisis of AMIS, which had caused lengthy delays in paying troops. He confirmed his understanding that the acceptance by the Government of the Sudan of the hybrid operation was unconditional.
records.actor_source: Alpha Oumar Konaré, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
records.political_signal: Urgent funding required for AMIS while confirming Sudan's acceptance of hybrid mission is unconditional.
records.policy_implication: Accelerated UNSC authorization and funding required to prevent AMIS operational collapse.

records.record_text: The mission stressed that the Security Council could recommend United Nations funding for the hybrid operation only if there was full accountability and transparency in the management of resources, and United Nations involvement in command and control.
records.actor_target: African Union Commission and Government of Sudan
records.political_signal: UN assessed funding is conditional on strict accountability and UN command structures.
records.policy_implication: Hybrid operation command structure must comply with UN standard governance.

records.record_text: The President and the Foreign Minister both confirmed their full acceptance of the hybrid United Nations-African Union operation.
records.actor_source: President and Foreign Minister of the Sudan
records.political_signal: Sudan formally reconfirms agreement to UN-AU hybrid operation.
records.policy_implication: Clears main political hurdle for UNSC resolution drafting.

records.record_text: Responding to the various briefs presented by the Government, several members of the mission stated that information provided by non-governmental organizations on the ground suggested different conditions from those described in the briefs. The members of the mission also inquired about the Government position on prosecutions by the International Criminal Court.
records.political_signal: Discrepancy between Government claims and ground reports regarding humanitarian/security conditions and ICC justice.
records.policy_implication: UNSC maintains scrutiny on humanitarian access and ICC compliance.

records.record_text: In the absence of an agreement on the demarcation of the boundary, however, both of these processes were at risk.
records.actor_source: Acting Special Representative of the Secretary-General for the Sudan
records.political_signal: Boundary demarcation stalemate threatens CPA election and troop redeployment deadlines.
records.policy_implication: Urgent mediation required on north-south border demarcation.

records.record_text: That the Security Council seek to authorize as soon as possible the deployment of the hybrid United Nations-African Union peacekeeping operation to Darfur;
records.political_signal: Immediate UNSC authorization of hybrid mission required.
records.policy_implication: Drafting and adoption of resolution mandating UNAMID.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister had secured the agreement of the Government to a 'consensual' road map for the implementation of the Agreement.
records.actor_source: Guillaume Soro, Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
records.political_signal: Political consensus achieved within Ivorian Cabinet on implementation roadmap.
records.policy_implication: Provides framework for UNOCI technical support.

records.record_text: The security situation throughout the country, however, remained precarious owing to the persistence of frequent criminal incidents. The mission was also noted that illegal roadblocks remained in place, including in Abidjan.
records.actor_source: Leaders of Impartial Forces / Security Council Mission
records.political_signal: Law enforcement gaps and illegal checkpoints threaten public security.
records.policy_implication: Requires operationalization of mixed gendarmerie units and security sector reform.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister noted that he had informed the Facilitator that, in his view, the implementation of the Agreement faced a two-month delay at this stage.
records.actor_source: Guillaume Soro, Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
records.political_signal: Acknowledge realistic timelines and minor technical slippage without losing momentum.
records.policy_implication: Adjust election preparation schedules flexibly while maintaining pressure on key benchmarks.

records.record_text: President Gbagbo concurred with the views of the mission. He stressed the need for certification and called for the United Nations to play a key role in ensuring the credibility of the elections, including the certification of each stage of the electoral process.
records.actor_source: Laurent Gbagbo, President of Côte d'Ivoire
records.political_signal: Formal request by Ivorian President for full UN certification of electoral process.
records.policy_implication: UNOCI/UN SRSG mandate must explicitly include step-by-step election certification.

records.record_text: That the Security Council carefully examine the request for a partial lifting of the arms embargo regime — and that the Committee established pursuant to resolution 1572 (2004), should it be seized with a request for exemption, carefully examine such a request — in order to contribute to the peace process, taking into account the peaceful implementation of the Ouagadougou Agreement.
records.actor_target: United Nations Security Council and Sanctions Committee
records.political_signal: Openness to targeted embargo exemptions to equip police forces if security reforms progress.
records.policy_implication: Sanctions Committee review of arms exemptions for civilian law enforcement.

records.record_text: The Government solution, which allowed for the nominal integration or mixage of the insurgent troops with units of the Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), has resulted in increasing the military influence of Nkunda in the region. The newly established mixed units subsequently launched offensive operations against FDLR with disastrous humanitarian consequences, including the displacement of more than 100,000 persons.
records.political_signal: Flawed mixage strategy empowered renegade commander Nkunda and caused mass civilian displacement.
records.policy_implication: Immediate termination of mixage in favor of standard brassage and military integration.

records.record_text: The President of the Senate stressed the need for a political rather than a judicial solution to be found concerning Bemba's future.
records.actor_source: Léon Kengo Wa Dondo, President of the Senate of the DRC
records.actor_target: Security Council Mission / Government of the DRC
records.political_signal: Call for political compromise regarding exiled opposition leader Jean-Pierre Bemba to maintain political stability.
records.policy_implication: Encourages political dialogue between AMP ruling coalition and opposition.

records.record_text: The mission urged its interlocutors to rapidly adopt a clear strategy focusing on political and diplomatic means to put an end to the conflict in the Kivus and address the long-standing root causes of the conflict, including inter-ethnic tensions, land, security and economic grievances and the regional dimension.
records.political_signal: Military-only approaches in the Kivus are inadequate; comprehensive political and regional strategy needed.
records.policy_implication: UN and MONUC to assist DRC in developing a holistic regional stabilization strategy.

records.record_text: In the light of its current financial and operational constraints, including the lack of training of a large number of soldiers, the Government had decided to prioritize the training of two or three well-trained and equipped elite brigades, which would focus on addressing the country's security concerns. The remainder of the armed forces would be constituted into a 'development army'...
records.political_signal: DRC army reform strategy focuses on small rapid reaction units and converting untrained troops into civil development units.
records.policy_implication: International SSR assistance must align with prioritized brigade training plans.

records.record_text: That the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo seeks a solution to the crisis in the Kivus through political and diplomatic means. The mission also stresses that the mixage experiment in North Kivu should be terminated and replaced with a real brassage, consistent with the principles of the integration of FARDC;
records.political_signal: Definitive call to abandon mixage and prioritize diplomatic conflict resolution in Kivus.
records.policy_implication: MONUC support contingent on standard army brassage procedures.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission on the Kosovo issue

main_risks: Risk of security escalation and instability if Kosovo's status remains undefined
Potential unilateral actions or establishment of faits accomplis on the ground
Persistent low rate of return and unaddressed obstacles for internally displaced persons
Deep inter-ethnic division and lack of trust between Kosovo Albanians and Kosovo Serbs
main_commitments: Provisional Institutions committed to implementing standards and building multi-ethnic state structures
NATO and KFOR commitment to maintain a safe and secure environment and protect religious sites
European Union commitment to forward planning and providing a European integration perspective
main_policy_signals: Belgrade and Kosovo Serbs firmly reject independence and the Ahtisaari settlement proposal, calling for broad autonomy and renewed direct negotiations
Kosovo Albanian leadership and non-Serb minorities strongly support the settlement proposal and demand rapid move to independence without further negotiation
International interlocutors emphasize the need for a clear Security Council resolution under Chapter VII to establish legal clarity and authorize post-status international presence
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Kosovo, Belgrade, Brussels, and Vienna provided Council members with first-hand information on the implementation of resolution 1244 (1999) and the situation on the ground following the presentation of Special Envoy Martti Ahtisaari's settlement proposal. While UNMIK and the Provisional Institutions have established functioning administrative structures, deep political and ethnic divisions persist. Kosovo Albanians and non-Serb minorities strongly advocate for independence based on the settlement proposal, whereas Belgrade and Kosovo Serbs firmly reject independence, advocating instead for supervised autonomy through further negotiations. The security situation remains calm but tense, and sustainable returns of displaced persons remain critically low.

activities.activity_description: Discussions in Brussels with NATO Secretary-General, EU Special Envoy for Kosovo Stefan Lehne, and European Enlargement Commissioner Olli Rehn (25 April 2007)
Meetings in Belgrade with Prime Minister of Serbia Vojislav Kostunica, members of the Serbian Negotiating Team, and informal exchange with civil society (26 April 2007)
Meeting in Belgrade with President of the Republic of Serbia Boris Tadic (26 April 2007)
Discussion in Belgrade with Chairman of the National Assembly of Serbia and representatives of party caucuses (26 April 2007)
Comprehensive briefings in Pristina by SRSG Joachim Rücker and KFOR Commander General Roland Kather (27 April 2007)

Meeting in Pristina with Prime Minister Agim Ceku and 15 Ministers of the Kosovo provisional government (27 April 2007)
Meeting in Pristina with Speaker of the Kosovo Assembly Kole Berisha and political group leaders (27 April 2007)
Meeting in Pristina with Kosovo Serb representatives including Randjel Nojkic and Minister Branislav Grbic (27 April 2007)
Meeting in Pristina with representatives of Islamic, Catholic, and non-Serb minority communities (Turkish, Bosniak, Roma) (27 April 2007)
Briefings in Pristina by EU Planning Team, International Civilian Office Preparation Team, European Commission Liaison Office, and UNMIK Pillar III (27 April 2007)
Visit to Monastery of Gracanica and meeting with Bishop Artemije of the Serbian Orthodox Church and Kosovo Serb representatives (27 April 2007)
Visit to Southern Mitrovica and meeting with Municipal Assembly President Mutsel Ibrahami and local representatives (27 April 2007)
Visit to Northern Mitrovica and meeting with Kosovo Serb political leaders and Municipal Assembly Presidents (27 April 2007)
Site visit to the rebuilt village of Svinjare (27 April 2007)
Briefing on the energy situation while passing the Kosovo Electricity Company (KEK) (27 April 2007)
Visit to the Serb quarter in Orahovac and meeting with local authorities, inhabitants, and Bishop Artemije (28 April 2007)
Visit to village of Krusha e Vogel and meeting with relatives of missing persons (28 April 2007)
Visit to Kosovo Serb return site of Brestovik and discussions with returnees (28 April 2007)
Informal exchange in Vienna with UN Special Envoy Martti Ahtisaari (28 April 2007)

records.record_text: The Secretary-General of NATO described the security situation in Kosovo as calm but tense.
records.policy_implication: Security environment requires ongoing vigilance despite absence of major violence.

records.record_text: He cautioned that as long as Kosovo’s status remained undefined, and its economic development inhibited, the situation in both Kosovo and the region remained at risk.
records.political_signal: Delay in resolving Kosovo's status poses security and stability risks to the wider region.
records.policy_implication: Prolonged status uncertainty impairs economic development and heightens risk of conflict.

records.record_text: The Secretary-General assured the mission that the Kosovo Force (KFOR) was ready to swiftly and effectively respond to security challenges and stressed that violence would not be tolerated.
records.political_signal: Strong military deterrence against any potential outbreak of violence.
records.policy_implication: KFOR maintains full operational readiness to preserve order regardless of status decisions.

records.record_text: The Secretary-General supported the Kosovo settlement proposal and recommendation on Kosovo’s future status prepared by the Special Envoy, Martti Ahtisaari.
records.political_signal: NATO officially endorses the Ahtisaari settlement proposal.
records.policy_implication: NATO is prepared to align its military posture with post-status mandate implementation.

records.record_text: The Secretary-General emphasized that NATO would need a Security Council resolution under Chapter VII in order to accomplish these tasks.
records.political_signal: Chapter VII resolution is essential to provide legal authority for post-status military deployment.
records.policy_implication: Security Council authorization is required to transition KFOR tasks under the settlement plan.

records.record_text: Mr. Lehne believed that maintaining the status quo in Kosovo was not possible and that further delay in the process was in nobody’s interest.
records.political_signal: The status quo is unsustainable and political delay must be avoided.
records.policy_implication: EU urges rapid conclusion of status negotiations by the Security Council.

records.record_text: Commissioner Rehn underlined the need for a Security Council resolution that would provide legal and political clarity.
records.political_signal: UN Security Council action is required to establish legal framework for EU engagement.
records.policy_implication: EU rule-of-law and civilian missions require explicit UN mandate backing.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Kostunica rejected an approach predetermining Kosovo's independence and reiterated that Security Council resolution 1244 (1999) had not been fully implemented.
records.actor_source: Prime Minister of Serbia Vojislav Kostunica
records.political_signal: Belgrade rejects independence predetermination and claims UNSCR 1244 remains unfulfilled.
records.policy_implication: Any status decision imposing independence lacks agreement from Serbia.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister noted that Serbia was not satisfied with the status quo, favoured direct talks between Belgrade and Pristina, and proposed 'supervised autonomy'.
records.actor_source: Prime Minister of Serbia Vojislav Kostunica
records.political_signal: Belgrade offers supervised autonomy through renewed direct negotiations as a compromise.
records.policy_implication: Serbia proposes alternative negotiation track short of full sovereignty.

records.record_text: President Tadic claimed that Serbia’s sovereignty over Kosovo, reaffirmed in Security Council resolution 1244 (1999), had been challenged by the Special Envoy’s proposal, and held that further negotiations were the only way forward.
records.actor_source: President of the Republic of Serbia Boris Tadic
records.political_signal: Serbian Presidency rejects Ahtisaari settlement proposal as violating Serbian sovereignty.
records.policy_implication: Status resolution without direct agreement risks long-term political confrontation.

records.record_text: President Tadic was particularly concerned that Kosovo’s independence could destabilize Serbia and undermine regional stability, thus damaging European prospects for the Balkans.
records.actor_source: President of the Republic of Serbia Boris Tadic
records.political_signal: Kosovo independence carries broader regional destabilization risks.
records.policy_implication: Regional European integration plans could be undermined by unilateral status outcomes.

records.record_text: Special Representative Rücker concluded that UNMIK had achieved what was possible, and that any further progress was dependent on a resolution of Kosovo’s status.
records.political_signal: UNMIK administration has reached structural limits of interim governance under UNSCR 1244.
records.policy_implication: Transition from UN administration to new status arrangements is urgently needed.

records.record_text: President Sejdiu conveyed the Team of Unity’s unanimous and unqualified support for the Kosovo settlement proposal and status recommendation, emphasizing that Kosovo’s independence was the only acceptable option.
records.political_signal: Kosovo Albanian political consensus demands full independence based on Ahtisaari plan.
records.policy_implication: Kosovo leadership refuses compromise solutions or additional status negotiations.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Ceku recognized that standards had not been entirely fulfilled, but emphasized that substantial progress in their implementation had been made and argued that clarity on status would accelerate returns.
records.actor_source: Prime Minister of Kosovo Agim Ceku
records.political_signal: Kosovo government argues status resolution will catalyze remaining standards fulfillment.
records.policy_implication: Standards implementation should proceed alongside status resolution rather than acting as a absolute prerequisite.

records.record_text: Kosovo Serb representatives stated that independence for Kosovo was not an option, the Kosovo settlement proposal was generally unacceptable, and mechanisms for minority protection would never be implemented.
records.political_signal: Kosovo Serbs reject independence and lack confidence in minority rights guarantees.
records.policy_implication: Implementation of status settlement will face boycotts or resistance from Kosovo Serbs.

records.record_text: Members of the Turkish, Bosniak and Roma communities supported the Special Envoy’s proposal, believing it provided an effective protective mechanism for minorities, while citing unemployment as the main challenge.
records.political_signal: Non-Serb minority communities endorse the Ahtisaari settlement framework.
records.policy_implication: Socioeconomic support and employment measures are needed to sustain non-Serb minority integration.

records.record_text: European Commission expressed concern that the lack of political and legal clarity on Kosovo’s status remained a major obstacle to economic development and investment.
records.political_signal: Unresolved political status harms Kosovo's economic viability and investment potential.
records.policy_implication: Defining legal status is essential for structural economic reforms and external investment.

records.record_text: Bishop Artemije asserted that none of the provisions of resolution 1244 (1999) with relevance for Kosovo’s Serbs had been fulfilled and considered the Kosovo settlement proposal entirely unacceptable.
records.political_signal: Serbian Orthodox Church leadership utterly rejects status proposal and UNMIK implementation track record.
records.policy_implication: Religiously linked community opposition complicates reconciliation efforts.

records.record_text: Serb representatives in Northern Mitrovica categorically rejected the Kosovo settlement proposal, believing its aim was to create a second Albanian state in the Balkans.
records.political_signal: Northern Kosovo Serbs refuse integration into independent Kosovo structures.
records.policy_implication: Risk of territorial partition or parallel structures in Northern Mitrovica.

records.record_text: The mission observed that although reconstruction of Svinjare village had been completed by the Kosovo Protection Corps at the end of 2006, inhabitants remained reluctant to return because of security-related concerns.
records.political_signal: Physical housing reconstruction does not guarantee return in the absence of security confidence.
records.policy_implication: Return programs must prioritize security guarantees alongside infrastructure building.

records.record_text: Kosovo Serb returnees in Brestovik indicated that lack of reconciliation and impunity for inter-ethnic crimes were impediments to returns, noting that Kosovo’s independence could negatively affect returns.
records.political_signal: Fear of independence and unpunished crimes suppress sustainable return of displaced Serbs.
records.policy_implication: Ending impunity for inter-ethnic violence is critical to sustainable returns.

records.record_text: The mission concluded that the overall security situation in Kosovo remains calm but tense, with memories of conflict and March 2004 attacks still perceptible, and Kosovo Serbs apprehensive about their prospects.
records.political_signal: Kosovo remains fragile with profound underlying ethnic tensions.
records.policy_implication: Robust international security presence remains indispensable.

records.record_text: The mission observed that Kosovo society is still recovering from conflict wounds, with Kosovo Albanian and Kosovo Serb communities remaining divided and living to a large extent separately.
records.political_signal: Severe inter-ethnic segregation persists across Kosovo.
records.policy_implication: Long-term institutional and social programs are needed to foster genuine integration.

records.record_text: The mission assessed that the Provisional Institutions of Self-Government and UNMIK have made serious progress in the implementation of standards for Kosovo, though more has still to be done.
records.political_signal: Acknowledges institutional governance growth while stressing unfinished standards requirements.
records.policy_implication: Continued oversight of minority standards implementation remains essential.

records.record_text: The mission concluded that the return of internally displaced persons remains a critical element in the implementation of resolution 1244 (1999), noting that the number of sustainable returns continues to be very low.
records.political_signal: Displaced person return rate remains an unfulfilled pillar of resolution 1244.
records.policy_implication: Streamlined return procedures and economic opportunities must be prioritized.

records.record_text: The mission noted that positions of the sides on the Kosovo settlement proposal remain far apart, with Belgrade and Kosovo Serbs opposed to independence and calling for negotiations, while Kosovo Albanians and non-Serb minorities support the proposal.
records.political_signal: Fundamental deadlock between primary parties over status outcome.
records.policy_implication: Security Council must resolve incompatible expectations between Pristina and Belgrade.

records.record_text: The mission noted the importance of promoting a European perspective for the region, including for Kosovo, to provide direction for political and economic development and consolidate stability.
records.political_signal: EU integration framework is vital to anchoring regional peace.
records.policy_implication: European integration offer provides crucial incentive for long-term reform and stability.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Afghanistan, 11 to 16 November 2006

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Security, Governance, and Development Assessment Mission
main_risks: Spread of Taliban-led insurgency and terrorist attacks by Al-Qaida and extremist groups, particularly in the south and east
Burgeoning narco-economy and record opium poppy production threatening state stability and financing insurgency
Weak state capacity, corruption, and continued impunity for warlords and commanders of illegal armed groups
Existence of insurgent sanctuaries across the border in neighbouring countries
Civilian casualties and cultural insensitivities during military operations threatening public trust
main_commitments: Firm and unyielding international commitment in support of the Afghan Government and political transition
Implementation of the Afghanistan Compact as the central strategic framework for cooperation
Continued expansion of UNAMA into provinces to enhance local coordination
Afghanistan and Pakistan commitment to hold cross-border peace jirgas
main_policy_signals: The Afghanistan Compact remains the central Afghan-owned blueprint for international cooperation and must be faithfully implemented
Security gains are inseparable from rule of law, anti-corruption, civil service reform, and counter-narcotics efforts
Long-term stability requires eliminating insurgent sanctuaries and enhancing Afghanistan-Pakistan regional cooperation
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Afghanistan in November 2006 found that while the initial political roadmap under the Bonn Agreement had been completed with functioning democratic institutions, progress under the new Afghanistan Compact was being undermined by an escalating Taliban insurgency, record drug production, rampant corruption, and weak state institutions. The mission reaffirmed the international community's steadfast support while emphasizing that long-term stability requires Afghan-led progress in governance, police and judicial reform, disbandment of illegal armed groups, protection of civilian rights, and robust regional collaboration with Pakistan to address cross-border insurgent sanctuaries.

records.record_text: The mission found that the Afghan partnership, begun in Bonn, Germany, in late 2001, was largely on track, concluding with the launch of the Afghanistan Compact as a new five-year blueprint for cooperation.
records.political_signal: Acknowledges successfully established democratic institutions while pointing to consolidation needs.
records.policy_implication: Focus must shift to faithful implementation of the Afghanistan Compact benchmarks.

records.record_text: Progress in 2006 towards realizing the vision of the Afghanistan Compact has not been as rapid as had been hoped, characterized by uneven efforts to improve governance, intensification of the Taliban-led insurgency, an upsurge in drug production, and continued impunity.
records.political_signal: Highlights that public confidence is being tested by growing insecurity and weak governance.
records.policy_implication: Requires balanced, accelerated delivery of security, governance, and development assistance.

records.record_text: The mission stressed two cardinal messages: firstly, that the firm and unyielding commitment of the international community in support of the Government and people of Afghanistan was unwavering; and secondly, the Afghanistan Compact remains the central, strategic framework for cooperation.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms international support and central primacy of the Afghanistan Compact.
records.policy_implication: Both the Afghan government and international donors must align actions strictly with Compact benchmarks.

records.record_text: The Afghan leadership underscored that the insurgency in Afghanistan cannot be brought to a halt with the existence of sanctuaries for insurgents in neighbouring countries.
records.political_signal: Directly links security challenges in Afghanistan to cross-border sanctuaries.
records.policy_implication: Requires high-level bilateral and international political action to address safe havens.

records.record_text: The mission welcomed the newly unified command structure of ISAF across the entire country and took note of the continuing need of ISAF for adequate forces and resources.
records.political_signal: Supports NATO/ISAF mandate expansion while calling on troop contributors to resource it adequately.
records.policy_implication: Member states must address force generation deficits for ISAF.

records.record_text: Afghan ministers and parliamentarians called for better coordination and increased information sharing between international security forces and the Government of Afghanistan, as well as respect for local culture and religion to avoid civilian casualties.
records.political_signal: Signals local resentment over military operational conduct and civilian harm.
records.policy_implication: Military operations must refine targeting, boost elder consultations, and improve joint communications.

records.record_text: The Afghan National Army remains poorly equipped and understaffed, with only 14,143 combat troops present and available for duty earlier in the fall despite commitments to develop an army of 70,000.
records.political_signal: Highlights severe capacity gap in national security forces amidst ongoing fighting.
records.policy_implication: Requires accelerated equipment, training, and operational support for the ANA.

records.record_text: President Karzai faulted international partners for inadequate and belated efforts to develop the Afghan National Police, which was designed for public order in peacetime and is no longer appropriately structured for insurgency.
records.political_signal: Assigns blame to international donors for delayed support to civilian policing.
records.policy_implication: Police reform must be restructured and adequately resourced to counter insurgency and criminality.

records.record_text: Throughout the mission, interlocutors cited corruption and the perpetuation of a culture of impunity as the root causes of popular Afghan disaffection and unease.
records.political_signal: Identifies governance failure and warlord impunity as driving popular alienation towards the Taliban.
records.policy_implication: Urgent anti-corruption action and political vetting are required to restore government credibility.

records.record_text: Implementation of the Disbandment of Illegally Armed Groups (DIAG) programme had slowed in 2006, requiring high level international and Afghan political commitment to re-energize efforts.
records.political_signal: Underlines that impunity of commanders with official ties severely hinders state authority.
records.policy_implication: Re-energize DIAG through political enforcement against high-level figures linked to armed groups.

records.record_text: Interlocutors observed that parallel administrations had emerged—one international and one Afghan—and urged greater investment in Afghan public sector capacity to disburse funds through the core budget.
records.political_signal: Criticizes off-budget aid mechanisms that weaken Afghan state legitimacy.
records.policy_implication: Donors should shift aid to core budget mechanisms while building public sector disbursement capacity.

records.record_text: The United Nations country team expressed concern that space for human rights and gender equality had recently begun to close, with attacks on schools and restrictions on public discourse.
records.political_signal: Warns of conservative blowback eroding post-2001 human rights gains.
records.policy_implication: Protect constitutional rights and resist efforts to dismantle key institutions like the Ministry of Women's Affairs.

records.record_text: The head of the Afghan Independent Human Rights Commission stressed the importance of reaffirming Governmental commitment to transitional justice by finally launching the Action Plan for Peace, Justice and Reconciliation.
records.political_signal: Pushes for official adoption and execution of postponed transitional justice frameworks.
records.policy_implication: Government must formally launch the Action Plan to address past crimes and promote reconciliation.

records.record_text: Afghanistan's burgeoning narco-economy was identified by the vast majority of interlocutors as a primary threat to stability, with opium poppy cultivation representing 60 per cent of gross domestic product in 2006.
records.political_signal: Frames drug trafficking as an existential threat ('cancer') to state building.
records.policy_implication: Comprehensive strategy required combining alternative livelihoods, ground eradication, governance, and interdiction.

records.record_text: ISAF cited a cross-border impact from the peace deal in North Waziristan, detecting a 70% and 50% increase in security incidents in Paktika and Khost provinces respectively.
records.political_signal: Directly links local Pakistani militant peace deals to heightened insurgent violence in Afghanistan.
records.policy_implication: Border control mechanisms and monitoring of local truce impact on cross-border violence must be improved.

records.record_text: Pakistani Foreign Secretary Khan stressed that a stable Afghanistan was essential to his country's security, detailing deployment of 80,000 troops along the border while noting the difficulties of controlling a long border.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms Pakistani counter-terrorism sacrifices while defending border management complexities.
records.policy_implication: Strengthen tripartite security mechanisms (Afghanistan, Pakistan, ISAF) and joint monitoring.

records.record_text: The mission urges NATO and other countries to maintain and, where possible, increase their commitment to ISAF to meet the challenge of the current security environment in Afghanistan.
records.political_signal: Direct call to NATO allies to fill force requirements and maintain troop presence.
records.policy_implication: Member states must provide necessary military capabilities and remove restrictive national caveats.

records.record_text: The mission calls upon the international community to revitalize its support to the increased efforts of the Government of Afghanistan to implement the programme to disband illegally armed groups.
records.political_signal: Re-prioritizes illegal armed group disbandment as vital for anti-impunity.
records.policy_implication: Sustain political pressure and financial support for DIAG implementation.

records.record_text: The mission encourages the Government to take immediate steps to strengthen justice sector institutions and provincial government, including through the replacement of corrupt officials and local power brokers.
records.political_signal: Demands concrete anti-corruption actions and removal of compromised officials.
records.policy_implication: Afghan executive must support judicial reform plans and purge corrupt provincial leadership.

records.record_text: The mission urges the Government and donors to make the empowerment of women a true cross-cutting priority and to actively defend the provisions for the rights of women enshrined in the Constitution.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms non-negotiable status of women's constitutional rights.
records.policy_implication: Mainstream gender protections across institutional reforms and counter conservative rollbacks.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the list established pursuant to Security Council resolution 1267 (1999) continue to be updated as necessary and on the basis of the most up-to-date information.
records.political_signal: Supports sanctions list maintenance as a functional counter-terrorism tool.
records.policy_implication: Correct inaccuracies and update entries in the 1267 Sanctions Committee list.

records.record_text: The mission supports the ongoing expansion of UNAMA into the provinces and encourages the Secretary-General to consider measures to promote the coordination role of UNAMA both in the capital and in the country.
records.political_signal: Endorses stronger UN leading role in civil-military and donor assistance coordination.
records.policy_implication: Provide necessary resources and mandate support for UNAMA provincial office expansion.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Sudan and Chad, 4-10 June 2006
mission_country_or_region: Sudan, Chad, and African Union Headquarters (Ethiopia)

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Peace Agreement Implementation and Transition Assessment Mission
main_risks: Rejection by the Government of the Sudan of a UN Chapter VII peacekeeping force in Darfur
Deterioration of humanitarian and security conditions in Darfur IDP camps and eastern Chad
Destabilizing cross-border tensions, proxy war, and militia incursions between Sudan and Chad
LRA terror activities and security vacuums in Southern Sudan threatening CPA implementation
Reluctance or failure of non-signatory rebel factions to accede to the Darfur Peace Agreement
main_commitments: Enhancing logarithmic and troop support for AMIS ahead of a transition to a UN operation
Pledging conference scheduled for 7 July 2006 to reinforce AMIS
Adherence to the Tripoli Agreement to diffuse Sudan-Chad border tensions
Establishing a seven-stage roadmap toward full UN operational deployment in Darfur by January 2007
main_policy_signals: The Security Council firmly supports Sudanese sovereignty while stressing that transition from AMIS to a robust UN mission in Darfur is essential for long-term peace
A Chapter VII mandate is a necessary operational tool to protect civilians and counter spoilers, not a vehicle for colonialism or political interference
Donor pledges from the 2005 Oslo conference must be fulfilled to prevent CPA implementation failure in Southern Sudan
Caution must be maintained when engaging politically with LRA leaders indicted by the International Criminal Court
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to the Sudan and Chad (4-10 June 2006) evaluated the implementation of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement (CPA) and the newly signed Darfur Peace Agreement (DPA). While key CPA structures were established, severe security, governance, and funding deficits risk eroding local trust. In Darfur, despite the DPA signing, security and humanitarian conditions remain dire. A critical rift emerged regarding peacekeeping: President Al-Bashir strongly rejected a Chapter VII UN transition in Darfur, maintaining that militia disarmament is a domestic responsibility, whereas the AU, IDPs, and international partners insisted that an overstretched AMIS must be urgently reinforced and transitioned to a robust UN force. Additionally, severe cross-border hostilites between Sudan and Chad and widespread gender-based violence highlight the urgent need for a integrated regional political and security strategy.

activities.activity_description: Meeting in Khartoum with President Omar Hassan al-Bashir, Minister for Foreign Affairs Lam Akol, and SPLM Cabinet Affairs Minister Deng Alor.
Meeting in Khartoum with members of the National Assembly, Sudanese opposition parties, and non-governmental organizations.
Briefing and discussion with the leadership of the United Nations Mission in the Sudan (UNMIS) in Khartoum.
Meeting in Juba with First Vice-President Salva Kiir and senior officials of the Government of Southern Sudan.
Meeting in Juba with the Ceasefire Joint Military Committee and members of the Southern Sudan Legislative Assembly.
Consultations in Juba with the United Nations country team and non-governmental organizations.
Meeting in El Fasher with AMIS Force Commander Major General Ihekire and the leadership of the African Union Mission in Sudan.
Session in El Fasher with the Wali of Northern Darfur, internally displaced persons, civil society representatives, tribal leaders, and UNCT members.
High-level consultation at AU Headquarters in Addis Ababa with Chairperson Alpha Oumar Konaré, Peace and Security Commissioner Said Djinnit, the AU Peace and Security Council, and AMIS TCCs.
Consultation in Addis Ababa with Under-Secretary-General Guéhenno and the UN joint technical assessment mission.
Meeting in N'Djamena with President Idriss Déby, his cabinet, diplomatic representatives, and the UN country team in Chad.
Field visit to Goz Beida in Chad to meet with Sudanese refugees, Chadian internally displaced persons, and humanitarian agencies.

records.record_text: President Al-Bashir made clear to the mission that a United Nations force in Darfur with a mandate under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations was unacceptable to the Government of the Sudan.
records.political_signal: Firm rejection of Chapter VII UN peacekeeping deployment in Darfur by the Sudanese executive.
records.policy_implication: Requires diplomatic negotiation to balance UN mandate robust requirements with host state consent.

records.record_text: President Al-Bashir stressed that it was for the Government of the Sudan to disarm the various militias, including the Janjaweed, by itself.
records.political_signal: Assertion of exclusive national sovereign authority over militia disarmament.
records.policy_implication: SPLM and international contacts expressed doubt regarding the Government's capacity or willingness to disarm militias unilaterally.

records.record_text: The IDPs that the mission met in the Sudan and Chad all called for United Nations protection.
records.political_signal: Grassroots demand for international protection due to lack of trust in domestic forces or AMIS.
records.policy_implication: Increases moral and operational imperative for a robust UN peacekeeping mandate.

records.record_text: AMIS Force Commanders warned that, without such reinforcements, Darfur risked becoming another Rwanda.
records.political_signal: Urgent appeal highlighting potential catastrophic security breakdown if force support is withheld.
records.policy_implication: Immediate necessity for additional troop contributions and logistical reinforcement for AMIS.

records.record_text: First Vice-President Kiir feared that if his Government proved unable to deliver swift improvement in the population's daily lives, the Comprehensive Peace Agreement could be put at risk.
records.political_signal: Lack of donor-delivered peace dividend jeopardizes fragile North-South peace.
records.policy_implication: Donors must rapidly disburse pledged funds from the 2005 Oslo conference.

records.record_text: President Al-Bashir said that the Abyei Boundaries Commission had failed to reach an agreement and that, as a result, he would never accept the subsequent decision of the Commission.
records.political_signal: Rejection of Abyei boundary determination creates a severe hurdle for CPA implementation.
records.policy_implication: Requires political mediation to prevent escalation around disputed border territories.

records.record_text: The humanitarian community strongly urged the Council not to consider cannibalizing UNMIS for any future operation in Darfur.
records.political_signal: Warning against reallocating vital peacekeeping assets away from Southern Sudan to cover Darfur deficits.
records.policy_implication: UNMIS operational integrity must be preserved independently of new Darfur operations.

records.record_text: While expressing determination to see the threat from LRA eliminated, the mission advised caution in dealing politically with LRA leaders wanted for trial in The Hague.
records.political_signal: Mediation efforts with LRA must respect ICC international legal warrants.
records.policy_implication: Peace initiatives with non-state armed actors must align with international justice obligations.

records.record_text: Humanitarian partners reported that between 60 per cent and 70 per cent of women who left the camps to collect firewood had experienced gender-based violence.
records.political_signal: Systemic failure to protect vulnerable women outside IDP perimeter zones.
records.policy_implication: Requires specialized patrols, law enforcement accountability, and targeted protection measures in line with UNSCR 1325.

records.record_text: President Déby said that the Sudan was determined to destabilize Chad and accused the Sudanese Government of supporting raids by the Janjaweed and armed terrorists.
records.political_signal: Allegation of active state-sponsored regional proxy war by Khartoum against Chad.
records.policy_implication: Needs immediate implementation of border mechanisms under the Tripoli Agreement.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission agreed with AU Chairperson Konaré on a seven-stage process towards full United Nations operational capacity in Darfur, targetted for January 2007.
records.political_signal: Strategic alignment between the UN Security Council and the African Union Commission on transition timeline.
records.policy_implication: Phased implementation plan must navigate host nation political hurdles and troop generation constraints.

records.record_text: The mission concluded that there can be no lasting peace in Darfur without the successful implementation of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement, and no sustainable peace in southern Sudan without the successful implementation of the Darfur Peace Agreement.
records.political_signal: Recognizing the total interdependence of Sudanese peace tracks.
records.policy_implication: International diplomatic resources must simultaneously support both CPA and DPA frameworks.

mission_title: Report on the visit to Ethiopia and Eritrea by Ambassador Kenzo Oshima

main_risks: Potential resumption of armed conflict through miscalculation caused by mutual mistrust and military movements along the border
Eritrean restrictions, particularly the helicopter flight ban, causing a 60 per cent reduction in UNMEE monitoring capabilities and endangering medical evacuations
Continued political stalemate due to non-implementation of the Boundary Commission decision and non-compliance with the Algiers Agreements
main_commitments: Security Council consideration of a new resolution urging Eritrea to lift restrictions and Ethiopia to fully accept/implement the border decision
Ethiopian pledge to exercise maximum restraint and not open fire first or be provoked
Commitment to continue efforts to launch new diplomatic initiatives involving influential states
main_policy_signals: Eritrean restrictions on UNMEE constitute a violation of the Algiers Agreements and must be lifted urgently
Ethiopia must fully accept and implement the Boundary Commission's decision without preconditions
Withdrawal of UNMEE would have devastating consequences and must be avoided by resolving operational and political impasses
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: Ambassador Kenzo Oshima's fact-finding mission to Ethiopia and Eritrea revealed a high-risk operational environment facing UNMEE, marked by military build-ups and severe restrictions imposed by Eritrea (most notably a helicopter flight ban). While Eritrea's actions stem from frustration over Ethiopia's failure to implement the Boundary Commission border ruling, the resulting operational degradation threatens force safety and stability. The report emphasizes that UNMEE withdrawal must be avoided, calling for immediate Security Council resolution, lifting of Eritrean restrictions, full Ethiopian acceptance of the border ruling, and renewed diplomatic engagement.

activities.activity_description: Received operational briefings and held extensive discussions with SRSG Legwaila Joseph Legwaila, Force Commander Major General Rajender Singh, and UNMEE staff in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Held meetings with representatives of UNMEE troop-contributing countries and members of the diplomatic community in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Met with Seyoum Mesfin, Foreign Minister of Ethiopia, in Addis Ababa on 7 November 2005.
Paid a visit to UNMEE Sector East headquarters at Assab, Eritrea, on 8 November 2005.
Met with Colonel Zecarias Ogbagaber, Acting Commissioner, Commission for Coordination with UNMEE, in Asmara on 8 November 2005.
Met with Yemane Gebremeskel, Director of the Office of the President of Eritrea, in Asmara on 8 November 2005.

actors_met.actor_name: Legwaila Joseph Legwaila, Special Representative of the Secretary-General
Major General Rajender Singh, UNMEE Force Commander
Seyoum Mesfin, Foreign Minister of Ethiopia
Colonel Zecarias Ogbagaber, Acting Commissioner, Commission for Coordination with UNMEE
Yemane Gebremeskel, Director of the Office of the President of Eritrea
Representatives of UNMEE Troop-Contributing Countries and military personnel
Members of the diplomatic community in Addis Ababa and Asmara

records.record_text: According to UNMEE, the current situation is tense and potentially volatile and could deteriorate further.
records.political_signal: The security situation along the border is unstable and at risk of escalation.
records.policy_implication: Immediate preventative measures and Council attention are needed to avert renewed conflict.

records.record_text: Both Ethiopia and Eritrea have been moving their military forces. Ethiopia has been reinforcing its military in areas adjacent to the Temporary Security Zone, while Eritrea may be doing the same outside the Zone, although UNMEE does not have full capability to verify such movement owing to the restrictions imposed by Eritrea.
records.actor_target: Government of Ethiopia / Government of Eritrea
records.political_signal: Unilateral military movements around the TSZ heighten risk while monitoring capability is severely constrained.
records.policy_implication: Verification capabilities must be restored to preserve military transparency and avoid conflict.

records.record_text: The restrictions have caused serious problems in terms of both operation and administration, the most serious one being the ban on helicopter flights, which has reduced UNMEE monitoring capabilities by 60 per cent and seriously affected medical evacuations.
records.political_signal: The helicopter flight ban directly jeopardizes mission mandate fulfillment and force safety.
records.policy_implication: Pressure must be exerted on Eritrea to lift the flight ban immediately.

records.record_text: I noted the concern of UNMEE that, if the two sides continue to strengthen their military postures, the possibility of the resumption of armed conflict through miscalculation cannot be excluded, given the atmosphere of mutual mistrust.
records.actor_target: Government of Ethiopia / Government of Eritrea
records.political_signal: Mutual mistrust and troop concentrations create an imminent risk of accidental war.
records.policy_implication: Urgent diplomatic intervention is required to lower military tensions.

records.record_text: At the meetings held in each capital, the same difficult dilemma was expressed by the contributing countries: while they wish to maintain the presence of their troops and other personnel, who carry out important tasks for UNMEE, the restrictions are impeding the Mission’s operation and putting their personnel at unreasonable risk.
records.political_signal: Troop-contributing countries are losing patience with operational risks caused by Eritrean restrictions.
records.policy_implication: Failure to remove restrictions may lead to TCC troop withdrawals.

records.record_text: There was a unified appeal from the contributing countries for the urgent removal of the restrictions imposed on UNMEE.
records.political_signal: Unified TCC demand for immediate removal of Eritrean operational restrictions.
records.policy_implication: Security Council must back TCC demands with decisive political leverage.

records.record_text: At the same time, it was acknowledged that behind the action taken by Eritrea were its frustrations over the refusal of Ethiopia to accept the Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission’s decision unequivocally and to proceed with demarcation of the border without preconditions.
records.political_signal: Eritrea's uncooperative behavior is linked directly to Ethiopia's non-implementation of the border ruling.
records.policy_implication: Addressing the border stalemate is prerequisite to resolving the crisis long-term.

records.record_text: Regarding the question of how to break the stalemate, there were some differences in assessment between those based in Addis Ababa and those based in Asmara. Some considered Ethiopia’s call for dialogue a more realistic approach than Eritrea’s insistence on implementation of the Boundary Commission’s decision “as is”, while others showed more understanding of the underlying cause of Eritrea’s frustrations.
records.political_signal: The diplomatic community is divided on whether dialogue or strict compliance with the ruling is the path forward.
records.policy_implication: Security Council needs to reconcile these approaches in its strategic guidance.

records.record_text: Despite the difficulties faced by UNMEE, many believed that its withdrawal would have devastating consequences.
records.political_signal: UNMEE presence remains essential to prevent immediate renewal of full-scale war.
records.policy_implication: Council must maintain UNMEE presence while working to overcome operational restrictions.

records.record_text: Foreign Minister Seyoum generally reiterated the position... that Ethiopia “accepts in principle” the Boundary Commission’s decision as final and binding. In response to my request for clarification, the Minister emphasized that Ethiopia was not asking for partial or total renegotiation of the decision, but rather believed that the decision should be implemented in a practical rather than a mechanical manner, pointing to locations to be reviewed since both Ethiopian as well as Eritrean communities and villages would be affected.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia maintains its stance of accepting the border ruling only in principle, seeking practical adjustments.
records.policy_implication: Ethiopia's qualified acceptance remains a primary point of political friction with Eritrea.

records.record_text: He also stressed that Ethiopia and Eritrea needed to address, as the Algiers Agreements provide, not only the border issue but also a range of other issues, including economic and trade issues, compensation and access for Ethiopia to the sea, and underscored the importance of normalizing relations with a view to achieving peace and stability.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia seeks comprehensive bilateral talks covering broader political and economic relations alongside border implementation.
records.policy_implication: Broader dialogue is rejected by Eritrea prior to border demarcation, complicating conflict resolution.

records.record_text: He indicated that Ethiopia was reorganizing its positions in view of the posts vacated by UNMEE and the recent concentration of Eritrean forces, in particular in Sector West, stressing that the redeployment of troops was for defensive purposes.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia frames its military redeployment as a defensive response to Eritrean force movements and vacated UN posts.
records.policy_implication: UNMEE post evacuations have triggered defensive posturing by military forces.

records.record_text: When I conveyed the Security Council’s concern over the situation, he stated that Ethiopia would exercise maximum restraint, neither being the first party to open fire nor allowing itself to be provoked.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia commits to non-first-use of force and defensive restraint.
records.policy_implication: Pledge reduces immediate threat of Ethiopian offensive actions.

records.record_text: The Minister, criticizing Eritrea for blackmailing the Council through the imposition of restrictions on the Mission’s freedom of movement, emphasized that the Council must not act in ways that would have the effect of rewarding Eritrea’s actions.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia urges Council not to yield to Eritrean coercion or penalize Ethiopia under Eritrean pressure.
records.policy_implication: Council must balance pressuring both sides simultaneously without appearing biased.

records.record_text: Yemane Gebremeskel stated that the current difficulties were a direct result of the violation by Ethiopia, namely, its refusal to accept the Boundary Commission’s decision as final and binding and to fully comply with it.
records.political_signal: Eritrea places sole blame for the crisis on Ethiopia's rejection of the border ruling.
records.policy_implication: No progress on other operational issues is likely without movement on border demarcation.

records.record_text: He criticized the Security Council for ignoring for too long the main reason for the stalemate and for failing to compel Ethiopia to accept the border ruling as provided in the Algiers Agreements and to proceed with demarcation without preconditions.
records.political_signal: Eritrea expresses deep dissatisfaction with perceived Security Council bias and inaction against Ethiopia.
records.policy_implication: Council must address Ethiopian compliance to regain leverage with Asmara.

records.record_text: He rejected the idea of a special envoy of the Secretary-General, saying that it would violate the Algiers Agreements. He also rejected the expansion of the mandate of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General to include political matters.
records.political_signal: Eritrea opposes political mediation mechanisms outside the strict framework of the Algiers Agreements.
records.policy_implication: Diplomatic initiatives must operate within parameters acceptable to Eritrea or utilize non-envoy channels.

records.record_text: He deplored the military build-up by Ethiopia along the border areas as provocative. He said that Eritrea wanted a peaceful solution but warned that unintended consequences could result unless the main problem was addressed promptly.
records.political_signal: Eritrea warns of unintended escalation if Ethiopian border troop concentrations persist.
records.policy_implication: De-escalation measures must address Ethiopian military positions to prevent hostilities.

records.record_text: I raised with Mr. Yemane the risks to UNMEE personnel resulting from the helicopter flight ban. While taking note of those concerns, he pointed out that a large number of Eritrean people living near the border could be affected if armed conflict resumed as a result of the continuing failure of the Security Council to address the major issue.
records.political_signal: Eritrea subordinates peacekeeping operational concerns to the overarching threat of renewed war.
records.policy_implication: Eritrea will not lift flight restrictions based purely on peacekeeping logistics without border progress.

records.record_text: The current stalemate is filled with risk, and any incidents resulting therefrom may cause further deterioration in the situation. To avoid the resumption of hostilities between Ethiopia and Eritrea, the Security Council needs to give serious attention to the question of how to help break the stalemate;
records.political_signal: Passive observation by the Council is untenable; active engagement is required to avert war.
records.policy_implication: Security Council must prioritize breaking the Ethiopia-Eritrea political stalemate.

records.record_text: The restrictions on UNMEE and, in particular, the ban on helicopter flights, which are a clear violation of the Algiers Agreements and seriously impede the Mission’s operational capabilities and put its personnel at risk, should be removed as quickly as possible. Therefore, Eritrea must be persuaded to lift the restrictions. In view of the difficulties and risks faced by UNMEE and the contributing countries, the Security Council must hasten consideration of a new resolution urging in the strongest terms that Eritrea lift the restrictions;
records.actor_target: UN Security Council / Government of Eritrea
records.political_signal: Immediate Council resolution is needed to condemn and demand the end of Eritrean restrictions.
records.policy_implication: Drafting and passing a strong resolution on UNMEE operational restrictions is urgently required.

records.record_text: Full acceptance of and compliance with the Boundary Commission’s decision by Ethiopia must be achieved urgently. Failure to do so would be a violation of the Algiers Agreements. In this regard, the new resolution should urge Ethiopia, for its part, to fully accept and implement the decision;
records.political_signal: The Council must demand Ethiopia's unconditional implementation of the Boundary Commission decision.
records.policy_implication: Resolution language must explicitly hold Ethiopia accountable to its Algiers commitment.

records.record_text: At the same time, the Council should ask the Secretary-General and the countries that have influence on the two parties to launch a new series of vigorous diplomatic initiatives to break the stalemate. While the idea of a special envoy of the Secretary-General appears unacceptable to one of the parties, we should continue our efforts to engage with the parties to end the crisis. The new resolution should support diplomatic efforts to be undertaken.
records.political_signal: Vigorous diplomatic initiatives involving influential member states must complement Council resolutions.
records.policy_implication: Design alternative diplomatic engagement channels that respect party sensitivities regarding Special Envoys.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Central Africa, 4 to 11 November 2005
mission_country_or_region: Central Africa (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Uganda, Rwanda, United Republic of Tanzania)

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Regional Security and Transition Monitoring Mission
main_risks: Continued presence and violence of foreign armed groups in eastern DRC (FDLR, LRA, Palipehutu-FNL)
Logistical and operational challenges putting pressure on the DRC electoral timeline ahead of 30 June 2006
Systemic corruption and irregular salary payments to FARDC military personnel driving local insecurity
Risks of premature peacekeeper disengagement weakening political and security stability in Burundi
Impunity for human rights violations and economic mismanagement across the region
main_commitments: DRC Transitional Authorities committed to respecting the electoral timeline and completing elections before 30 June 2006
DRC Parliament committed to expedited article-by-article review and promulgation of the draft electoral law
Government of Burundi established a committee to negotiate truth commission and special judicial chamber modalities with the UN
Burundian Government agreed to conduct any disengagement of ONUB in a gradual, cautious manner in consultation with the UN
Government of Rwanda established an inter-ministerial committee to enforce the arms embargo and cooperate with the UN Group of Experts
main_policy_signals: Strict adherence to the transitional timetable in DRC with an unalterable deadline of 30 June 2006 for elections
Unilateral military operations or cross-border force without host state consent violate the UN Charter
Peacekeeping disengagement in Burundi must be gradual, cautious, and security-linked to avoid destabilization
Urgent implementation of military pay reform (EUSEC recommendations) and army integration as prerequisites for regional stability
Rigorous regional enforcement of arms embargoes and border controls against illicit arms and natural resource flows
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The sixth Security Council mission to Central Africa assessed critical transitional developments in the DRC and Burundi while engaging key regional leaders in Uganda, Rwanda, and Tanzania. In the DRC, the mission highlighted encouraging voter registration figures while demanding strict adherence to the 30 June 2006 deadline for elections, urgent FARDC integration, and military salary reform based on EUSEC recommendations. In Burundi, the mission celebrated the post-transitional democratic government while cautioning against premature ONUB withdrawal. Across the region, the mission focused on neutralization of foreign armed groups (FDLR, LRA, Palipehutu-FNL), strict enforcement of the DRC arms embargo, prohibition of illegal natural resource exploitation, and absolute respect for state sovereignty under the UN Charter.
