records.record_text: The overall impression gained by the mission is that Guinea-Bissau is gripped by a deep social, economic, administrative and political crisis.
records.political_signal: Highlights severe systemic fragility in Guinea-Bissau requiring urgent international attention.
records.policy_implication: Demands preventative political and economic intervention to stop state collapse.

records.record_text: In Guinea-Bissau, President Kumba Yalá set 12 October 2003 as the election date and welcomed international observers, but he made no commitments on restoring democratic freedoms or respecting human rights.
records.political_signal: Partial compliance on election scheduling accompanied by persistent reluctance on governance and human rights commitments.
records.policy_implication: Electoral assistance must be tied to verified progress on civil liberties.

records.record_text: It recommends that the Security Council monitor closely the progress being made in the electoral process and in implementing the other steps outlined in the presidential statement of 19 June 2003. To that end, the Council should request the Secretary-General to update it by the end of July and regularly thereafter during the electoral period on the progress being made by the Government.
records.political_signal: Establishes sustained Security Council oversight over Guinea-Bissau's electoral timeline.
records.policy_implication: Requires SG reporting mechanism to track compliance with Council benchmarks.

records.record_text: Now that the date of 12 October has been announced for the parliamentary elections, the mission recommends that donors urgently consider providing financial and technical assistance so that the required electoral preparations can proceed and the polls can be held as scheduled. The continuing provision of such assistance should be contingent on the Government creating the conditions for the conduct of free and credible elections.
records.political_signal: Conditions donor aid on democratic compliance while mobilizing essential electoral funding.
records.policy_implication: Donors should establish conditional assistance frameworks for election logistics.

records.record_text: The Government must now urgently take the actions necessary to implement all steps outlined in the presidential statement of 19 June. The international community should maintain pressure on the Government to that end. The mission is gravely concerned that, unless the Government takes such actions promptly and unless enough well-targeted assistance is provided in the near future, there is a strong possibility that the country will slide back into conflict, with dire consequences for the people of Guinea-Bissau and the subregion.
records.political_signal: Explicit warning of imminent conflict relapse if governance reforms are resisted.
records.policy_implication: Urgent diplomatic pressure and targeted aid needed to avert civil war.

records.record_text: The mission greatly appreciates the cooperation of the Economic and Social Council regarding the visit to Guinea-Bissau and recommends that the Security Council continue such collaborative initiatives with the Economic and Social Council in the area of peace-building in post-conflict countries.
records.political_signal: Promotes inter-body cooperation between Security Council and ECOSOC for holistic peacebuilding.
records.policy_implication: Institutionalization of joint UNSC-ECOSOC advisory frameworks.

records.record_text: President Laurent Gbagbo agreed with the mission that the Agreement was the viable way forward and had to be implemented in full. The mission also stressed this message, with some success, to the Forces nouvelles, who at the time of the mission's visit were threatening to withdraw their cooperation on Linas-Marcoussis.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms Linas-Marcoussis Agreement as the sole legitimate framework for Ivorian peace.
records.policy_implication: All parties must align constitutional and military actions with Linas-Marcoussis obligations.

records.record_text: Concern was expressed about the continuing activities of the armed militias, which some allege have links at high levels in the Government of Côte d'Ivoire; there are also continuing reports of murders and disappearances of persons suspected of having links with the Forces nouvelles. Concern was also expressed by senior ECOWAS officials about the Government's economic priorities, including the continuing acquisition of new and sophisticated weapons.
records.political_signal: Signals international alarm over state-sponsored militia activity, rearmament, and human rights violations.
records.policy_implication: Requires strict monitoring of armaments acquisition and militia dismantling.

records.record_text: On 30 June, the Forces nouvelles had issued a communiqué in which they announced the end of their participation in the programme of disarmament, the closure of all the corridors of access to the zones under their control and the declaration of a state of emergency.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates severe breakdown of trust following violent attack on Minister Guillaume Soro.
records.policy_implication: Urgent mediation needed to restore security guarantees and reboot DDR negotiations.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council pay sustained attention to the implementation of the actions mentioned in paragraph 31, especially relating to the appointment of the Ministers of Defence and National Security and the assured security of all government ministers. It suggests that the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Côte d'Ivoire, as Chairman of the Monitoring Committee, should keep the Council closely informed of developments in this regard.
records.political_signal: Prioritizes key cabinet appointments and minister safety as prerequisites for stability.
records.policy_implication: UNSC monitoring must focus on executive appointment deadlocks in Abidjan.

records.record_text: The mission suggests that the United Nations Mission in Côte d'Ivoire (MINUCI) pay serious attention to the important lessons learned from a similar experience in Sierra Leone. In this connection, the mission hopes that MINUCI will soon receive its full complement of staffing, especially in such crucial areas as the political and human rights components.
records.political_signal: Emphasizes rapid operational deployment and cross-mission learning for MINUCI.
records.policy_implication: Accelerate recruitment for MINUCI political and human rights divisions.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that, at the appropriate time, the Security Council support international involvement in the electoral process.
records.political_signal: Prepares UN framework for supporting Ivorian national elections in 2005.
records.policy_implication: UN to plan electoral technical assistance and monitoring mandate for Côte d'Ivoire.

records.record_text: It notes with concern the funding constraints of ECOMICI and urges Member States in a position to do so to provide additional resources to ECOMICI so that it can continue its important work.
records.political_signal: Highlights urgent financial deficit threatening regional peacekeeping presence in Côte d'Ivoire.
records.policy_implication: Member states urged to contribute bilateral funds for ECOMICI operations.

records.record_text: The humanitarian cost of the continued fighting was disastrous: hundreds of civilians had been killed, thousands displaced and most humanitarian aid agencies forced to cease operations.
records.political_signal: Underscores catastrophic civilian suffering caused by renewed assault on Monrovia.
records.policy_implication: Demands immediate international military intervention to secure humanitarian corridors.

records.record_text: The Security Council should commend the dedication of General Abubakar, the ECOWAS team and the Government of Ghana as current chair of ECOWAS for their facilitation and mediation of the Liberian peace talks, and express its strong support for their work.
records.political_signal: Strong political backing for ECOWAS mediation leadership in Liberia.
records.policy_implication: Reinforce ECOWAS authority in steering political transition talks.

records.record_text: The Security Council should insist on strict implementation of the ceasefire in order to create a sufficiently stable security environment for humanitarian agencies to return and to give space for a negotiated political agreement. It should condemn the initiators of any breaches of the ceasefire.
records.political_signal: Zero tolerance for ceasefire violations and attacks disrupting humanitarian relief.
records.policy_implication: Identify and sanction factions breaking the 17 June ceasefire.

records.record_text: The Security Council should make clear that it will not condone any attempts to seize power by force or accept the appointment of those responsible for such attempts to key positions of political leadership.
records.political_signal: Rejects military conquest as a route to political legitimacy or governance participation in Liberia.
records.policy_implication: Exclude insurgent leaders attempting armed takeover from interim executive roles.

records.record_text: The Security Council should urgently consider authorizing an international stabilization force on the basis of current ECOWAS plans, taking account of the ECOWAS appeal for troops and other support from outside the region. While any decision on such a force will inevitably be linked with progress in the political negotiations, plans for deployment should be drawn up rapidly, since delay will risk renewed breakdowns of the ceasefire.
records.political_signal: Urgent call for UNSC authorization of a multinational stabilization force for Liberia.
records.policy_implication: Draft Chapter VII mandate for regional/multinational force deployment.

records.record_text: Countries in a position to do so should consider rapidly providing financial or logistical support to ECOWAS and its member States to facilitate their deployment of a stabilization force.
records.political_signal: Mobilizes Western and international donor logistical capabilities for ECOWAS deployment.
records.policy_implication: Provide airlift, equipment, and sustained operational funding to ECOWAS troops.

records.record_text: The Security Council must insist to all parties that international humanitarian law and the human rights of all, especially women and children, must be respected; that recruitment of child soldiers must cease; and that action will be taken against those who abuse these principles.
records.political_signal: Warns of individual accountability for gross human rights abuses and child recruitment.
records.policy_implication: Prepare targeted sanctions and legal action against grave violations against children and civilians.

records.record_text: The donor community should respond urgently to the serious and immediate humanitarian needs of the Liberian people.
records.political_signal: Urgent plea for emergency humanitarian aid relief for displaced Liberian population.
records.policy_implication: Release emergency funding for food, clean water, and medical aid.

records.record_text: Liberia is likely to require an increased level of United Nations attention and involvement in the short- to medium term. The Secretary-General should consider appointing a suitably senior representative in Liberia at the appropriate time, suitably resourced. A United Nations operation in Liberia should promote close coordination between peacekeeping and peace-building, development and humanitarian programmes, perhaps through the appointment of a Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General who also acts as United Nations resident coordinator, as has worked very well in Sierra Leone.
records.political_signal: Recommends establishing a fully integrated UN multidimensional operation in Liberia.
records.policy_implication: Design an integrated UN structure combining peacekeeping, peacebuilding, and humanitarian coordination.

records.record_text: However, the conflict in Liberia would always threaten Sierra Leone's stability until it was resolved. Over 80,000 refugees had returned, and hundreds of deserters from both the armed forces of Liberia and LURD had crossed the border into Sierra Leone.
records.political_signal: Highlights cross-border vulnerability of Sierra Leone to ongoing combat in Liberia.
records.policy_implication: Border monitoring and disarming of combatants entering Sierra Leone must be reinforced.

records.record_text: The Government of Sierra Leone should intensify its efforts to develop the capacity of the Sierra Leonean armed forces and police to ensure security when UNAMSIL leaves. Donors should support such efforts generously, as assistance here will be less costly than the continuation of UNAMSIL.
records.political_signal: Links UNAMSIL drawdown timeline to local security sector capability building.
records.policy_implication: Increase donor assistance for equipment and training of Sierra Leone police and army.

records.record_text: The Security Council should recognize the linkage between establishing peace in Liberia and consolidating stability in Sierra Leone and the Mano River Union subregion, and should take this into account when deciding on the best option for the drawdown of UNAMSIL.
records.political_signal: Cautions against hasty UNAMSIL withdrawal while neighbouring Liberia remains in armed conflict.
records.policy_implication: Calibrate UNAMSIL drawdown benchmarks to broader subregional security stability.

records.record_text: The successful disarmament, demobilization and reintegration programme in Sierra Leone should be thoroughly assessed by the United Nations system to ensure that such programmes in other countries, particularly in due course in Liberia, take full account of the lessons learned.
records.political_signal: Promotes operational learning from Sierra Leone's DDR model for future Liberian DDR.
records.policy_implication: UN Secretariat to conduct comprehensive DDR evaluation in Sierra Leone.

records.record_text: The Security Council should examine the lessons to be drawn from UNAMSIL for the coordination of United Nations peacekeeping, peace-building, humanitarian and development efforts, so that the transition from peacekeeping to longer-term development can be more effectively managed in other United Nations operations.
records.political_signal: Advocates integrated UN mission design as best practice for post-conflict transitions.
records.policy_implication: Apply UNAMSIL integrated transition structure to upcoming multidimensional missions.

records.record_text: The Security Council and other parts of the United Nations system should give careful consideration to the different roles women play in conflict and in subsequent peacemaking and peace-building; donors should support efforts by civil society to empower women's peace-building efforts and to help those who have been victims of conflict, including refugees.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms commitment to Resolution 1325 (Women, Peace and Security) in subregional peacebuilding.
records.policy_implication: Fund civil society initiatives targeting women combatants and victims of sexual violence.

records.record_text: The Government of Sierra Leone should devote special effort to consolidating its control over the diamond-mining areas by ensuring that police and other civil servants are fully deployed there; and should take all the necessary measures to enforce fully the certification and licensing regime and to enable Sierra Leone to participate fully in the Kimberley Process.
records.political_signal: Demands state regulation of natural resource sectors to eliminate illicit conflict financing.
records.policy_implication: Deploy mining monitors and enforce Kimberley Process certification rigorous compliance.

records.record_text: Donors should respond rapidly and generously to the urgent funding needs of the Special Court for Sierra Leone, and the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. UNAMSIL should provide full cooperation to and support for the Court.
records.political_signal: Strong endorsement of transitional justice mechanisms and closing Special Court funding deficit.
records.policy_implication: Pledge funds to cover $25 million shortfall for Special Court operations.

records.record_text: The local elections in Sierra Leone in 2004 should allow as much community representation as possible, so as to reinforce the principles of inclusion and high standards of governance. The United Nations system should, with the cooperation of the Government of Sierra Leone, monitor the conduct of the elections carefully.
records.actor_target: Government of Sierra Leone / UN System
records.political_signal: Decentralization and inclusive local elections essential for preventing future political marginalization.
records.policy_implication: UN system to assist and monitor 2004 local government election conduct.

records.record_text: The mission believes that the Security Council, as agreed in resolution 1478 (2003), should consider ways of promoting regional compliance by following up its demand that such interference, particularly the provision of weapons to armed groups in neighbouring countries, must cease.
records.political_signal: Demands cessation of state proxy warfare and illegal arms proliferation across West African borders.
records.policy_implication: Enforce sanctions against states supplying cross-border insurgencies.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for West Africa, Ahmedou Ould-Abdallah, undertake a comprehensive study, in conjunction with the Executive Secretary of ECOWAS and concerned Member States, of ways in which the international community can increase its cooperation with, and assist in strengthening the capacity of, ECOWAS.
records.political_signal: Institutionalizes strategic alignment between UN Office for West Africa (UNOWA) and ECOWAS.
records.policy_implication: Commission study on structural institutional support and capacity building for ECOWAS.

records.record_text: In the meantime, the mission believes that the Security Council would benefit from more regular exchanges with the Executive Secretary of ECOWAS and invites him to transmit the Organization's reports to the Council, as appropriate.
records.political_signal: Enhances institutional dialogue between UNSC and regional security organizations under Chapter VIII.
records.policy_implication: Establish regular UNSC reporting channels for ECOWAS Executive Secretary.

records.record_text: Given the proactive and essential role ECOWAS forces have played in a number of West African countries in recent years, the mission recommends that the international community should give priority to the provision of timely and adequate funds and materiel for the various peacekeeping forces set up by ECOWAS.
records.political_signal: Calls for systematic financial and material underwriting of ECOWAS regional peacekeeping initiatives.
records.policy_implication: Establish sustainable funding mechanisms for regional peace support operations.

records.record_text: The mission believes that this Office should be strengthened by resources from within the United Nations or from Member States in order to carry out some of the additional tasks suggested in this report... In order to further improve cooperation with ECOWAS, the mission recommends that, if acceptable to ECOWAS, an officer from the Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General be co-located at ECOWAS headquarters.
records.political_signal: Strengthens UN regional presence in Dakar and operational liaison with ECOWAS in Abuja.
records.policy_implication: Allocate budget resources for UNOWA staffing expansion and co-locate liaison officer at ECOWAS HQ.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that donors give consideration to the funding proposals made by the Economic Commission for Africa for strengthening the secretariat and for economic initiatives among the Mano River Union countries as ways of building subregional cooperation.
records.geographic_scope: Mano River Union (Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea)
records.political_signal: Revitalizes Mano River Union institutions to address core socio-economic cross-border conflict causes.
records.policy_implication: Fund ECA economic cooperation projects in MRU states.

records.record_text: Donor countries and institutions should pay far greater attention to this problem — by providing expert assistance, training and funding — than many have done to date. The United Nations system, with appropriate assistance from Member States, should, with the experience now gained, be ready to provide essential elements for security sector reform in the subregion. This might include the possibility of a regional disarmament, demobilization and reintegration programme.
records.political_signal: Promotes regional security sector reform and cross-border DDR frameworks to prevent mercenary circulation.
records.policy_implication: Develop regional DDR strategies targeting foreign combatants and mercenaries.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that Member States should take all necessary measures to stem the sales of arms to countries under arms embargoes imposed by the Security Council... The mission recommends that the United Nations and ECOWAS propose concrete measures for strengthening the ECOWAS Moratorium on small arms and light weapons in the subregion...
records.political_signal: Calls for strict compliance with sanctions panel investigations and small arms moratoriums.
records.policy_implication: Strengthen national arms export controls and establish SALW verification mechanisms.

records.record_text: The mission urges the parties to conflict to arrest and prosecute anyone responsible for the recruitment of children.
records.actor_target: Parties to Conflict in West Africa
records.political_signal: Criminalizes child recruitment and demands immediate penal accountability for commanders.
records.policy_implication: Investigate and prosecute commanders recruiting child soldiers in violation of Resolution 1460 (2003).

records.record_text: It requests the Secretary-General's representatives in the subregion to make a particular effort to monitor the protection of children, as well as the protection of women from sexual and other types of violence. The mission also encourages them to continue to include this issue in their reports to the Security Council.
records.political_signal: Mandates systematic field monitoring of sexual violence and child rights in UN country reporting.
records.policy_implication: Embed child protection and gender advisers across all regional UN missions.

records.record_text: In addition, the mission noted the serious shortfall in funding for the operations of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees to provide assistance and protection to refugees and also for programmes for internally displaced persons in the subregion, and it calls on donors to make additional contributions.
records.political_signal: Urgent appeal to remedy critical funding deficits for refugee and IDP protection.
records.policy_implication: Mobilize immediate donor pledges for UNHCR West Africa appeals.

records.record_text: The mission hopes that the Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for West Africa will undertake a major collaborative effort with the peace-building and peacekeeping operations as well as the rest of the United Nations system and its partners in the subregion, to devise a practical and concerted regional approach to this pressing problem [youth unemployment].
records.political_signal: Identifies youth unemployment as a root driver of instability and combatant recruitment across borders.
records.policy_implication: Develop subregional employment strategies targeting at-risk youth and ex-combatants.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Central Africa, 7 to 16 June 2003

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Peace Process Support and Field Assessment Mission
main_risks: Persistent military offensives in eastern DRC (North Kivu, South Kivu, Bunia/Ituri) threatening to undermine the national transitional government agreement.
Potential security vacuum and resumption of militia violence in Bunia/Ituri following the expiry of IEMF's mandate on 1 September 2003 without an adequately equipped Chapter VII successor force.
Ongoing armed attacks and refusal of rebel groups (FNL and FDD) in Burundi to implement ceasefire agreements, threatening the second phase of the political transition.
Rampant impunity for gross human rights abuses, child recruitment, and illegal natural resource exploitation fueling continuing violence across the region.
main_commitments: Undertaking by Congolese political parties to establish a functioning transitional Government by 30 June 2003.
Security Council commitment to consider a robust Chapter VII MONUC mandate and force structure for Ituri post-IEMF.
Burundian Government commitment to continue Arusha reforms and initiate preparation for voluntary repatriation of FDD combatants, refugees, and IDPs.
UN Security Council commitment to support the African Mission in Burundi (AMIB) politically, technically, and through appeals for international financial support.
main_policy_signals: Impunity for grave violations of international humanitarian law and serious crimes by armed faction leaders and de facto local authorities will no longer be tolerated.
Transition in the DRC must move forward urgently from military confrontation to political power-sharing; factional interests must be subordinated to national interest.
Rebel groups in Burundi must halt hostilities immediately and join the Arusha political process, as no alternative negotiation framework exists.
Regional States must end all direct and indirect arms transfers to militias in DRC and actively exert positive influence to halt hostilities.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Central Africa (7–16 June 2003) engaged seven heads of State and major political, military, and regional actors in DRC, Burundi, and neighboring countries. The mission focused on securing commitments for the 30 June 2003 inauguration of the DRC Transitional Government, planning the transition from the Interim Emergency Multinational Force (IEMF) to a robust MONUC mandate in Ituri, halting military offensives in North/South Kivu, pushing for ceasefire compliance and donor aid in Burundi, and establishing strict accountability for human rights violations and arms embargo breaches.

activities.activity_description: Meeting in Pretoria with President of South Africa Thabo Mbeki and Deputy President Jacob Zuma.
Meeting in Luanda with President of Angola José Eduardo dos Santos.
Meeting in Kinshasa with President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo Joseph Kabila.
Consultations in Kinshasa with the Commission nationale de suivi, International Committee to Support the Transition, Vice-Presidents designate, RCD (Goma), and MLC.
Visit to Bunia to consult with the Ituri Pacification Commission, Ituri interim administration, IEMF Commander, and humanitarian community.
Meeting in Bujumbura with President of Burundi Domitien Ndayizeye, Vice-President Kadege, and President of the Senate Mr. Bararunyeretse.
Consultations in Bujumbura with the Implementation Monitoring Committee, AU Mission Chief, AU Force Commander, representatives of FDD, and FNL.
Meeting in Kigali with President of Rwanda Paul Kagame.
Meeting in Dar-es-Salaam with President of the United Republic of Tanzania Benjamin Mkapa.
Meeting in Entebbe with President of Uganda Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.
Meeting in Pretoria with the Chairman and members of the Expert Panel on the Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources and Other Forms of Wealth of the DRC.
Briefings in Kinshasa, Bujumbura, and Kigali by MONUC, UN Office in Burundi, SRSG for the Great Lakes Region, and EU Special Representative Aldo Ajello.
Meetings with international non-governmental organizations and women's organizations in Bunia and Bujumbura.
Commemorative ceremony at MONUC headquarters in Kinshasa to honor fallen peacekeepers.

records.record_text: While the Security Council mission noted the progress made so far, members also manifested their disappointment at the slow pace of implementation of the global and all inclusive accord on the establishment of a transitional government for the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: The international community expects faster implementation of the global political agreement.
records.policy_implication: Continued delays in forming the transitional government risk delaying international financial and technical support.

records.record_text: In the view of the Security Council mission, the time for war had passed and the time had come to carry out the political agreements the parties had already signed, and the leadership of President Kabila himself should be fully engaged in order to prevail upon all parties to put the national ahead of the factional interest.
records.political_signal: President Kabila must exercise decisive leadership to prioritize national unity over factional divisions.
records.policy_implication: UN and donor political backing is contingent upon high-level leadership driving the transition.

records.record_text: The mission registered its expectation with all the parties concerned that a functioning transitional Congolese Government would be set up by 30 June, with a unified national army capable of the defence of its national borders and population, and a developing economy in control of the country’s natural resources.
records.political_signal: 30 June 2003 is a strict benchmark for establishing the transitional government and unifying the army.
records.policy_implication: The Security Council will benchmark peace progress against compliance with the 30 June target date.

records.record_text: The mission made clear its deep concern at the persistent fighting that continued to afflict Bunia and North and South Kivu, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, which posed the risk that political agreements might be undermined, and called for all parties in North Kivu to withdraw their forces to positions previously agreed.
records.actor_target: Armed Groups in North and South Kivu
records.political_signal: Military offensives in the east directly threaten the national political transition and must cease.
records.policy_implication: Failure to withdraw forces risks Security Council condemnation and potential targeted sanctions.

records.record_text: The gross and widespread violations of human rights that have accompanied the fighting in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, including murder, rape and the destruction of property, the large-scale displacement of civilians, the use of child soldiers, the illegal exploitation of natural resources and reported cannibalism, were cause for extreme dismay and should be stopped forthwith.
records.political_signal: Severe international outrage at atrocities in eastern DRC; human rights violations must immediately end.
records.policy_implication: Heightened UN monitoring and potential international criminal accountability for perpetrators.

records.record_text: The mission felt that, if properly conceived, the international conference on the Great Lakes Region could help to address and resolve the long-term peace and security issues, following the necessary progress of the peace process in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Burundi, with regional ownership being important for success.
records.political_signal: A regional conference is supported provided peace processes in DRC and Burundi achieve requisite progress.
records.policy_implication: UN Secretariat to continue preparatory steps in coordination with regional states.

records.record_text: The mission expressed the view that the problems of Ituri could best be resolved in the context of the broader political agreement to be reached in Kinshasa among the Congolese parties, so that Iturian issues, institutions and actors could be integrated into the national transitional political process.
records.actor_target: Ituri interim administration and Congolese Parties
records.political_signal: Ituri cannot be treated in isolation; its political solution depends on full integration into national transitional structures.
records.policy_implication: MONUC and national authorities must align local reconciliation in Ituri with Kinshasa political organs.

records.record_text: Some of the mission's interlocutors pointed out that if MONUC was to take over from IEMF as from 2 September, it should be given, at least for a limited period of time, the same mandate and means as IEMF under Chapter VII of the Charter with sufficient strength, proposed as many as 3,000 troops for the whole Ituri region.
records.political_signal: A weak successor mandate will embolden local militias to resume attacks once IEMF departs.
records.policy_implication: Security Council must consider drafting a Chapter VII authorization and robust force deployment for MONUC in Ituri.

records.record_text: The mission called on those of its interlocutors in the region with influence on the armed groups and militias to exert pressure in favour of a cessation of hostilities and the restoration of calm in Ituri.
records.political_signal: Regional actors will be held responsible for the actions of proxy militias under their influence.
records.policy_implication: Diplomatic pressure on regional capitals to sever political and logistical ties to Ituri militias.

records.record_text: The States of the region should take all necessary measures to end the supply of arms to militias and armed groups, and countries should use their positive influence to prevail upon the militias and armed groups to abandon the military option and participate in the political process.
records.political_signal: Cross-border arms flows to non-state armed groups must cease immediately.
records.policy_implication: Potential adoption of formal arms embargoes and enhanced UN sanctions monitoring.

records.record_text: The mission discussed with its interlocutors the possibility of imposing an arms embargo on Ituri, as recommended by the Secretary-General, and many interlocutors expressed support, stressing that to be effective an embargo should be enforced and monitored.
records.political_signal: Broad support exists for a targeted, monitored arms embargo on Ituri.
records.policy_implication: Security Council consideration of formal sanctions mechanisms covering arms flows into Ituri.

records.record_text: The offensive launched by RCD (Goma) taking Kanyabayonga in North Kivu represents not only a violation of the agreements but also a threat to the pursuit of the political process, and the mission vigorously condemns it.
records.political_signal: Violations of ceasefire lines by RCD (Goma) are intolerable and jeopardize the peace process.
records.policy_implication: Immediate demand for complete troop withdrawal and cessation of hostile actions.

records.record_text: Members of the mission drew the particular attention of RCD (Goma) representatives, and subsequently of the Rwandan Government, to their views on disruptions to MONUC's voluntary DDRRR operations, emphasizing that de facto local authorities will be held accountable for any failure to proceed rapidly with DDRRR.
records.political_signal: Obstruction of voluntary disarmament operations will be directly attributed to local de facto authorities and supporting governments.
records.policy_implication: UN Council will hold specific political actors publicly accountable for obstructing peacekeeper operations.

records.record_text: The mission stressed to all its interlocutors that impunity would no longer be tolerated, that those responsible for crimes should expect to be held accountable, and that this responsibility was considered to extend to leaders of armed factions guilty of serious crimes.
records.actor_target: Armed Faction Leaders and Regional Authorities
records.political_signal: Command responsibility applies to political and military commanders committing human rights atrocities.
records.policy_implication: Potential referral or judicial action against individual commanders committing grave crimes.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council be prepared to pledge its full support to the transitional Government to be established in the Democratic Republic of the Congo by 30 June 2003, and call on bilateral and multilateral donors to render all possible assistance in reconstruction, including developing unified armed forces and police service.
records.actor_target: UN Security Council and Donor Community
records.political_signal: Establishing the transitional government will unlock international financial and security sector aid.
records.policy_implication: Donor coordination for Security Sector Reform (SSR) and national reconstruction.

records.record_text: The mission recommends to the Security Council that it increase pressure on the parties, both in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and throughout the region, to ensure that the necessary guarantees are provided to MONUC to permit its verification activities.
records.political_signal: All regional parties must grant full freedom of movement and verification access to MONUC peacekeepers.
records.policy_implication: Security Council resolution reinforcing MONUC's operational access rights and verification mandate.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that consideration be given to what practical steps can be taken to end impunity in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Burundi.
records.political_signal: Practical international judicial mechanisms are needed to stop widespread impunity in the region.
records.policy_implication: Exploration of judicial commissions of inquiry or specialized tribunals.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council be prepared to consider carefully and act on the recommendations to be made by the Expert Panel on the Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources in its forthcoming report.
records.political_signal: Resource exploitation is a core driver of conflict that requires Council action.
records.policy_implication: Follow-up sanctions or regulatory measures targeting natural resource networks financing conflict.

records.record_text: All interlocutors urged the mission to exert strong pressure on both parties in Burundi to cease hostilities: on FNL to enter into serious ceasefire negotiations and on FDD to implement the ceasefire agreement it had signed.
records.political_signal: Ceasefire non-compliance by armed rebel groups is the primary barrier to the Arusha peace process.
records.policy_implication: Increased diplomatic pressure and potential coercive measures against recalcitrant rebel leadership.

records.record_text: The mission called on the Burundian rebel groups to cease hostilities immediately and join the Arusha process, emphasizing that there were no alternative processes and that joining Arusha was in their own interest, while calling on the Army to exercise restraint.
records.actor_target: FNL, FDD, and Burundian Armed Forces
records.political_signal: The Arusha Agreement is the sole legitimate framework for peace in Burundi; parallel mechanisms will not be recognized.
records.policy_implication: Rejection of attempts by rebel groups to reopen core constitutional or political negotiations outside Arusha.

records.record_text: The mission encouraged the transitional Government of Burundi to put in place measures to enable some FDD combatants in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to be repatriated voluntarily to Burundi as a confidence-building measure.
records.political_signal: Cross-border DDR and repatriation build momentum for ceasefire compliance.
records.policy_implication: Coordination between MONUC, Burundian authorities, and regional bodies to facilitate repatriation.

records.record_text: AMIB leadership indicated that preparation of cantonment sites was seriously hampered by the failure of the parties to provide location and troop strength to the Joint Ceasefire Commission (JCC), and urged the mission to appeal to FDD to send its representatives to JCC.
records.political_signal: Failure by armed groups to disclose troop data prevents deployment of peace operations and cantonment.
records.policy_implication: Urgent diplomatic intervention required to make the JCC operationally functional.

records.record_text: The transitional Government asked the mission to respond positively to its request for the establishment of an international judiciary commission of inquiry, as provided for in the Arusha Agreement, to help Burundi put an end to impunity and facilitate genuine national reconciliation.
records.political_signal: An international judicial body is required to overcome domestic impunity and historical grievances.
records.policy_implication: UN Secretariat and Security Council review of options for establishing an international judicial commission of inquiry for Burundi.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council call on the international financial community to assist AMIB with adequate financial and logistical assistance and on the Secretary-General to provide appropriate expertise.
records.actor_target: UN Security Council and Donor Community
records.political_signal: AMIB requires urgent international support to sustain deployment and cantonment.
records.policy_implication: UN Secretariat technical assistance and international trust fund mobilization for AMIB.

records.record_text: The mission sees a clear need for providing adequate budgetary and economic support to the transitional Government of Burundi, warning that all gains achieved so far could collapse if such assistance is not provided immediately, and recommends urging donor countries to fulfill Paris and Geneva conference pledges.
records.actor_target: Donor Countries and UN Security Council
records.political_signal: Economic fragility threatens to destroy political progress in Burundi.
records.policy_implication: Immediate disbursement of donor funds and backing for UNDP donor round table to clear arrears.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council assist Burundi in putting an end to impunity and that it consider carefully the Government’s request for the establishment of the international judicial commission of inquiry as provided for in the Arusha Agreement.
records.political_signal: The Council supports legal mechanisms under Arusha to address grave historical human rights violations.
records.policy_implication: Formal Security Council consideration of Arusha judicial mechanisms.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council Mission to Kosovo and Belgrade, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
mission_country_or_region: Kosovo and Belgrade, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

main_risks: Persistent inter-ethnic violence, organized crime, and extremist tendencies threatening public security.
Extremely low rate of minority return and ongoing displacement across Kosovo.
Severe economic challenges, high unemployment (56%), corruption, and imminent drop in international financial assistance.
Deep ethnic division and lack of willingness among political actors to commit to a multi-ethnic society.
Unilateral status demands and attempts by local provisional institutions to overstep their constitutional mandate.
main_commitments: UNMIK operationalizing benchmarks to measure progress under the 'standards before status' framework.
Full cooperation between UNMIK, KFOR, provisional institutions, and Belgrade authorities to resolve missing persons cases.
Continued international engagement and security presence (KFOR) to ensure stability in Kosovo.
Promotion and facilitation of direct dialogue between Pristina and Belgrade on practical matters.
main_policy_signals: Reaffirmation of 'standards before status' as the only viable framework for Kosovo's future.
Strict insistence on the full implementation of Security Council resolution 1244 (1999).
Unilateral steps will not determine final status; status remains open and will be decided solely by the UN Security Council.
Rejecting violence, extremism, and parallel institutions while demanding genuine inter-ethnic inclusion and multi-ethnicity.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission conducted from 13 to 17 December 2002 evaluated progress in Kosovo under resolution 1244 (1999) and met with wide-ranging actors in Pristina, Mitrovica, Vucitrn, Gnjilane, and Belgrade. The mission recognized notable progress in municipal elections, rule of law, police development, and the extension of UNMIK authority to northern Mitrovica. However, it identified critical fragilities, including slow minority returns, persistent organized crime, economic stagnation, high unemployment, and deep political and ethnic polarization. The mission firmly established 'standards before status' as the governing policy and called for enhanced local ownership, protection of minority rights, and practical dialogue between Pristina and Belgrade.

activities.activity_description: Briefing by Special Representative of the Secretary-General Michael Steiner and UNMIK Pillar Heads in Pristina.
Meeting with representatives of the Provisional Institutions of Self-Government (Ibrahim Rugova, Bajram Rexhepi, Nexhat Daci, Milorad Todorovic) in Pristina.
Meeting with representatives of the Kosovo Assembly, including major Kosovo Albanian political parties and the Kosovo Serb coalition (Povratak).
Meeting with families of missing persons in Pristina.
Briefing at KFOR headquarters by KFOR Commander Lieutenant General Fabio Mini.
Field visit to Mitrovica and briefing on the Kosovo Trust Agency and privatization by DSRSG Andy Bearpark.
Meeting with representatives of Kosovo Serb and Bosniac civil society in Mitrovica.
Briefing by SRSG and Mitrovica Regional and Municipal Administrators on UNMIK strategy in northern Mitrovica.
Meeting with Presidents of Municipal Assemblies in Mitrovica region (Leposavic, Mitrovica, Srbica, Vucitrn, Zubin Potok, Zvecan).
Visit to Kosovo Police Service School in Vucitrn and meeting with multi-ethnic KPS officers.
Meeting in Gnjilane with leaders of returnees, Municipal Assembly President, UNHCR, and NGOs.
Visit to Pristina Municipal Assembly and meeting with deputies from various political parties.
Meeting with a group of Kosovo women representing different ethnic communities, political establishment, and civil society.
Joint press conference in Pristina held by Head of Mission and SRSG.
Meetings in Belgrade with President Vojislav Kostunica, Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic, and Deputy Prime Minister Nebojsa Covic.
Meeting in Belgrade with representatives of the Serbian Association of Families of Missing Persons.
Meeting in Belgrade with Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs Goran Svilanovic.
Press conference in Belgrade held by Head of Mission.

records.record_text: The Special Representative of the Secretary-General stated that Kosovo had made notable progress over the past three years, with important developments occurring in the last six months, including a 27 per cent decrease in crime rate and minority return inflows exceeding outflows for the first time.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates progress in stabilization under UNMIK administration.

records.record_text: Among the problems encountered were attempts by the Kosovo Assembly to go beyond its mandated powers and not fully comply with all the provisions of the Constitutional Framework, particularly with regard to minority interests.
records.political_signal: Reaffirmation that constitutional framework limits must be strictly respected by local self-government institutions.
records.policy_implication: Requires UNMIK to use reserved powers to block non-compliant legislation.

records.record_text: UNMIK was adjusting to face new budget realities with reductions in its budget (18 per cent less than the previous year's funding), accelerating reductions in the Civil Administration pillar.
records.policy_implication: Minimizes monitoring capabilities in municipalities, risking reduced management controls and inter-ethnic oversight.

records.record_text: The situation remained fragile, as ethnically motivated incidents and vandalism hampered the return process.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the necessity of continued KFOR security support and local community commitment to minority protection.

records.record_text: The Special Representative had emphasized the importance of the 'standards before status' concept, noting that, while it had been widely accepted in Kosovo, concrete actions in that direction had yet to be seen.
records.political_signal: Implementation of benchmark standards must precede any final status negotiations.
records.policy_implication: Calls for operationalizing concrete indicators to hold local provisional institutions accountable.

records.record_text: The Council Mission in its interventions supported the 'standards before status' approach and the prioritization of the rule of law, economic development and the return of internally displaced persons and refugees.
records.political_signal: Strong, unified Council support for UNMIK's core benchmark strategy.
records.policy_implication: Establishes benchmarks as the official baseline for future Security Council reviews.

records.record_text: An early recognition of Kosovo's independence was advocated as a means of accelerating the democratization of the region and economic development in Kosovo.
records.political_signal: Divergence from UNSC resolution 1244 baseline by local Albanian leadership seeking rapid independence.
records.policy_implication: Reaffirms necessity for UNSC to reiterate resolution 1244 framework and reject prejudgement.

records.record_text: The Inter-Ministerial Coordinator for Returns provided a different assessment, stating that two thirds of the Kosovo Serb population remained displaced and freedom of movement inside Kosovo remained unsatisfactory.
records.actor_source: Inter-Ministerial Coordinator for Returns (Kosovo Serb Representative)
records.policy_implication: Underscores severe gap between official minority return objectives and actual reality on the ground.

records.record_text: The Mission called upon the Kosovo leaders to publicly denounce acts of violence, hate speech and expressions of intolerance.
records.political_signal: Political leaders must take direct responsibility for inter-ethnic reconciliation.
records.policy_implication: Conditioning political support on clear rejection of anti-minority rhetoric and violence.

records.record_text: Representatives of the families of missing persons sought the Mission's assistance in receiving relevant information from Serbian and Yugoslav authorities on the fate of their family members, including opening court records.
records.policy_implication: Urges UNSC engagement to pressure Serbian and Yugoslav authorities on missing persons archives.

records.record_text: KFOR had assessed that a safe and secure environment existed in Kosovo, punctuated by some acts of violence, but principal challenges included continuing inter-ethnic violence, organized crime, and social and political extremism.
records.policy_implication: Sustained necessity of KFOR presence to maintain stability despite security improvements.

records.record_text: Serbs in the north would be unable to cope without humanitarian assistance, especially as connections with Belgrade were being cut by UNMIK.
records.actor_source: Kosovo Serb and Bosniac Civil Society Representatives
records.political_signal: Kosovo Serb concern over displacement and loss of support structures from Belgrade.
records.policy_implication: Requires balanced UNMIK intervention ensuring public service continuity while dismantling parallel structures.

records.record_text: The Yugoslav and Serbian authorities supported the establishment of a multi-ethnic society in Kosovo, but stressed that Kosovo remained far from this goal and that decentralization and returns were key to improving the situation.
records.actor_source: Yugoslav and Serbian Authorities (Kostunica, Djindjic, Covic)
records.political_signal: Demand for tangible return results and institutional guarantees for Serbs prior to status discussions.
records.policy_implication: Advocates implementation of the UNMIK-FRY Common Document and decentralization models.

records.record_text: The Mission holds the view that 'standards before status' is the only viable way forward.
records.political_signal: Rejection of quick status fixes or premature political negotiations.
records.policy_implication: Mandates UNMIK to focus unconditionally on standard-setting and benchmark evaluation.

records.record_text: Sustainable return of minorities is a precondition for a multi-ethnic society, requiring region-wide and local commitment to supporting conditions for security, confidence-building and economic viability.
records.political_signal: Minority return is non-negotiable for Kosovo's international legitimacy.
records.policy_implication: Directs UNMIK and local government to dedicate resources and administrative effort to return projects.

records.record_text: The Mission urges UNMIK, in consultation with local institutions and elected representatives, to further elaborate the proposal for a decentralization of competences to municipalities without delay.
records.political_signal: Decentralization is essential for securing minority inclusion and local governance stability.
records.policy_implication: Requires prompt UNMIK policy action to design and implement decentralization frameworks.

records.record_text: No unilateral steps will determine Kosovo's final status. The United Nations Security Council will, in consultation with all concerned, ultimately determine Kosovo's final status.
records.actor_source: Head of UN Security Council Mission
records.political_signal: Unilateral declarations or demands for independence carry no legal standing; sole authority rests with the UNSC.
records.policy_implication: Prevents local provisional bodies from attempting unilateral status decisions.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Great Lakes region, 27 April-7 May 2002

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Regional Peace and Security Assessment and Political Engagement Mission
main_risks: Continuation of fighting and refusal of Burundian armed groups to enter negotiations or agree to a cessation of hostilities
Fragility of the inter-Congolese political transition without a fully inclusive agreement among all Congolese parties
Severe economic distress and lack of direct financial assistance/donor funding threatening the peace processes in both DRC and Burundi
Security challenges impeding voluntary DDRRR of armed groups in eastern DRC
Ongoing human rights violations and grave humanitarian conditions affecting millions of displaced persons, women, and children
main_commitments: RCD leadership solemn reiteration to demilitarize Kisangani
Agreement in principle by the Government of Rwanda to accept a delegation representing Kamina combatants as a confidence-building measure
Signing of an agreement by DRC Government, MLC, and RCD to reopen the River Congo to commercial traffic
Security Council commitment to follow up on the upcoming report of the Panel of Experts on the Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources
main_policy_signals: Strong demand for immediate and unconditional demilitarization of Kisangani by RCD and its supporters
Call for an inclusive agreement among all Congolese parties to establish a broad-based transitional authority
Endorsement of a temporary border security 'curtain' mechanism to facilitate complete foreign troop withdrawal
Warning of potential robust measures or regional sanctions if Burundian rebel groups refuse an immediate cessation of hostilities
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The UN Security Council mission to the Great Lakes region (27 April–7 May 2002) evaluated progress and sought to propel peace processes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Burundi. In the DRC, while key milestones were reached at the Sun City inter-Congolese dialogue, the mission stressed the necessity of a fully inclusive transitional agreement, complete withdrawal of foreign forces, and effective DDRRR supported by a robust MONUC deployment in Kindu and an innovative border 'curtain' proposal. In Burundi, despite the installation of a transitional government, ongoing hostilities by non-signatory armed groups pose the single greatest threat, prompting calls for an immediate ceasefire, regional diplomatic intensification, and urgent donor funding to prevent process collapse.

activities.activity_description: High-level bilateral consultations with regional Heads of State and executive leaders in Johannesburg, Pretoria, Harare, Kinshasa, Luanda, Kampala, Dar es Salaam, Bujumbura, and Kigali.
Joint meeting with the Political Committee of the Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement in Luanda.
Meetings with rebel group leaders and political movements, including RCD-Goma leadership in Pretoria and MLC leader Jean-Pierre Bemba in Kampala.
Meetings with Burundian rebel groups in Pretoria in the presence of the facilitation.
Meeting with the Neutral Facilitator of the Inter-Congolese Dialogue, Sir Ketumile Masire.
Meeting in Pretoria with the Chairman and members of the Panel of Experts on the Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources and Other Forms of Wealth of the DRC.
Meetings with representatives of civil society, human rights groups, religious organizations, and women's groups in Kinshasa and Kisangani.
Unscheduled informal encounters with local residents in Kisangani.
Meetings with senior government ministers and the Implementation Monitoring Committee in Bujumbura and Kigali.

records.record_text: There were three main aspects to the conflict, all mutually interlinked, which had to be taken forward in parallel, namely, the outcome of the inter-Congolese dialogue, the withdrawal of foreign forces from the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and the disarmament, demobilization and repatriation of the armed groups listed in the Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement.
records.political_signal: Framework for resolving the DRC conflict requires parallel advancement on political transition, foreign force withdrawal, and DDRRR.
records.policy_implication: UN and international strategy must link political dialogue outcomes directly with military withdrawal and disarming of armed groups.

records.record_text: Since no comprehensive agreement was reached, however, the Security Council mission also underlined the need for further talks among the Congolese parties in order to develop a fully inclusive agreement on the transition.
records.political_signal: Partial political agreements are insufficient; an inclusive transitional agreement involving all major political and military components is mandatory.
records.policy_implication: Facilitate immediate follow-up negotiations among DRC Government, MLC, and RCD-Goma.

records.record_text: The idea was for the creation of a 'curtain' of troops along the eastern borders of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, subject to the invitation of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo... to have the military presence of the countries concerned in a limited portion of the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for a limited period, in order to ensure a better monitoring of the borders, as a stage in the implementation of the Lusaka Agreement.
records.political_signal: Proposes a temporary, cooperative border security force to reassure DRC's neighbours and enable complete withdrawal of foreign troops.
records.policy_implication: MONUC may be requested to advise and monitor border security arrangements.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission reiterated the strong position of the Security Council that the city of Kisangani should be demilitarized immediately and without conditions.
records.political_signal: RCD-Goma must unconditionally execute UN Security Council demands to demilitarize Kisangani without delay.
records.policy_implication: Immediate withdrawal of RCD military forces from Kisangani.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission made clear its position that the Council would severely condemn any party that violated the ceasefire in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: Ceasefire breaches will result in severe UNSC condemnation and potential coercive political fallout.
records.policy_implication: Enforce strict monitoring of confrontation lines by MONUC.

records.record_text: It must also be noted, however, that, of all the original belligerents, only Namibia has withdrawn all its combat troops from the territory. The withdrawals of contingents by Angola, Uganda and Zimbabwe are partial, and need to be finally verified. Reported withdrawals by Rwanda have been verified neither by MONUC nor by the Joint Military Commission.
records.political_signal: Foreign troop withdrawals remain incomplete and lack mandatory verification.
records.policy_implication: MONUC and JMC must conduct full verification of unverified foreign military movements.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission further notes the expression by President Kagame of Rwanda’s willingness and readiness to repatriate and reintegrate Rwandan fighters from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: Rwanda commits to absorbing and reintegrating Rwandan combatants repatriated from the DRC.
records.policy_implication: Operationalize DDRRR repatriation pathways with MONUC assistance.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission takes note of the solemn reiteration by the RCD leadership before the Ministers of the Political Committee and the Ambassadors of the Security Council of their 'irrevocable' commitment to demilitarizing Kisangani, and calls on them to proceed to take the necessary steps without further delay.
records.political_signal: RCD is publicly bound to demilitarize Kisangani following formal pledge.
records.policy_implication: MONUC must monitor and assist the transition and deployment of civilian police.

records.record_text: The mission heard from President Kagame that Rwanda would wish to work closely with such a united administration on the demobilization of the armed groups, and that Rwanda’s presence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was related only to its legitimate security concerns.
records.political_signal: Rwanda conditions troop exit on address of security concerns and cooperation with a unified DRC government on disarming armed groups.
records.policy_implication: Accelerate DDRRR mechanisms and regional security dialogues.

records.record_text: The mission underlined to its interlocutors the importance that the Security Council attached to the question of the illegal exploitation of the natural resources of the Democratic Republic of the Congo... the Council would follow up on the next report of the Panel of Experts to the Security Council.
records.political_signal: Illegal resource extraction in DRC will remain under active Security Council scrutiny and potential action.
records.policy_implication: Prepare for recommendations in the upcoming Panel of Experts report.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission recommends that the Council may wish, following the establishment of a fully inclusive Congolese transitional authority, to consider, on the basis of recommendations to be submitted by the Secretary-General at an appropriate time... adding to the future mandate of MONUC elements concerning the organization and conduct of free and fair elections.
records.political_signal: Future MONUC expansion should incorporate support for national elections once transitional governance is achieved.
records.policy_implication: Secretary-General to prepare electoral assistance options for MONUC's mandate.

records.record_text: Further progress in creating the necessary climate of confidence and security, which is essential to the success of the voluntary approach to DDRRR taken by MONUC, will require the deployment of a robust force at Kindu within the existing mandate of MONUC.
records.political_signal: Voluntary DDRRR cannot succeed without military deterrence and security backing at Kindu.
records.policy_implication: Urgent recruitment of a capable troop-contributing country for the Kindu force within the 5,537 ceiling.

records.record_text: The Security Council should consider supporting the efforts of MONUC to train the Kisangani police force and taking prompt action on the request of the Secretary-General, in his tenth report to the Security Council (S/2002/169), for 85 additional police officers for this purpose.
records.political_signal: Demilitarization of Kisangani requires professional civilian police capacity building.
records.policy_implication: Approve deployment of 85 CIVPOL officers for Kisangani police training.

records.record_text: The continuation of fighting is the most serious risk that faces the implementation of the Burundi peace process. The Security Council mission demanded that the rebel groups cease hostilities immediately and enter into negotiations with the support of the facilitation within the framework of the Arusha Agreement.
records.political_signal: Continued rebel violence threatens to destroy the Arusha transition; non-state armed actors must halt attacks now.
records.policy_implication: Pressure non-signatory armed groups to join negotiation frameworks immediately.

records.record_text: Of all the mission’s interlocutors (the Burundian authorities and regional heads of State), the armed groups alone did not share the view that a sense of urgency was required in achieving a cessation of hostilities... Some considered the time might have come to contemplate more robust measures. If that were the case, the possibility of regional sanctions has been raised.
records.actor_source: Regional Heads of State / Security Council Mission
records.political_signal: Refusal by Burundian rebel groups to negotiate a ceasefire may trigger regional sanctions or punitive measures.
records.policy_implication: Regional initiative and Security Council to coordinate potential sanctions mechanism.

records.record_text: All the mission’s interlocutors, both Burundian and non-Burundian, stressed the risk that the tremendous economic and financial difficulties currently facing the country might undermine the peace process.
records.political_signal: Economic collapse in Burundi poses a direct risk to the sustainability of political institutions.
records.policy_implication: Urgent economic and donor intervention is required to stabilize Burundi's transition.

records.record_text: The support of the international community will be critical. It will in particular be essential for donors to fulfil the commitments they made at the Paris conference of December 2000 and the Geneva conference of December 2001... There is a risk that the peace process, and all the gains made with it so far, might collapse if further assistance, including direct aid, is not forthcoming in the near future.
records.political_signal: Failure by donors to disburse promised direct financial assistance directly threatens Burundi's political transition.
records.policy_implication: UNSC mission follow-up with international financial institutions and donor nations to release aid.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Ethiopia and Eritrea

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Border Delimitation and Demarcation Support / Mandate Renewal Assessment
main_risks: Potential destabilization from unilateral actions regarding territorial transfer or civil authority before modalities are agreed upon
Demining bottlenecks delaying boundary demarcation
Restrictions on UNMEE freedom of movement north of the Temporary Security Zone and outstanding SOFA conclusion with Eritrea
Financial costs and operational delays resulting from the lack of a direct flight route between Addis Ababa and Asmara
Unmet humanitarian needs and funding gaps for Consolidated Appeals and Trust Funds
main_commitments: Reaffirmation by leaders of both Ethiopia and Eritrea that the decision of the Boundary Commission is final and binding
Parties' agreement to establish field offices for the Boundary Commission in Addis Ababa and Asmara
Security Council commitment to prepare a resolution renewing UNMEE's mandate and providing an overall framework for the implementation phase
main_policy_signals: Strong international endorsement of the Algiers Agreements and peaceful resolution through the Boundary Commission
Requirement for orderly transfer of territory and civil authority without unilateral steps
Imperative for full freedom of movement for UNMEE and immediate release of all prisoners of war and civilian detainees
Encouragement for donors to generously fund CAP 2002, Quick Impact Projects, and the Boundary Commission Trust Fund
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission visited Ethiopia and Eritrea from 21 to 25 February 2002 to support the peace process prior to the border delimitation decision by the Boundary Commission. The mission met with Prime Minister Meles Zenawi of Ethiopia and President Isaias Afwerki of Eritrea, both of whom reaffirmed that the Commission's decision is final and binding. The mission emphasized that security arrangements in the Temporary Security Zone must remain in place, demining must be accelerated, transfer of territory must occur orderly without unilateral action, and UNMEE's mandate should be renewed and adapted to support demarcation. The mission also highlighted confidence-building, humanitarian response, and regional cooperation as crucial elements for durable peace.

activities.activity_description: Received strategic update on the mission area situation and road ahead from SRSG Legwaila Joseph Legwaila and Force Commander Major General Patrick Cammaert in Addis Ababa.
Held meetings with P5 Ambassadors, EU Ambassadors, Peace Process Guarantors, Troop-Contributing Countries, and Friends of UNMEE in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Met with the Secretary-General of the Organization of African Unity (OAU), Amara Essy, in Addis Ababa.
Held high-level political meeting with Prime Minister Meles Zenawi of Ethiopia in Addis Ababa.
Met with UN Country Teams, World Bank, Economic Commission for Africa (ECA), and non-governmental organizations in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Held meetings with religious leaders of Ethiopia and Eritrea in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Visited the historic Axum ruins by road and helicopter.
Held a symbolic ceremonial crossing at the Mereb River Bridge linking Ethiopia and Eritrea, including addresses and a brief press conference.
Visited the Temporary Security Zone (TSZ), including an operational briefing at the Indian Battalion base at Camp Dunn in Senafe.
Toured Senafe, inspected the Mine Risk Education Project, and visited a camp holding approximately 5,000 internally displaced persons.
Held high-level political meeting with President Isaias Afwerki of Eritrea at the Den Den Club in Asmara.
Conducted a press conference via videoconferencing at UNMEE headquarters in Asmara.
