records.record_text: President Taylor said that his Government was not involved in the smuggling of diamonds and arms and that Governments accusing Liberia of this should come forward with the evidence... Members of the mission made clear to him... warned that the instability and isolation of Liberia could increase.
records.political_signal: The Security Council explicitly warned Liberia of international isolation if destabilizing actions continue.
records.policy_implication: International sanction mechanisms will be triggered if illegal trade and rebel support persist.

records.record_text: The humanitarian community in Sierra Leone voiced serious concern about the lack of access to the RUF-held areas, which was depriving many Sierra Leoneans of vital support.
records.political_signal: RUF territorial blockades are causing severe humanitarian distress.
records.policy_implication: Humanitarian corridor agreements must be secured as a priority in any negotiations with RUF.

records.record_text: Several of the mission’s interlocutors, in particular non-governmental organizations and civil society, stressed the negative impact of the establishment and jurisdiction of the Court on the minds of ex-combatants who could be more reluctant to come forward to disarm for fear of prosecution.
records.political_signal: Misunderstandings regarding Special Court prosecutions risk deterring rebel combatants from disarming.
records.policy_implication: Clear messaging and explicit legal boundaries focusing on key leaders are needed to preserve DDR participation.

records.record_text: Our first recommendation, therefore, is for the establishment of a United Nations-based mechanism for overall coordination.
records.political_signal: Uncoordinated international and regional initiatives are undermining overall peace efforts.
records.policy_implication: Establish a formal UN-led mechanism to harmonize UN, ECOWAS, and Government strategies.

records.record_text: The Special Representative of the Secretary-General might wish to give high and immediate priority to the coordination of active contacts, liaising in particular, beyond UNAMSIL itself, with Presidents Kabbah, Conté, Konaré, Obasanjo and Taylor.
records.political_signal: Regional political dialogue must be led directly by the SRSG.
records.policy_implication: The SRSG's diplomatic mandate should prioritize continuous multi-head-of-state engagement.

records.record_text: The process should, inter alia, cover an early ceasefire throughout the territory of Sierra Leone, agreed arrangements for withdrawal, the return of all seized UNAMSIL weapons and equipment, and the opening up of humanitarian and other access in the north and east of the country.
records.political_signal: Ceasefire and weapon returns are non-negotiable preconditions for RUF political integration.
records.policy_implication: Negotiation frameworks must explicitly link dialogue to territorial access and equipment recovery.

records.record_text: UNAMSIL must be strengthened in terms of numbers, effectiveness and capability, as recommended by the Secretary-General (see S/2000/832), taking advantage of the offers of further troops from, inter alia, ECOWAS countries.
records.political_signal: A robust military footprint is essential to maintain pressure on armed groups.
records.policy_implication: Approve force expansion and integrate ECOWAS troop offers with necessary logistical support.

records.record_text: the Security Council and individual Governments should look positively at what they can do to support the decision by ECOWAS to prepare for and deploy an ECOWAS observer force on the borders of the three Mano River Union member countries, in coordination with UNAMSIL. The Government of Guinea in particular needs encouragement and support to provide access and protection for humanitarian personnel and aid.
records.political_signal: Border stability in the Mano River Union requires direct international backing for ECOWAS observers.
records.policy_implication: Provide financial and logistical resources to operationalize border monitoring.

records.record_text: The Security Council should give early consideration to whether the balance of responsibilities in the programme among the Government, the World Bank, UNAMSIL and bilateral agencies can be improved, following the publication of the report of the assessment team sponsored by the World Bank.
records.political_signal: Institutional responsibilities for DDR are improperly balanced and require realignment.
records.policy_implication: Adjust institutional mandates to enhance UNAMSIL's role in supporting DDR execution.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that UNAMSIL and ECOWAS explore with RUF the possibility of access under conditions of adequate security for a needs assessment to be conducted in the areas under its control, and for safe access for the delivery of humanitarian assistance thereafter.
records.political_signal: Humanitarian relief access to rebel-held areas must be negotiated immediately.
records.policy_implication: UNAMSIL and ECOWAS should initiate humanitarian access negotiations with RUF command.

records.record_text: As a key first step, the mission recommends an immediate package of international assistance to help the ECOWAS secretariat to develop its capacity, including the placing of UNAMSIL liaison staff at ECOWAS headquarters.
records.political_signal: ECOWAS capacity deficits hinder regional peacekeeping execution and require institutional reinforcement.
records.policy_implication: Fund institutional capacity packages for ECOWAS and embed UNAMSIL liaison personnel in Abuja.

mission_title: Security Council special mission visit to Eritrea and Ethiopia, 9 and 10 May 2000

main_risks: Imminent resumption of full-scale warfare between Ethiopia and Eritrea
Severe aggravation of humanitarian famine due to diversion of transport resources to war
Continued military mobilization along the border
main_commitments: Both leaders expressed willingness to resume proximity talks without preconditions under OAU auspices
Draft resolution mechanism proposing Secretary-General reporting within 30 days
main_policy_signals: Differences over territorial issues do not warrant a return to armed conflict
Full Security Council backing for the OAU peace process and framework agreements
Demand for immediate cessation of force and return to positions held prior to 6 May 1998
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The UN Security Council special mission carried out rapid shuttle diplomacy between Addis Ababa and Asmara to avert a renewed outbreak of war between Ethiopia and Eritrea. Although both governments reaffirmed their acceptance of the OAU Framework Agreement and agreed in principle to resume proximity talks without preconditions, the mission recorded extreme concern and a pessimistic outlook regarding the likelihood of preventing imminent military hostilities.

activities.activity_description: Met with Prime Minister Meles Zenawi in Addis Ababa on the evening of 8 May 2000 to receive Ethiopia's position on the suspension of proximity talks in Algiers and the OAU settlement framework.
Held a breakfast meeting on 9 May 2000 with representatives of the OAU and the chargé d'affaires of Algeria in Addis Ababa.
Travelled to Asmara on 9 May 2000 and met with President Isaias Afwerki to hear Eritrea's views on the situation and OAU documents.
Returned to Addis Ababa on the evening of 9 May 2000 for a second meeting with Prime Minister Meles Zenawi to clarify Ethiopia's position.
Met late night on 9 May 2000 with OAU Assistant Secretary-General Saïd Djinnit and OAU officials in Addis Ababa to discuss document text interpretations.
Travelled to Asmara on 10 May 2000 to seek President Isaias Afwerki's views on a draft Security Council resolution text.
Conveyed the draft Security Council text to Prime Minister Meles Zenawi in Addis Ababa on 10 May 2000 for his views.

actors_met.actor_name: Meles Zenawi (Prime Minister of Ethiopia)
Isaias Afwerki (President of Eritrea)
Chargé d'affaires of the Government of Algeria in Addis Ababa
Saïd Djinnit (Assistant Secretary-General of OAU) and OAU officials
Representatives of the Organization of African Unity (OAU)
Resident Coordinators of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and staff
Captain Khaled Bassiouny and AMC Aviation crew

records.record_text: Prime Minister Meles set out at length his Government’s position with regard to the suspension of the proximity talks at Algiers, as well as providing a detailed account of the situation between Ethiopia and Eritrea.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia maintained a firm stance on the terms required to resolve remaining points of contention in the OAU Framework Agreement and Technical Arrangements.
records.policy_implication: Highlighting unresolved procedural and technical details that caused the stall in Algiers proximity talks.

records.record_text: President Afwerki in turn explained to the mission the views of his Government of the current situation and its position on the documents in question.
records.political_signal: Eritrea outlined its specific interpretation and conditions regarding the OAU texts and implementation modalities.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrated the divergent positions between the two belligerents on technical implementation details.

records.record_text: Secretary-General Djinnit stressed that only the French text of the documents concerned was authentic. This raised a possible difference in meaning concerning the phrase 'consolidated technical arrangements', which in English is preceded in most instances by the word 'the', but in French by the word 'des'.
records.political_signal: Authentic French language drafting created semantic discrepancies that contributed to mutual suspicion between the parties.
records.policy_implication: Precise textual translation and legal clarity are required to prevent diplomatic impasses over technical arrangements.

records.record_text: The differences between the two sides, while real, are clearly, in the view of the mission, relatively small and manageable and could be resolved by intensive negotiations over time.
records.political_signal: The remaining substance of the dispute does not justify military conflict and can be resolved diplomatically.
records.policy_implication: Sustained political pressure should be maintained to force parties back into negotiations.

records.record_text: Nevertheless, the two sides are on the verge of resuming a senseless war over these differences. The war, which could resume at any time, would not only cause enormous numbers of casualties on both sides, but would greatly add to deaths from famine, as the war would divert much-needed transportation from famine relief.
records.political_signal: Urgent international action is required to prevent immediate war and disastrous compound humanitarian effects.
records.policy_implication: Conflict resumption threatens catastrophic civilian casualties and severe exacerbation of regional famine.

records.record_text: Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of stringing out negotiations to avoid redressing its offensive of May 1998; Eritrea accuses Ethiopia of actively holding to the option of resuming the conflict while negotiations continue.
records.actor_source: Government of Ethiopia / Government of Eritrea
records.actor_target: Government of Eritrea / Government of Ethiopia
records.political_signal: Deep distrust and mutual accusations of bad faith prevent direct progress without external diplomatic bridging mechanisms.
records.policy_implication: An independent bridging mechanism is necessary to re-engage the parties without triggering bilateral narrative blockages.

records.record_text: The members of the mission made it repeatedly clear that they would not enter into the substance of the OAU texts, nor substitute for the OAU process, but that the two leaders had to understand that, as seen from the outside, the differences between them on the territorial issue in itself did not warrant a return to fighting.
records.actor_target: Meles Zenawi (Prime Minister of Ethiopia) / Isaias Afwerki (President of Eritrea)
records.political_signal: The UN Security Council fully backs the OAU as the primary mediator and strongly condemns any return to force over minor territorial details.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces OAU primacy while leveraging Security Council authority to deter military escalation.

records.record_text: At the time of the finalization of the present report, the special mission did not know whether the Security Council would adopt a resolution, whether the parties would both decide to resume early discussions or whether renewed conflict can be avoided. The members of the mission tended to a pessimistic view on the last point.
records.political_signal: Diplomatic efforts are struggling against imminent military escalation.
records.policy_implication: The Security Council must prepare for potential mandatory sanctions or robust peacekeeping interventions if conflict erupts.

records.record_text: The draft resolution urges the earliest possible reconvening, without preconditions, of proximity talks involving substantive discussions on the basis of the Framework Agreement and Modalities for its Implementation.
records.actor_target: Government of Ethiopia / Government of Eritrea
records.political_signal: Immediate resumption of talks without preconditions is the only acceptable course of action for the UN Security Council.
records.policy_implication: Establishes a UN Security Council endorsed mandate for OAU proximity talks.

records.record_text: The draft resolution welcomes the statements of both leaders, made directly to the Security Council special mission, that they will resume proximity talks without preconditions.
records.actor_source: Meles Zenawi (Prime Minister of Ethiopia) / Isaias Afwerki (President of Eritrea)
records.political_signal: Locks both leaders into publicly stated verbal commitments made directly to ambassadors representing the UN Security Council.
records.policy_implication: Holds parties accountable to international commitments to return to negotiations.

records.record_text: The draft resolution insists that both parties implement their commitment to refrain from the use of force, as is consistent with their acceptance of the provisions of the OAU Framework Agreement and Modalities for its Implementation and with the principles of the Charter of the United Nations.
records.actor_target: Government of Ethiopia / Government of Eritrea
records.political_signal: Any resort to force will be viewed as a breach of UN Charter principles and OAU commitments.
records.policy_implication: Lays legal and political groundwork for Security Council measures under Chapter VII if military violence resumes.

records.record_text: The draft resolution also insists that both parties implement their commitment to return to positions held prior to 6 May 1998, consistent with the sequence laid out in the Modalities for Implementation accepted by both parties.
records.actor_target: Government of Ethiopia / Government of Eritrea
records.political_signal: Reversion to status quo ante 6 May 1998 remains a non-negotiable principle for territorial dispute settlement.
records.policy_implication: Mandates specific geographical troop redeployments as prerequisite for border demarcation.

mission_title: Security Council mission visit to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 4-8 May 2000

main_risks: Escalation of heavy fighting between Ugandan and Rwandan forces in Kisangani causing high civilian casualties
Unravelling of the fragile ceasefire without immediate MONUC Phase II deployment
Lack of agreement and accurate data regarding the scale and process for DDRR of armed groups like ex-FAR and Interahamwe
Persistent disagreement among Congolese parties over the venue for the inter-Congolese dialogue and lack of funding for the neutral facilitator
Illegal exploitation of DRC natural resources by external armed forces continuing to fuel the conflict
main_commitments: Signing of the Status-of-Forces Agreement (SOFA) between the UN and the DRC Government in Kinshasa
Joint declaration by the Governments of Rwanda and Uganda on 8 May 2000 to withdraw forces from Kisangani and demilitarize the city under MONUC supervision
Agreement to invite the Political Committee established by the Lusaka Agreement to meet in New York in June 2000
Commitment by belligerents to engage with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to facilitate an exchange of prisoners of war
main_policy_signals: Peace in the DRC requires simultaneous progress on both the military track (ceasefire/MONUC) and the political track (inter-Congolese dialogue)
Shadows cast by the Sierra Leone peacekeeping crisis must not cloud the international community's responsibility or commitment to the DRC
Belligerent parties must provide firm, written undertakings supporting MONUC Phase II deployment and security before full deployment occurs
An expert panel should be established by the Security Council to investigate the illegal exploitation of natural resources in the DRC
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to the DRC and the region (4-8 May 2000) sought to reinvigorate the Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement and lay the groundwork for MONUC Phase II deployment. Amid serious flare-ups of fighting between Rwandan and Ugandan armies in Kisangani, the mission successfully facilitated a joint agreement between Rwanda and Uganda to demilitarize Kisangani and witnessed the signing of the MONUC Status-of-Forces Agreement with President Kabila. While regional leaders overwhelmingly demanded rapid MONUC deployment, the mission emphasized that peacekeeping success depends on strict adherence to the ceasefire, clear political reconciliation through the inter-Congolese dialogue, effective DDRR mechanisms, and addressing illegal resource exploitation.

activities.activity_description: Call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Belgium in Brussels on 3 May 2000.
Meeting with President Laurent-Désiré Kabila in Kinshasa on 4 May 2000.
Witnessing the official signing of the Status-of-Forces Agreement (SOFA) between MONUC and the DRC Government at the Presidential Palace in Kinshasa on 4 May 2000.
Luncheon meeting with heads of United Nations agencies operating in Kinshasa on 4 May 2000.
Meeting with Congolese civil society, religious leaders, and political parties in Kinshasa on 5 May 2000.
Field visit by three mission members (Namibia, Netherlands, UK) to Kananga, a proposed MONUC battalion deployment site, meeting with local officials, UNICEF, and military observers on 5 May 2000.
Meeting with the Joint Military Commission (JMC) in Lusaka on 5 May 2000.
Meeting with President Frederick J. T. Chiluba in Lusaka on 6 May 2000.
Meeting with the Political Committee established by the Lusaka Agreement in Lusaka on 6 May 2000.
Meeting with President Robert G. Mugabe in Harare on 6 May 2000.
Meeting with President Paul Kagame in Kigali on 7 May 2000.
Meeting with representatives of the Congolese Rally for Democracy-Goma (RCD-Goma) in Kigali on 7 May 2000.
Meeting with President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni outside Kampala on 8 May 2000.
Meeting with Professor Ernest Wamba dia Wamba and delegation of RCD-Kisangani at Entebbe airport on 8 May 2000.

actors_met.actor_name: Minister for Foreign Affairs of Belgium
President Laurent-Désiré Kabila (DRC)
Yerodia Abdoulaye Ndombasi, Minister for Foreign Affairs (DRC)
Kamel Morjane, Special Representative of the Secretary-General
Heads of UN Agencies in Kinshasa
Congolese Civil Society Representatives
Congolese Religious Leaders
Representatives of Congolese Political Parties
Claudel André Lubaya, Governor of Kasaï Occidentale Province
General T. J. Kazembe, Acting Chairman, Joint Military Commission
President Frederick J. T. Chiluba (Zambia)
Amama Mbabazi, Chairman of the Political Committee / Minister of State of Uganda
President Robert G. Mugabe (Zimbabwe)
President Paul Kagame (Rwanda)
Emile Ilunga and representatives of RCD-Goma
President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni (Uganda)
Professor Ernest Wamba dia Wamba and delegation of RCD-Kisangani
Major General Mountaga Diallo, MONUC Force Commander

records.record_text: As and if the Secretary-General, in accordance with paragraph 5 of resolution 1291 (2000), determined that the conditions for deployment existed, the full support and cooperation of the Government would be needed.
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Deployment of Phase II depends on government cooperation and meeting statutory conditions.
records.policy_implication: Deployment readiness requires firm government commitments on access and security.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission urged the President to agree to an exchange of prisoners of war, to be facilitated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
records.political_signal: Exchanging prisoners of war is an essential confidence-building measure under the Lusaka process.
records.policy_implication: ICRC operational facilitation required for POW release.

records.record_text: President Kabila, expressing concern over the fragility of the ceasefire, called for the speedy deployment of the second phase of MONUC. His Government would interpose no obstacle to that deployment.
records.political_signal: DRC Government publicly commits to unhindered Phase II MONUC deployment.
records.policy_implication: Removes official DRC executive objection to peacekeeping deployment.

records.record_text: President Kabila criticized the international community for failing to condemn the presence of uninvited foreign troops in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and accused Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of paying for weapons with diamonds taken from his country.
records.political_signal: DRC treats foreign troop presence as illegal exploitation and aggression.
records.policy_implication: UN Council requested to address illegal exploitation of resources directly.

records.record_text: Immediately following their meeting with President Kabila, the members of the mission witnessed the signing of the status-of-forces agreement by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Ambassador Kamel Morjane, and the Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Yerodia Abdoulaye Ndombasi.
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Formal legal framework established for MONUC presence in DRC.
records.policy_implication: Provides legal basis for operational movement and administrative procedures.

records.record_text: Ambassador Holbrooke said he was deeply disturbed that no steps had been taken to alert MONUC military personnel to the dangers of AIDS despite the undeniable involvement of United Nations peacekeeping troops in the spread of AIDS. He said that a plan must be prepared immediately...
records.political_signal: Peacekeeping operations must actively prevent HIV/AIDS transmission.
records.policy_implication: DPKO and troop contributors must formulate mandatory HIV awareness protocols.

records.record_text: The main points of view that emerged from these discussions with the Congolese participants included their insistence on a democratic political structure for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, without privilege for those who had resorted to armed force...
records.political_signal: Unarmed political actors and civil society reject political privilege for armed insurgencies.
records.policy_implication: Inter-Congolese dialogue must include inclusive, non-armed representation.

records.record_text: Ambassador Levitte said that it was the right and duty of the United Nations to intervene to help stop the fighting in Kisangani, not least because it had caused the deaths of a number of Congolese civilians.
records.political_signal: UN asserts moral and mandate authority to intervene to stop civilian loss of life.
records.policy_implication: MONUC deployment prioritized to Kisangani to halt allied inter-state clashes.

records.record_text: President Chiluba stated that in addition to the implementation of the disengagement plan of 8 April, two things were required: the full and immediate deployment of phase II of MONUC... and the success of the inter-Congolese dialogue.
records.political_signal: Regional mediator emphasizes urgency of MONUC deployment to prevent security vacuum.
records.policy_implication: Immediate funding and deployment essential for sustaining Lusaka framework.

records.record_text: In a discussion of the process of disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and resettlement, it emerged that there was little agreement on the scale of the problem. A rough provisional figure of some 15,000 members of armed groups existed, but the members of the groups were very hard to identify...
records.political_signal: DDRR is critical yet severely under-planned and contentious.
records.policy_implication: Detailed data collection and planning mechanisms needed immediately for eastern DRC armed groups.

records.record_text: In President Mugabe's opinion, the political dialogue was at this juncture less important than MONUC deployment, since the conflict remained uppermost in people's minds and the rebel groups were essentially the creation of Uganda and Rwanda.
records.political_signal: Zimbabwe prioritizes foreign troop withdrawal/MONUC over inter-Congolese dialogue.
records.policy_implication: Highlights divergence among regional leaders on political vs military sequencing.

records.record_text: President Kagame proposed that both Rwandan and Ugandan forces should withdraw from the city under United Nations supervision, and that MONUC should at once deploy there in accordance with the concept of operations approved by the Security Council.
records.political_signal: Rwanda accepts UN-supervised demilitarization of Kisangani.
records.policy_implication: Requires urgent MONUC observer deployment to create a demilitarized zone.

records.record_text: In the statement, the Government of Uganda and the Government of Rwanda stated that they were ready to withdraw their forces currently deployed in and around Kisangani to a distance to be agreed between them in detailed negotiations to be held without delay under the auspices of MONUC/the Joint Military Commission.
records.political_signal: Bilateral commitment to cease hostilities and demilitarize Kisangani.
records.policy_implication: MONUC/JMC must establish technical disengagement mechanisms immediately.

records.record_text: While concurring with the idea, RCD-Goma objected to the proposal that MONUC should fly directly from Kinshasa to Kisangani without transiting through Goma. The Security Council mission categorically rejected the conditions posed by RCD-Goma...
records.political_signal: UN rejects insurgent group attempts to impose transit control on peacekeeping flights.
records.policy_implication: Flight notification protocols established under SOFA apply across all DRC airspace.

records.record_text: Ambassador van Walsum raised the Mwenga incident, in which 15 women were reportedly buried alive... Ambassador van Walsum, supported by the entire delegation, firmly declared this response to be unacceptable. Members of the delegation stated that they would continue to pursue this issue...
records.actor_source: Ambassador A. Peter van Walsum / Security Council Mission
records.political_signal: UN Council will hold armed groups accountable for grave human rights atrocities.
records.policy_implication: Requires formal UN human rights investigation into the Mwenga killings.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission accepted that the disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and resettlement of the armed groups, including the ex-Rwandan Armed Forces and Interahamwe militia, was an essential element in restoring confidence in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: DDRR of non-signatory armed groups is indispensable for long-term regional stability.
records.policy_implication: Substantial peacekeeping resources beyond Phase II needed for future DDRR execution.

records.record_text: Sierra Leone should not be allowed to cloud the international community's responsibility in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and its capacity to make a real difference there.
records.geographic_scope: Democratic Republic of the Congo / Global
records.political_signal: UN engagement in DRC must be evaluated on its own merits despite setbacks in West Africa.
records.policy_implication: Prevents political retreat from African peacekeeping mandates.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Secretary-General, before he makes his final decision, should speak to each of the Lusaka parties at the highest level, seeking their unequivocal commitment to assist the proposed deployment of phase II of MONUC, testing their commitment to the maintenance of the ceasefire and asking for their firm undertaking, in writing...
records.geographic_scope: Democratic Republic of the Congo / Regional
records.political_signal: Written guarantees from state and non-state leaders required prior to deploying Phase II forces.
records.policy_implication: Mitigates operational risks to UN peacekeeping personnel.

records.record_text: The mission recommends the early establishment of an expert panel by the Security Council to take this matter forward [illegal exploitation of resources].
records.political_signal: Security Council will formally investigate illegal natural resource exploitation financing the war.
records.policy_implication: Mandates creation of the Panel of Experts on Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that an interim solution, possibly Kisangani, could be explored [for the inter-Congolese dialogue venue] and that Kinshasa could be re-examined at a later date, when confidence between the parties has grown.
records.actor_target: Sir Ketumile Masire / Facilitation Team / Political Committee
records.political_signal: A neutral interim venue within DRC should overcome political impasse over national dialogue.
records.policy_implication: Facilitator encouraged to propose Kisangani following demilitarization.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council Mission on the implementation of Security Council resolution 1244 (1999)

main_risks: Persistent inter-ethnic violence, lack of security, and restricted freedom of movement for non-Albanian minorities.
Non-participation of the Kosovo Serb community in civil registration and upcoming municipal elections.
Uncontrolled and unmanaged returns of displaced persons destabilizing fragile local security conditions.
Severe resource, personnel, and equipment shortages for UNMIK Police, the judicial/penal system, and ICTY forensic investigations.
main_commitments: Report local and stakeholder support for the appointment of a special envoy for missing persons and detainees to the Security Council.
Pursue personnel constraints and civil service wage imbalances through the appropriate General Assembly processes.
Continue working towards establishing a Joint Committee to enhance productive dialogue with Federal Republic of Yugoslavia authorities.
main_policy_signals: Unconditional rejection of violence and intolerance by all ethnic communities is required to enable peaceful coexistence.
Full and effective implementation of Security Council resolution 1244 (1999) remains a high priority for the Security Council.
Sustained international political, financial, and material support is vital for UNMIK and KFOR to fulfill their mandates.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Kosovo (27–29 April 2000) evaluated the status of resolution 1244 (1999) implementation across key sectors including civil administration, security, rule of law, civil registration, and refugee returns. While recognizing significant progress made by UNMIK and KFOR under challenging circumstances, the mission highlighted deep-seated inter-ethnic divisions, ongoing security risks for minorities, and severe resource deficits in policing and justice. The mission engaged a broad range of local political and community actors, minority groups, FRY officials, and international presences, emphasizing reconciliation, law and order, and non-violent political participation.

activities.activity_description: Comprehensive briefing by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General (Bernard Kouchner) and heads of UNMIK's four pillars (UNHCR, UN, OSCE, EU) in Pristina.
Meeting with representatives of Bosniac, Roma, and Turkish communities at Prizren to discuss cultural rights and administrative representation.
Meeting with members of the Kosovo Transitional Council to hear perspectives from Kosovo Albanian and Serb representatives.
Field visit to the Kosovo Police School at Vucitrn to review police recruitment, screening, and multi-ethnic training procedures.
Visit to Mitrovica, including the Confidence Area, Employment Rehabilitation Project, and a meeting with Kosovo Serb and Kosovo Albanian leaders.
Meeting with Bishop Artemije and members of the Serb National Council at Gracanica regarding security, resolution 1244 implementation, and missing persons.
Meeting with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Committee for Cooperation with UNMIK regarding sovereignty and mandate implementation.
Briefing at KFOR Headquarters by KFOR Commander General Ortuño on the security situation, Military Technical Agreement, and arms embargo monitoring.
Visit to Gnjilane region, observing the civil registration process at Dobrecani and visiting the orthodox church of Saint Nicolas.
Briefing by the UNMIK Police Commissioner on law and order, executive policing challenges, and resource requirements.
Briefings by co-heads of the Administrative Department of Justice, head of Correctional System, and head of the International Support Section for the Kosovo War and Ethnic War Crimes Court.
Meeting with heads of departments of the Joint Interim Administrative Structures (Health, Sports, Agriculture, Governance, Central Fiscal Authority).
Visit to Djakovica, observing ICTY exhumation activities at Brekoc cemetery and meeting families of missing and detained persons.
Joint press conference in Pristina held by the Head of Mission (Ambassador Chowdhury) and SRSG Kouchner.

actors_met.actor_name: Special Representative of the Secretary-General (Bernard Kouchner) and UNMIK Leadership
Heads of UNMIK Four Pillars (UNHCR, UN, OSCE, European Union)
Bosniac, Roma, and Turkish Community Representatives (Prizren)
Kosovo Transitional Council Members
Kosovo Police School Leadership and Trainees
Mitrovica Community Leaders (Kosovo Serb and Kosovo Albanian)
Bishop Artemije and Serb National Council (Gracanica)
Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Committee for Cooperation with UNMIK
KFOR Commander (General Ortuño)
UNMIK Police Commissioner
Administrative Department of Justice and War Crimes Court Representatives
Heads of Departments of Joint Interim Administrative Structures
International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia (ICTY) Forensic Experts
Families of Missing and Detained Persons (Djakovica)

records.record_text: UNMIK is currently concentrating on the development of the interim political framework and on economic revitalization, including strong and sustainable macroeconomic policies for Kosovo.
records.policy_implication: Focusing on political and economic frameworks helps stabilize interim administrative authority.

records.record_text: Both UNMIK and KFOR emphasized that uncontrolled and massive returns could actually destabilize the security situation and seriously aggravate inter-ethnic tensions, not least due to competition for scarce housing and other resources.
records.policy_implication: Refugee and IDP returns must be regulated, gradual, and supported by enhanced physical and social infrastructure.

records.record_text: Representatives of the ethnic communities [Bosniac, Roma, Turkish] expressed their concern about their cultural rights and inadequate representation in the local administration, health, education and other sectors of public life.
records.policy_implication: UNMIK administrative structures must prioritize inclusive representation and protect minority linguistic and cultural rights.

records.record_text: Some Kosovo Albanian representatives urged the Security Council to adopt a resolution demanding the release of all Kosovo Albanian detainees and prisoners in Serbia.
records.political_signal: Demands international political action against Yugoslav authorities regarding detainees.
records.policy_implication: Unresolved detainee issues hamper inter-community reconciliation efforts.

records.record_text: Serb representatives emphasized the need for the full implementation of Security Council resolution 1244 (1999) and for the return of all internally displaced persons, and expressed their concern about the lack of security for Serbs in Kosovo.
records.policy_implication: Serb engagement hinges on concrete security guarantees and return mechanisms under Resolution 1244.

records.record_text: Leaders of both ethnic communities [in Mitrovica] are again in direct contact with one another, and have expressed the intention to cooperate with the international presences.
records.policy_implication: Local-level dialogue can serve as a catalyst for broader confidence-building and reduced violence.

records.record_text: Representatives of the Serb National Council at Gracanica insisted that the Serbs will not be in a position to participate in the registration process until adequate security conditions are established and the process of the return of Serb internally displaced persons has begun.
records.political_signal: Boycott of democratic civil registration process unless core security and return demands are met.
records.policy_implication: Risk of political boycott threatens the legitimacy of planned municipal elections.

records.record_text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia representative expressed concern that some of UNMIK's and KFOR's actions could undermine the sovereignty of the FRY.
records.political_signal: Asserts FRY sovereign rights over Kosovo against perceived UNMIK administrative overreach.
records.policy_implication: Requires UNMIK to maintain delicate political balancing in defining administrative actions.

records.record_text: The UNMIK mission faces the unprecedented dual challenge of simultaneously running operations of UNMIK police while building a new local police service from the ground up.
records.policy_implication: Executive policing and capacity-building require distinct operational resources and clear mandate support.

records.record_text: Significant impediments have also been presented by the slow provision of basic equipment and resources necessary to carry out executive policing functions.
records.policy_implication: Member States must accelerate logistics and resource delivery to maintain law enforcement credibility.

records.record_text: The Mission was informed by the Tribunal's forensic experts that they are hampered in their work by the lack of resources to finance DNA tests.
records.policy_implication: Funding shortfalls for forensic identification directly delay missing persons closures and transitional justice.

records.record_text: KFOR's continued assistance in protecting minorities and joint security operations with UNMIK police thus remain vital.
records.political_signal: Underlines mandatory ongoing military-civil security coordination to protect vulnerable minorities.
records.policy_implication: KFOR must maintain operational posture focused on minority protection.

records.record_text: The Mission noted the strong support of the different ethnic communities for the appointment of a special envoy for detainees and missing persons. Given its urgency, the Mission undertook to report that support to the Council.
records.political_signal: Signals potential creation of a dedicated high-level diplomatic post for missing persons.
records.policy_implication: The Security Council will consider formalizing a dedicated mandate/envoy for missing persons.

records.record_text: The Mission notes that UNMIK's intention to recruit international judges and prosecutors and their staff to work alongside their local counterparts will be critical to redress the perceived culture of impunity which currently undermines the judicial system.
records.policy_implication: Deploying international judicial personnel is essential to counter ethnic bias and reinforce law enforcement.

records.record_text: While noting the serious staffing constraints faced by UNMIK in civil administration and police, the Mission recognizes the significant imbalance in wages between its locally recruited civil service staff and the rest of the Kosovo population... It feels that both issues should be pursued through the appropriate General Assembly process.
records.policy_implication: Requires budgetary and administrative review in Fifth Committee to address local civil service distortions.

records.record_text: It is unfortunate, however, that all factions of the Kosovo Serb community have chosen not to participate in this process, due to the current lack of physical security and freedom of movement.
records.policy_implication: Electoral credibility will be impaired unless security conditions allow full Serb registration.

records.record_text: Property issues, however, remain unresolved, and could potentially undermine international efforts aimed at the economic recovery of Kosovo and even peace initiatives by UNMIK.
records.policy_implication: Establishing robust property dispute resolution frameworks is critical to avoid persistent conflict and economic stagnation.

records.record_text: The Mission feels that detailed information on KFOR's activities in the implementation of Security Council resolution 1160 (1998) should be provided to the Committee established pursuant to resolution 1160 (1998).
records.political_signal: Reaffirms Security Council oversight over sanctions and arms embargo enforcement.
records.policy_implication: KFOR must report monthly arms embargo findings directly to the Security Council Sanctions Committee.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council Mission to Jakarta and Dili, 8 to 12 September 1999

main_risks: Escalating violence, destruction, and systematic scorched-earth policy in East Timor by pro-autonomy militias backed by TNI and police
Severe humanitarian crisis involving forced relocation of tens of thousands of East Timorese to West Timor and imminent starvation among IDPs in the hills
Targeted executions of students, intellectuals, pro-independence activists, and clergy
Impaired operational capability and severe security threats facing UNAMET and international relief organizations
main_commitments: President Habibie announced Indonesia's readiness to unconditionally accept international peacekeeping forces through the United Nations to restore peace and security in East Timor
Indonesian Government agreed to allow the evacuation of IDPs in the UNAMET compound to Australia, facilitate air drops of humanitarian aid, and ensure Falintil would not come under militia attack
main_policy_signals: The result of the direct ballot reflecting the East Timorese population's clear choice for independence must be respected
Indonesian authorities must fulfill their obligations under the 5 May Agreement and facilitate an international peacekeeping presence and humanitarian access without hindrance
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council Mission to Jakarta and Dili was dispatched at a critical juncture following the post-ballot outbreak of widespread violence in East Timor. Through direct engagement with top Indonesian government officials, military leaders, political actors, local civil society, UN staff, and a site visit to Dili, the Mission established clear evidence of complicity by elements of the Indonesian military and police in militia-led violence and forced displacement. The Mission successfully pressed the Indonesian Government to acknowledge the limits of its domestic security measures and agree to the unconditional deployment of an international peacekeeping force through the United Nations.

activities.activity_description: Briefing by United Nations and UNAMET staff in Jakarta regarding the security and humanitarian deterioration in East Timor.
Meeting with Foreign Minister Ali Alatas to convey Security Council concerns and discuss humanitarian and security arrangements.
Meetings with the Jakarta diplomatic corps on 8 and 10 September to assess political and security perspectives.
Meeting with Madam Megawati Soekarnoputri regarding political support for an international security presence.
Meetings with Mr. Xanana Gusmao on 9 and 12 September regarding the security situation, Falintil stance, and political communications.
Meeting with President B.J. Habibie to press for international assistance and UNAMET protection.
Meeting with Defence Minister General Wiranto and the General Staff to review security assessments, martial law, and military conduct.
Meeting with Indonesian NGO representatives who presented a joint statement calling for UN peacekeeping and stopping violence.
Visit to Dili on 11 September, including meetings with local military commanders, touring the destroyed town, inspecting the UNAMET compound, and meeting with Bishop Nasciemento.
Follow-up meeting with President Habibie following his public announcement accepting international peacekeeping forces.

actors_met.actor_name: United Nations and UNAMET Staff
Ali Alatas, Foreign Minister of Indonesia
Jakarta Diplomatic Corps
Megawati Soekarnoputri
Xanana Gusmao
B.J. Habibie, President of Indonesia
General Wiranto, Defence Minister of Indonesia, and General Staff
Indonesian NGO Representatives
Local Military Commanders in Dili
Bishop Nasciemento

records.record_text: The Security Council Mission dispatched to Jakarta and Dili from 8 to 12 September 1999 was entrusted with the task of discussing with the Government of Indonesia concrete steps for the peaceful implementation of the 5 May Agreement (S/1999/513).
records.political_signal: The UN Security Council expects full implementation of agreed mechanisms.
records.policy_implication: Mission framework defined by prior trilateral agreements.

records.record_text: The people of East Timor had made a clear choice in favour of independence, that their will must be respected and that the international community looked forward to working with the Government of Indonesia in bringing East Timor to independence.
records.political_signal: The popular consultation result is definitive and non-negotiable.
records.policy_implication: Transition to independence must be supported internationally.

records.record_text: Staff described unequivocally the deterioration in the security and humanitarian situation in East Timor since the announcement of the result of the ballot, leaving the Mission in no doubt that large elements in the military and police authorities had been complicit in organizing and supporting the action of the militias.
records.political_signal: Indonesian security forces directly implicated in militia violence.
records.policy_implication: Indonesian state authority alone cannot guarantee security.

records.record_text: Foreign Minister Alatas insisted that while the Government would welcome any assistance in providing humanitarian relief, it would not contemplate any foreign military presence in East Timor before the Indonesian Parliament met and addressed the outcome of the popular consultation.
records.actor_source: Ali Alatas, Foreign Minister of Indonesia
records.political_signal: Initial rejection of foreign military deployment based on constitutional sequence.
records.policy_implication: Delay in foreign military deployment risks further violence.

records.record_text: A number of ambassadors firmly underscored the complicity by the Indonesian military and police in the actions of the militia and expressed concerns that the Government no longer had control over the military with respect to East Timor.
records.political_signal: Diplomatic consensus that civilian government lacks command over local military forces.
records.policy_implication: Intervention required beyond domestic command structures.

records.record_text: Mr. Gusmao stated categorically that East Timor was suffering what amounted to a campaign by the military to exterminate East Timorese and lay waste to its cities, reporting that 12 battalions of TNI had entered from West Timor.
records.political_signal: Call for immediate international intervention to prevent genocide/destruction.
records.policy_implication: Falintil self-defence stance risks armed confrontation if TNI advances.

records.record_text: General Wiranto expressed full confidence that martial law would allow his forces to stabilize the situation and stated that pro-integration anger at UNAMET was so high that United Nations troops would only cause the situation to deteriorate further.
records.actor_source: General Wiranto, Defence Minister of Indonesia
records.political_signal: Military resistance to external peacekeeping deployment.
records.policy_implication: Martial law framing disproved by ongoing violence during mission visit.

records.record_text: Indonesian NGO representatives presented a joint statement calling for immediate Security Council meetings to decide on the dispatch of a peacekeeping force, concrete steps by the Government to stop violence, and the lifting of martial law.
records.actor_target: UN Security Council / Government of Indonesia
records.political_signal: Domestic civil society support for UN peacekeeping intervention.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates internal pressure on Government of Indonesia.

records.record_text: President Habibie announced to the press that Indonesia was ready to unconditionally accept international peacekeeping forces through the United Nations from friendly nations to restore peace and security in East Timor.
records.political_signal: Major policy shift accepting UN international peacekeeping force.
records.policy_implication: Paves the way for Security Council resolution authorizing INTERFET.

records.record_text: The organized and coordinated nature of the campaign, the Territory-wide effort to force out UNAMET and other international presences, and the lack of adequate response to militia violence despite military superiority support the view that militia activities were organized and supported by parts of TNI.
records.political_signal: Formal determination of state responsibility in militia terror.
records.policy_implication: Indonesian military cannot be relied upon as sole security provider.

records.record_text: Martial law, implemented on 7 September, had not succeeded in stabilizing the situation and had been unable to respond adequately to the humanitarian crisis in East Timor.
records.political_signal: Domestic emergency powers failed to halt violence.
records.policy_implication: Necessitates international enforcement mechanisms.

records.record_text: In humanitarian terms, the situation of the majority of the population in East Timor and of the refugee population in West Timor is extremely grave, with tens of thousands fleeing to cantonment sites perilously close to starvation.
records.political_signal: Imminent mass disaster without urgent aid intervention.
records.policy_implication: Requires immediate air drops and unhindered humanitarian corridors.

records.record_text: There is strong prima facie evidence of abuses of international humanitarian law committed since the announcement of the ballot result on 4 September.
records.political_signal: Systematic international crimes requiring accountability.
records.policy_implication: Establishment of international investigative mechanisms required.

records.record_text: The grave humanitarian crisis in East Timor should be given the topmost priority by the United Nations, in terms both of supply of basic needs to the displaced population, including in West Timor, and of insistence that the Government of Indonesia provide access and security to United Nations and international humanitarian organizations.
records.actor_target: UN Security Council / Government of Indonesia
records.political_signal: Humanitarian relief must take precedence over political delays.
records.policy_implication: Priority resource mobilization and security guarantees.

records.record_text: The Security Council should welcome the decision of the President of Indonesia to invite an international peacekeeping force to cooperate with Indonesia in restoring peace and security in East Timor and should adopt a resolution without delay to provide a framework for the implementation of that proposal.
records.political_signal: Prompt adoption of a Chapter VII mandate authorized.
records.policy_implication: Drafting and adoption of Resolution 1264 (1999).

records.record_text: The Security Council should hold the Government of Indonesia to its obligations under phase II of the 5 May Agreement, with particular insistence on the proper care of IDPs and on curtailing the role of the militias and preventing any clashes between the militias and Falintil.
records.political_signal: Indonesia remains legally responsible for security until transition.
records.policy_implication: Continued pressure on TNI to disarm militias immediately.

records.record_text: The Security Council should institute action for the investigation of apparent abuses of international humanitarian law on the ground in East and West Timor since 4 September.
records.political_signal: Commitment to international accountability for atrocities.
records.policy_implication: Mandating human rights inquiry and evidence gathering.

records.record_text: The events witnessed in East Timor since 4 September 1999 represent nothing less than a systematic implementation of a 'scorched earth' policy in East Timor, under the direction of the Indonesian military.
records.political_signal: Military leadership directly responsible for state-sponsored destruction.
records.policy_implication: Nullifies claims of uncontrolled civil conflict.

records.record_text: Massive forced displacement of the population to refugee camps in West Timor and efforts to permanently disperse these people around Indonesia are under way, accompanied by militia and TNI combing camps to remove and execute students, intellectuals and activists.
records.political_signal: Systematic purge and demographic engineering targeting pro-independence groups.
records.policy_implication: Requires humanitarian access to West Timor refugee camps.

records.record_text: The scale and thoroughness of the destruction of East Timor demonstrated a new level of open participation of the military in the implementation of what was previously a more veiled operation, legitimized by the invocation of martial law.
records.political_signal: Martial law served as cover for military-led destruction.
records.policy_implication: Immediate international military force required to stop TNI-led destruction.

mission_title: Security Council mission to Western Sahara

main_risks: Risk that the referendum target date of January 1996 will not be met due to persistent identification delays.
Risk of return to armed hostilities in Western Sahara if MINURSO is prematurely withdrawn.
Politicization of technical identification issues arising from mutual suspicion and lack of trust between the parties.
Logistical and operational deficiencies facing MINURSO military and civilian operations due to administrative and financial constraints.
main_commitments: The Government of Mauritania agreed to enable MINURSO to proceed with the identification of applicants living in Mauritania.
The Government of Morocco agreed to consider increasing its financial contribution to MINURSO upon receipt of a formal request.
Morocco reaffirmed its commitment to cooperate on troop reductions, political detainee releases, and refugee repatriation once key milestones are set.
main_policy_signals: There is no viable alternative to the settlement plan, and both parties must stay committed to it.
Premature withdrawal of MINURSO would be dangerous and catastrophic for regional stability.
The parties must abandon insistence on strict reciprocity regarding identification centres and cease blaming each other for delays.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Western Sahara (3–9 June 1995) assessed the implementation of the settlement plan, focusing on the identification of potential voters for the referendum. The mission found deep mutual suspicion between Morocco and Frente POLISARIO, resulting in frequent interruptions and politicization of technical procedures. Consequently, the mission concluded that the target of holding the referendum by January 1996 is at serious risk. To overcome these bottlenecks, the mission recommended expanding identification capacity in fixed centres, expediting legal reviews, commencing identification in Mauritania, and requiring Morocco to pre-vet 100,000 non-resident applicants. The mission emphasized that MINURSO's presence remains crucial for maintaining the cease-fire and preventing a return to hostilities.

activities.activity_description: Pre-departure meetings in New York with Permanent Representatives of Morocco, Algeria, and Mauritania, and the representative of Frente POLISARIO to elicit views on terms of reference.
Briefing session in Rabat with the Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General (DSRSG), Mr. Erik Jensen.
Meeting in Rabat with Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Morocco, Mr. Abdellatif Filali, and Foreign Ministry officials.
Meeting in Rabat with Minister of State for the Interior of Morocco, Mr. Driss Basri, and Ministry officials.
Meeting in Algiers with Minister for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Algeria, Mr. Mohammed Salah Dembri, and working session with senior Foreign Ministry officials.
Meetings in Tindouf with the leadership of Frente POLISARIO, including Secretary-General Mohamed Abdelaziz and Deputy SG Bachir Mustapha Sayed.
Meeting in Smara refugee camp with local sheikhs (Chioufs).
Observation of voter identification operations at the Smara and Ayoune identification centres in the Tindouf region.
Meeting in Laayoune at Palais des Congrès with local Moroccan government officials, sheikhs, and Sahrawi representatives.
Briefings in Laayoune by MINURSO Force Commander Brigadier-General Andre Van Baelen and Civilian Police Commissioner Colonel Wolf-Dieter Krampe.
Meetings in Tindouf and Laayoune with Organization of African Unity (OAU) observers.
Inspection of MINURSO identification facilities and observation of the identification process in Laayoune.
Audience in Nouakchott with President Maaoya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya and Prime Minister Mohamed Ould Boubakar of Mauritania.
Press conference held by the Chairman of the mission at Casablanca airport prior to departure.

actors_met.actor_name: Government of Morocco (Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, Minister of State Driss Basri, and senior officials)
Frente POLISARIO (Secretary-General Mohamed Abdelaziz, Deputy SG Bachir Mustapha Sayed, and senior leadership)
Government of Algeria (Minister for Foreign Affairs Mohammed Salah Dembri and Foreign Ministry officials)
Government of Mauritania (President Maaoya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya, Prime Minister Mohamed Ould Boubakar, and Minister for Foreign Affairs Mohamed Salem Ould Lekhal)
MINURSO (Deputy Special Representative Erik Jensen, Force Commander Brig. Gen. Andre Van Baelen, Police Commissioner Col. Wolf-Dieter Krampe, and staff)
Organization of African Unity (OAU) Observer Delegation
Saharan Sheikhs and Community Representatives (Tindouf Smara refugee camp and Laayoune)

records.record_text: In its discussions with the two parties the mission observed that there was continuing suspicion and lack of trust. As a result, in the course of identification, technical problems that could have been resolved easily had there been goodwill, had become politicized and blown out of proportion, with each party blaming the other for the lack of progress.
records.political_signal: Mutual distrust between the parties is politicizing technical tasks and stalling the peace process.
records.policy_implication: UN intervention must address political confidence-building, not merely technical administrative support.

records.record_text: Given the complexity of the tasks to be performed, the continuing delays caused by the two parties and the constraints imposed by limited resources and local conditions, the mission is concerned that the time necessary to perform the functions associated with the identification process and other aspects of the settlement plan has been underestimated. The mission therefore feels that there is a real risk that the identification process may be extended beyond the time previously envisaged and the referendum may not be held in January 1996.
records.political_signal: The target deadline of January 1996 for holding the referendum is unlikely to be met unless significant adjustments occur.
records.policy_implication: The Security Council may need to adjust the settlement plan timetable or exert greater leverage on the parties.

records.record_text: The mission strongly recommends that both parties abandon their insistence on reciprocity in the number and operation of identification centres on each side and refrain from their habit of blaming their lack of cooperation on the other side.
records.political_signal: Strict operational parallelism between sides is counterproductive and must be discarded.
records.policy_implication: Identification operations should proceed independently at maximum speed on each side regardless of the other side's pace.

records.record_text: The mission calls upon the Government of Morocco to conduct preliminary vetting of the 100,000 applicants currently not residing in the Territory prior to examination by the Identification Commission, in order to enable MINURSO to maintain its timetable for completing the identification process.
records.political_signal: Morocco must take responsibility for pre-screening external applicant files to prevent overwhelming the UN process.
records.policy_implication: Reduces administrative backlog for MINURSO Identification Commission.

records.record_text: MINURSO should without delay commence the identification operation for applicants living in Mauritania, in cooperation with the Government of Mauritania, with a view to completing that operation as soon as possible.
records.political_signal: Identification in neutral neighboring territories must proceed immediately.
records.policy_implication: Expands identification footprint into Mauritania.

records.record_text: The mission calls attention to the fact that one of MINURSO’s main successes has been the establishment and maintenance of the cease-fire. It was very clearly communicated to the mission that in the event of MINURSO’s withdrawal before completing its mandate, the risk of a return to some form of hostilities would increase.
records.political_signal: Terminating or prematurely pulling out MINURSO risks immediate re-ignition of war.
records.policy_implication: The Council must maintain MINURSO despite implementation delays to preserve peace.

records.record_text: Mr. Filali stressed that MINURSO needed four essential conditions to be met for the implementation of the settlement plan: (a) permanent support by the Security Council; (b) full cooperation by the two parties; (c) assurances of cooperation and support by the neighbouring countries; and (d) availability of the necessary financial resources.
records.political_signal: Morocco outlines core prerequisites for UN plan success.
records.policy_implication: UN must ensure adequate resourcing and political backing.

records.record_text: With respect to such numbers [100,000 non-resident applicants], Mr. Basri put forward his Government’s offer to provide the logistical and technical support for the identification of those applicants either by transferring them to the Territory or by transporting the Identification Commission to them with the aim of identifying 30,000 to 50,000 persons per month.
records.political_signal: Morocco offers resources to rapidly process large numbers of applicants.
records.policy_implication: Requires MINURSO verification to ensure processing integrity is not compromised.

records.record_text: Mr. Sayed stressed that, in the Frente POLISARIO’S view, the list of voters should be based on the 1974 census, with a small margin of increase to allow for population growth. He informed the mission that the Frente POLISARIO had expressed serious reservations about the implementation of criteria 4 and 5 and about the admission of oral testimony by the sheikhs...
records.political_signal: POLISARIO rejects expansion of voter lists beyond 1974 census norms.
records.policy_implication: Core political blockage on eligibility criteria remains unresolved.

records.record_text: At the same time, the mission observed the POLISARIO leadership’s increasing doubts about MINURSO’s ability to ensure fairness in the process, doubts that some observers believe could place the settlement plan at risk. The mission argued, in the strongest terms possible, that the interests of the POLISARIO were best protected by staying with the plan...
records.political_signal: The UN warning to POLISARIO that walking away from the settlement plan is unacceptable.
records.policy_implication: UN must ensure transparency to maintain POLISARIO's participation.

records.record_text: On the matter of the confinement of the POLISARIO troops, the Government of Algeria strongly rejected the proposal made in 1991 by the then Special Representative of the Secretary-General that they be confined in Algeria. In the Government’s view, this would extend the theatre of conflict to Algerian territory.
records.political_signal: Algeria refuses to host POLISARIO troop cantonment on its soil.
records.policy_implication: POLISARIO troop confinement must take place inside Western Sahara territory.

records.record_text: The Force Commander highlighted the difficulties faced by MINURSO’s military component in its operational capabilities as a result of administrative problems and financial limitations placed on the mission. Those problems and limitations had caused critical logistical deficiencies.
records.political_signal: Administrative budget constraints are directly eroding MINURSO operational capability.
records.policy_implication: UN Headquarters and Security Council must resolve funding and administrative bottlenecks.

records.record_text: The Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, in consultation with the two parties and the observer countries, should seek ways to secure a date in the near future for the reduction and confinement of troops in order to allow the Secretary-General to make his ruling in the matter in early September.
records.actor_target: UN Secretariat / Special Envoy (DSRSG Erik Jensen)
records.political_signal: Military aspects of the plan must be scheduled and delinked from identification delays.
records.policy_implication: Prepares timelines for troop reduction decisions by September.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Deputy Special Representative should also consult with the two parties on the exchange of prisoners of war and the release of political detainees, so that those issues could be removed from the timetable and linked closely to the commencement of the transitional period.
records.actor_target: UN Secretariat / Special Envoy (DSRSG Erik Jensen)
records.political_signal: Humanitarian measures like POW exchanges should be decoupled from technical identification hurdles.
records.policy_implication: Builds confidence between parties ahead of the formal transitional period.

mission_title: REPORT OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL MISSION TO RWANDA ON 12 AND 13 FEBRUARY 1995

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Political, Reconstruction, and Refugee Repatriation Engagement
main_risks: Pervasive fear preventing the voluntary return of internally displaced persons and refugees
Insecurity and intimidation in refugee camps created by armed elements, particularly in Zaire
Presence of 2 million external refugees sustaining inherent regional and domestic instability
Absence of an effective judiciary, trained police force, and civil administration impeding reconciliation and justice
main_commitments: Government of Rwanda reaffirmed full commitment to the Arusha Peace Agreement
Government of Rwanda reaffirmed readiness to cooperate with the International Tribunal for Rwanda
Implementation of UNHCR arrangements with Zaire and Tanzania to enhance refugee camp security
Deployment of expanded UNAMIR civilian police observers (from 90 to 120) to train an integrated national police force
main_policy_signals: Primary responsibility for national reconciliation, order, and healing rests with the Rwandese themselves and cannot be imposed
Accelerated repatriation of refugees and IDPs is a matter of highest priority for long-term stability
Justice for genocide and serious violations of international humanitarian law must move forward in tandem with reconciliation
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Rwanda on 12 and 13 February 1995 assessed post-genocide normalization, political reconciliation, refugee repatriation, and national reconstruction. While recognizing progress in restoring basic stability and the launching of 'Opération Retour', the mission concluded that deep structural challenges remain. Crucially, pervasive fear, security threats in regional refugee camps, and the lack of a functioning judiciary and national police impede full recovery. The mission emphasized that national healing must be indigenous, backed by international support for justice, mine action, civil administration, and political dialogue.

activities.activity_description: Meeting with United Nations agencies and offices operating in Rwanda
Meeting with representatives of the Steering Group of the NGO community in Rwanda
Briefing by Special Representative of the Secretary-General Shaharyar M. Khan and Deputy Force Commander of UNAMIR Brig. Gen. Henry Anyidoho
Meeting with members of the diplomatic corps accredited to Rwanda
Meeting of Mission Chairman Ibrahim A. Gambari with the Nigerian military contingent serving with UNAMIR
Field visit to Kibeho camp for internally displaced persons and Rukondo in south-western Rwanda
Meeting with Prime Minister Faustin Twagiramungu
Meeting with Vice-President and Minister of Defence Major General Paul Kagame
Meeting with President Pasteur Bizimungu, accompanied by Minister for Foreign Affairs Anastase Gasana and Minister for Rehabilitation and Social Reintegration Jacques Bihozagara
Press conference conducted by the mission members at Kigali airport

actors_met.actor_name: Pasteur Bizimungu, President of Rwanda
Major General Paul Kagame, Vice-President and Minister of Defence
Faustin Twagiramungu, Prime Minister
Anastase Gasana, Minister for Foreign Affairs
Jacques Bihozagara, Minister for Rehabilitation and Social Reintegration
Shaharyar M. Khan, Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Rwanda
Brig. Gen. Henry Anyidoho, Deputy Force Commander, UNAMIR
United Nations Country Team in Rwanda (UNDP, UNHCR, World Bank, UNICEF, UNREO, WFP, UN Human Rights Field Operation, IOM, WHO, FAO, UNFPA, DDSMS)
Diplomatic Corps in Kigali (Ambassadors/Representatives of Canada, China, France, Germany, United States, Burundi, Holy See, Belgium, United Kingdom)
Steering Group of the NGO Community in Rwanda (Africa Humanitarian Action, Save the Children, Médecins Sans Frontières, Équilibre, Forum des ONG rwandaises)
Internally Displaced Persons in Kibeho camp

records.record_text: while significant progress has been made towards restoring normality and stability to Rwanda, more needed to be done.
records.policy_implication: Indicates the need for continued international assistance and governmental action.

records.record_text: the Security Council expects the Government to intensify its efforts to repatriate refugees, to promote national reconciliation and to reinvigorate the political process, including the creation of an appropriate mechanism for sustaining dialogue between the Government, the refugee community and the United Nations.
records.political_signal: The Security Council places clear expectation on the Rwandan Government to take proactive political and humanitarian steps.
records.policy_implication: Failure to create dialogue mechanisms could undermine international support and sustainable return.

records.record_text: While it was generally agreed that the most important goal was to prevent the recurrence of the tragedy that had recently befallen Rwanda, the specific issues of repatriation, reconciliation, reconstruction and the need for justice were seen as interrelated, although differences were evident as to the priorities in addressing those concerns.
records.policy_implication: Highlighting differing national and international priorities regarding sequencing justice versus reconciliation.

records.record_text: The return and resettlement of internally displaced persons and refugees was seen as a prerequisite for long-term stability and progress.
records.policy_implication: Puts refugee and IDP return at the center of peacebuilding policy.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister emphasized that, without reconciliation, peace would not be possible.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces reconciliation as a fundamental pillar of government policy.

records.record_text: Bringing to justice those responsible for genocide and other serious violations of international humanitarian law in Rwanda constituted another priority.
records.policy_implication: Justice is imperative to combat impunity and foster long-term stability.

records.record_text: The mission was informed of progress in facilitating the return and resettlement of internally displaced persons, especially through 'Opération Retour'. This programme, coordinated jointly by UNAMIR and United Nations agencies, in cooperation with the Government and supported also by NGOs, was launched on 29 December 1994.
records.actor_source: UNAMIR / UN Country Team / Government of Rwanda
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates successful joint operational framework between UN and national authorities.

records.record_text: Fear remains the single most important factor impeding the return of internally displaced persons and refugees.
records.policy_implication: Requires confidence-building measures and security guarantees to enable population return.

records.record_text: Government officials informed the mission of progress made in safeguarding the rights of innocent citizens and stressed the urgent need for assistance in order to restore an effective judiciary and a trained police force.
records.policy_implication: Urgent requirement for international resource allocation towards judicial capacity-building and police training.

records.record_text: Government officials explained their concerns with regard to the International Tribunal for Rwanda, but reaffirmed Rwanda’s readiness to cooperate with the Tribunal and expressed the hope that it would begin its work as soon as possible.
records.policy_implication: Ensures governmental political buy-in for the operationalization of the ICTR.

records.record_text: Regarding reconciliation, progress has been marginal so far.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the need for renewed political strategies to overcome social polarization.

records.record_text: While recognizing that national reconciliation was a continuous process, the view was stressed that a number of immediate steps and measures were called for, such as active repatriation, the creation of a political and psychological climate conducive to reconciliation and the restoration of an effective and functioning judiciary.
records.policy_implication: Requires synchronized efforts on repatriation, legal reform, and social outreach.

records.record_text: Concern was expressed, on the other hand, that many of those accused or suspected of carrying out atrocities had so far shown no remorse or contrition, a situation that was seen as discouraging efforts towards reconciliation, by making forgiveness difficult.
records.policy_implication: Lack of accountability or contrition delays psychological healing and reconciliation.

records.record_text: Government officials also emphasized that they respected, and indeed accepted the spirit of an inclusive and broad-based Government, as provided for under the Arusha peace agreement, to which their Government remained fully committed. It was pointed out that the Arusha accords were part of Rwanda’s fundamental or basic law ('loi fondamentale').
records.political_signal: The Government signals its adherence to constitutional continuity based on the Arusha framework.
records.policy_implication: Provides a legitimacy baseline for political governance and UN support.

records.record_text: They further pointed out, however, that returning to the country was the precondition for participating in the political process.
records.political_signal: Political engagement is strictly contingent upon physical return to Rwandan territory.
records.policy_implication: Excludes external political factions unless they repatriate.

records.record_text: Officials also indicated that the Government had recently commenced dialogue with representatives of Rwandese refugee communities in Burundi. They explained that dialogue with the refugee community in Zaire was not yet feasible in view of the insecurity and intimidation to which those refugees were subjected by armed elements in their midst.
records.policy_implication: Armed control over camps in Zaire prevents peaceful negotiation and voluntary return.

records.record_text: The role of civic education and sensitization programmes emphasizing the respect for human rights, the rule of law and tolerance, was underlined. In this connection, Radio UNAMIR will make a positive contribution by providing Rwandese, both inside the country and in refugee camps, with factual and objective information.
records.policy_implication: Radio UNAMIR serves as a key tool against hate speech and misinformation.

records.record_text: Concerning rehabilitation and reconstruction, the mission was informed that the emergency phase was largely over and that emphasis was increasingly being placed on longer-term measures to rebuild the country.
records.actor_source: UN Country Team / Government of Rwanda
records.policy_implication: Shift focus from emergency humanitarian response to developmental assistance.

records.record_text: In this connection, the response of the international community to the January 1995 round-table meeting in Geneva and to the consolidated inter-agency appeal was encouraging.
records.policy_implication: Positive donor commitments need rapid disbursement to impact ground conditions.

records.record_text: The importance of setting up an effective mine-clearance programme in Rwanda was also emphasized.
